Harry Burlguard asks for proof of a novice's backbone before teaching deeper combat skills in the Pig and Whistle Tavern. Across the room, Bartleby nurses his drinks at the far end of the counter. Harry wants you to take the man's mug, knowing Bartleby would rather fight than surrender his ale. The challenge puts a warrior's resolve to the test. Soldiers, laborers, and rough locals fill the Pig and Whistle, where polished manners count for little. Bartleby mocks newcomers as too prissy for a tavern scuffle instead of answering politely. The exchange leads to a brawl on the floorboards, where a warrior's training in Stormwind begins with a test of basic barroom fighting.

quest:1640.text: Beat Bartleby. In Stormwind, Bartleby guards the mug a young warrior must claim. The instructors send recruits to face him in a bare-knuckle fight and earn the vessel for their training. Stormwind's warrior instructors expect recruits to face combat without excuses or grand ceremony. As part of their formal training, young warriors must retrieve a particular mug from Bartleby, a notorious drunkard who lounges in the city. He scoffs at polite requests and swears no one will take his prized drinkware without prying it from his cold, dead fingers. For a fledgling warrior, words soon give way to a fistfight. Bartleby boasts that he will fight to the death, but a thorough thrashing is enough to sober him. Once beaten, his bravado gives way to bruised admiration. He recognizes that his opponent is tougher than they appear and yields peacefully, letting the victor claim the mug and complete the trial at the training hall.

quest:1641.text: The Tome of Divinity. In Stormwind, The Tome of Divinity guides young paladins through a solemn rite. Under Duthorian Rall's care in the Cathedral of Light, you face teachings on virtue, devotion, and the duties that come with the Holy Light. Duthorian Rall guides those who answer the paladin's calling in the Cathedral of Light. Early training teaches martial discipline and the order's rites, but advancement asks for a deeper commitment to the spirit. The trials ask you to look beyond battle and weigh the moral duties of a paladin. Stormwind faces dangers within its borders and beyond, and its people need defenders who understand that duty. Receiving the Book of Divinity binds you to service and self-sacrifice. Duthorian asks you to study the holy text and learn what the Light demands of its defenders. Its lessons prepare paladins to oppose the Scourge's creeping horrors and protect common folk. Righteous power must answer to virtue and compassion.

quest:1645.text: The Tome of Divinity. In Ironforge, Tiza Battleforge places the Tome of Divinity in a dwarven paladin's hands. Its teachings begin trials meant to test devotion to the Light and readiness to defend Azeroth from dark forces such as the Scourge. Promising paladin initiates from across the eastern kingdoms come to Ironforge's Hall of Mysteries after mastering the martial and spiritual basics. Tiza Battleforge guides young dwarven paladins in the principles that set a champion of the Holy Light apart from an ordinary warrior. Taking up this calling means pledging a life to duty, self-sacrifice, and spiritual discipline. The novice receives the Book of Divinity as a guide to its duties, virtues, and spiritual teachings. Its words show how sacred power may be wielded against wicked threats. Study is only the first step; the initiate must carry those lessons into acts of faith across Khaz Modan and beyond.

quest:1665.text: Bartleby's Mug. In Stormwind, Bartleby's Mug marks a young warrior's trial of grit. After besting Bartleby in the Pig and Whistle Tavern, you claim his drinking mug for your trainer, Harry Burlguard. Harry Burlguard tests young warriors with a brawl in Old Town. He asks you to take down Bartleby, a stubborn drunk at the bar of the Pig and Whistle Tavern. Once subdued, Bartleby reluctantly gives up his prized drinking mug, but first takes one final swig to drain the dregs. Returning the mug to Harry Burlguard completes your novice trial. Burlguard sees that you can persuade through sheer force and recognizes your readiness for defensive mastery. He points you onward to further battlefield instruction with Marshal Haggard, a seasoned veteran in Elwynn Forest.

quest:1666.text: Marshal Haggard. At Eastvale, Marshal Haggard keeps the arms he gathered over a lifetime of service. Harry Burlguard sends novice warriors from Stormwind City to meet the retired marshal and seek better weapons. Stormwind's novice warriors need more than skill to face danger beyond the city. Harry Burlguard sends promising fighters east through Elwynn Forest to find Marshal Haggard, a retired officer who served the realm for years. Haggard gathered a personal armory over a lifetime in the field, and his home near the Eastvale Logging Camp holds weapons for young warriors seeking better arms. Marshal Haggard lives in a secluded manor near the Eastvale Logging Camp. Years of service have weakened his failing sight, and he sometimes mistakes approaching travelers for prowling riverpaw gnolls. Though age keeps him in this quiet corner of eastern Elwynn, Stormwind's guards and trainers still respect the old marshal.

quest:1667.text: Dead-tooth Jack. A stolen badge puts Marshal Haggard's authority in Defias hands. The retired officer lives in eastern Elwynn Forest, where Dead-tooth Jack tricked him into surrendering his official insignia. Jack wore a Stormwind tabard in the dark and posed as Marshal Dughan. Haggard needs the badge back before the Defias Brotherhood can use it to impersonate Stormwind officials. Marshal Haggard lives in an isolated cottage on Elwynn's eastern ridges. One night, a figure in a Stormwind tabard approached, claiming official business and asking for Haggard's old marshal's badge. Believing he was handing it to a fellow officer, Haggard complied. The stranger laughed in his face and vanished into the woods. The thief was a Defias rogue called Dead-tooth Jack. Marshal Haggard has retired, but his old badge still carries the legal weight of Stormwind. Defias bandits are creeping across Elwynn, Westfall, and Redridge, and the badge could help them pass guard checkpoints, redirect patrols, or take command of supplies. Jack retreated to a camp to the south and left the badge locked in a strongbox. Haggard needs it recovered before the Defias can cause serious harm.

quest:1679.text: Muren Stormpike. In Ironforge, Muren Stormpike awaits warriors sent from Kharanos for formal training. Granis Swiftaxe sends recruits who have proved their mettle in Dun Morogh to the city's Military Ward. Granis Swiftaxe sends promising warriors from Kharanos to Ironforge after they face local threats in Dun Morogh. He knows rough skirmishes can teach only so much. In the Military Ward, senior fighters oversee formal training for those bound for battle. At the Hall of Arms, you meet Muren Stormpike, a veteran of a storied dwarven clan. He wants proof that his new charges can endure real combat, not tavern tales. Reporting to him opens the way to learn defensive arts, control an enemy's aggression, and earn iron arms for the front line.

quest:168.text: Collecting Memories. In Stormwind City, Wilder Thistlenettle asks you to remember the miners lost beneath Moonbrook. He wants their Miners' Union Cards returned to their grieving families. Before lawlessness and the Defias Brotherhood took hold in Moonbrook, Westfall's mines supported many working-class families. Wilder Thistlenettle survived a cave-in that buried one wing of the tunnels. Many of his friends and fellow miners died underground, beyond the reach of rescue. Their families in Stormwind never learned for certain what had become of them. The miners who died in the collapse now wander the tunnels outside the main iron works as undead. You search those haunted passages for the Miners' Union Cards, facing the remains of the men Wilder worked beside. Bringing the cards back to Stormwind will tell their families what happened and let Wilder honor his fallen companions.

quest:1681.text: Ironband's Compound. At Ironband's Compound, Tormus Deepforge seeks vengeance for his slain mentor. Sturgy Ironband's teaching outpost in eastern Dun Morogh fell after a shipment of rare umbral ore drew the Dark Iron dwarves. Sturgy Ironband taught smithing at a secluded compound south of Helm's Bed Lake. Across Ironforge, he was revered as an unmatched instructor. He trained promising pupils far from the crowded anvils of the Great Forge. That peaceful work ended when one student acquired an unfamiliar mineral called umbral ore. Intrigued by its properties, Ironband chose to experiment with the sample. He did not know that possessing the ore had marked his school for ruin. Dark Iron dwarves attacked the compound soon after the umbral ore arrived. The assault was sudden and ruthless. They killed Sturgy Ironband and every apprentice in his care, then took over the grounds. Tormus Deepforge, one of Ironband's surviving protégés in the capital, refuses to let the massacre go unanswered. He sends Alliance travelers to avenge his teacher and recover the ore that brought destruction to the outpost.

quest:1683.text: Vorlus Vilehoof. In Darnassus, young night elf warriors face a trial set by Elanaria. They must hunt a satyr who has defiled a hidden moonwell near the Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Elanaria asks you to prove your dedication and discipline before she teaches advanced martial techniques. She needs more than words from those who defend Kalimdor. A guardian must face corruption and cleanse the sacred boughs of Teldrassil. Your trial leads to Vorlus Vilehoof, a satyr hiding at a moonwell in the mountains southeast of Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Satyrs were once ancient betrayers, twisted by demonic influence, and they hate sacred Kaldorei relics. Vorlus bathes in the moonwell, fouling its blessed waters and mocking the grace of Elune.

quest:1685.text: Gakin's Summons. A summons delivered to promising Alliance warlocks by Remen Marcot on behalf of Gakin the Darkbinder. It directs fledgling practitioners down into the crypts beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind's Mage Quarter to begin their next stage of dark occult training. Demonology is strictly outlawed across the civilized districts of Stormwind, yet dark arts persist right under the noses of the city guard. When a warlock displays sufficient proficiency with their introductory imps, word quietly travels to senior practitioners. Remen Marcot delivers the message with deliberate discretion, urging initiates to keep the meeting place quiet and head into the shadowy recesses beneath the Mage Quarter. Behind the modest facade of the Slaughtered Lamb tavern lies a network of damp cellars and hidden catacombs. Here, shielded from prying Kirin Tor mages and the Cathedral's inquisitors, Gakin the Darkbinder oversees the instruction of Stormwind's warlocks. The summons serves as the gateway to commanding a voidwalker, a rite requiring dangerous stolen reagents and perilous summoning circles.

quest:1686.text: The Shade of Elura. At Auberdine, Elura's shade guards a sunken ship and its Elunite ore. Elanaria sends young night elf warriors into the waters to lay the captain to rest and recover her medallion and ore for a weapon forged by Smith Mathiel. Long ago, a ship carrying rare Elunite ore struck jagged coastal rocks near the Auberdine lighthouse and sank. The captain, Elura, cursed her own soul in despair and out of unwavering duty. Bound to the wreck beneath the waves, her shade guards the lost cargo from anyone who would disturb it. Elanaria sends young night elf warriors into Darkshore's surf to defeat Elura, recover her medallion, and salvage the ore. They need both the medallion and ore to put the captain to rest and bring the metal to Smith Mathiel's forge. The work tests their martial skill and respect for the fallen, and provides the ore for a crafted weapon.

quest:1688.text: Surena Caledon. Beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind, Gakin seeks his former pupil and a bloodstone choker. He sends an aspiring warlock after Surena Caledon, who betrayed him to join the Defias Brotherhood. Beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind's Mage Quarter, Gakin the Darkbinder teaches novices the forbidden arts of fel summoning. He once took a young woman named Surena Caledon as his pupil. He admired her natural magical talent and her beauty. Surena left her studies and Gakin's favor, then fled Stormwind with her lover, Erlan Drudgemoor, to join the Defias Brotherhood.

quest:1689.text: The Binding. In Stormwind, Gakin the Darkbinder puts a novice warlock through a final trial. With his recovered Bloodstone Choker, you draw a voidwalker into a hidden circle and force it to submit. Beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind's Mage Quarter, forgotten catacombs run beyond the watchful gaze of the Silver Hand and Kirin Tor magistrates. Gakin the Darkbinder teaches novice warlocks that dark magic demands more than channeling power; they must also dominate otherworldly beings. You have recovered Gakin's stolen Bloodstone Choker from Surena Caledon. Now he asks you to call a voidwalker into the summoning circle beneath the tavern. A voidwalker will not bargain with you. The power in the Bloodstone Choker opens a rift and draws the shadow creature into the mortal world. You must batter it with magic and force until its will breaks, proving you can command it. Once defeated, the voidwalker's essence binds to you, giving you a durable, shadowy protector that can endure punishment in the battles ahead.

quest:1692.text: Smith Mathiel. In Darnassus, sacred ore is on its way to the forge. After you recover elunite from the shipwreck off Auberdine, Elanaria sends you to Mathiel to have it shaped into a weapon for the Kaldorei. Elanaria sends you across Darnassus's Warrior's Terrace with the elunite ore you recovered from the haunted shipwreck off Auberdine. The warrior trainer packs it in a sturdy case and directs you to Mathiel, one of the capital's finest smiths. He can shape the metal into a weapon worthy of your calling. Mathiel treats smithing as a craft of devotion. Elunite bears the sacred blessing of Elune, the Moon Goddess, and he accepts the case as an honor. He will shape the holy metal into arms to defend the young boughs of Teldrassil.

quest:1693.text: Weapons of Elunite. In Darnassus, Weapons of Elunite brings a young warrior's early rite of passage to its close. After recovering ore blessed by Elune, you bring it to Mathiel to forge arms for a defender of Kalimdor. Night elf warriors defend Teldrassil and the kaldorei people. Promising young warriors gather elunite, a mineral blessed by the Moon Goddess, rather than relying on mundane steel alone. Its ore calls for a smith skilled in metalcraft and mindful of Elune's gift. Smith Mathiel works in Darnassus, shaping blessed elunite into weapons of war. He considers the work an honor, not routine metalcraft. When you bring him the ore, he fashions arms to suit your style and rewards your service with weapons blessed by your goddess.

quest:170.text: A New Threat. Balir Frosthammer calls for help as troggs surge through Coldridge Valley. Rockjaw troggs are breaking through across Dun Morogh, catching dwarven mountaineers off guard and threatening the settlements and camps. In Coldridge Valley, Rockjaw troggs are clawing up from below in growing numbers. Anvilmar hears reports of them swarming the frozen lake and nearby foothills. Their attacks disrupt patrols and cut off supply routes through the valley pass, turning a training refuge for young dwarven warriors and mountaineers into a place under threat. A dwarven camp west of the valley has fallen to a coordinated trogg attack. The mountaineers retreated and abandoned their posts. Ironforge cannot spare full battle regiments, so Balir Frosthammer calls on newly recruited adventurers to fight through the Rockjaw ranks and secure the hills before the creatures reach Anvilmar.

quest:1715.text: The Slaughtered Lamb. In Stormwind, The Slaughtered Lamb gives gnome warlocks a place to seek training. With King Magni Bronzebeard watching dark practitioners in Ironforge, mentors send their students to human warlocks for instruction. Before Gnomeregan fell, aspiring warlocks in Khaz Modan studied with tinker-mages and demonic scholars inside the techno-city. The disaster scattered those institutions and drove the gnomes into exile. Surviving practitioners crowded into Ironforge's underground caverns, watched by King Magni Bronzebeard and the dwarven guard. They cannot openly practice demonic arts or perform dangerous rituals there, so senior instructors such as Lago Blackwrench send students away. Gnome students sent south from Ironforge seek instruction at the Slaughtered Lamb, a tavern in Stormwind's Mage Quarter. Twisting stone passages and stairs lead from its taproom to a hidden sanctum where human warlocks gather. Gakin the Darkbinder oversees the covert gathering. Its space and dark paraphernalia let instructors teach novices to summon and bind minor demons without drawing the immediate anger of the city marshals. Stormwind's coven welcomes capable hands, but the arrival of refugee novices brings friction. Human mentors already risk discovery by the city's paladins and authorities. Gakin and his colleagues find their hidden sanctuary more crowded as practitioners arrive from Khaz Modan. The steady stream from the dwarven mountain could expose their discreet operation, yet neither the gnomes nor the human warlocks have an easier choice.

quest:176.text: Wanted: "Hogger". Wanted: "Hogger" is an Alliance bounty posted outside Goldshire for the head of a massive, savage gnoll chieftain. Hogger prowls the southwestern woods of Elwynn Forest and has violently thwarted every attempt by the local authorities to bring him down. While Elwynn Forest struggles with banditry and kobold infestations, the gnoll tribes in the south have grown bolder and more organized under the brute leadership of Hogger. Towering over typical Riverpaw gnolls, Hogger has established camp near the Forest's Edge, ambushing travelers and overpowering the local militia patrols sent to subdue him. With the Stormwind Army stretched thin and unable to spare regular forces to police the outskirts of the capital, Marshal Dughan took the unusual step of posting an open bounty on the beast. Taking down Hogger requires venture into deeply hostile gnoll territory, and his ferocity has earned him a reputation as the deadliest threat facing novice adventurers in Elwynn.

quest:179.text: Dwarven Outfitters. Sten Stoutarm gives new recruits a bargain in Coldridge Valley. Hunt wolves and bring back their tough meat for winter rations, and he provides sturdy gloves against Dun Morogh's cold. Cold waits on every path through Coldridge Valley. Outside Anvilmar, Sten Stoutarm asks new recruits to hunt the wolves prowling the snowy drifts and bring back their tough meat for the outpost. In return, he provides gloves to protect their hands from the cold. Wolves threaten dwarven scouts and young gnomes training in the valley, yet they also feed the garrison at Anvilmar. Culling them makes the paths between local encampments somewhat safer. Stoutarm's bargain tests a recruit's ability to handle local wildlife while adding food for the bitter nights ahead.

quest:18.text: Brotherhood of Thieves. Deputy Willem sends recruits across Northshire's eastern river to face the Defias Brotherhood. Their red burlap bandanas give Stormwind its first tangible evidence of the brigands' organized presence in the valley. Northshire Valley has long been a safe haven in Elwynn Forest, guarded by Stormwind and used to train recruits and Clerics of the Holy Light. Recently, discipline along its perimeter has frayed. Vagrants and thieves have crossed the eastern river, lurking near the woods and making small camps close to the abbey. Deputy Willem maintains local order, but the guards cannot spare the manpower to watch every corner of the valley without volunteers. These outlaws are coordinated and wear matching attire. They call themselves the Defias Brotherhood, and their red burlap bandanas mark their allegiance. Deputy Willem sends recruits to drive back the brigands and recover their masks, hoping to curb their advance and learn how deeply the Defias have reached into the kingdom's heartland.

quest:1818.text: Speak with Dillinger. In Brill, Austil de Mon sends fighters to Deathguard Dillinger for a hazardous mission in service of Lady Sylvanas. The order begins at the Gallows' End Tavern, where the warrior trainer directs able-bodied recruits to the west end of the village. At the Gallows' End Tavern in Brill, warrior trainer Austil de Mon seeks fighters willing to serve the Dark Lady. When the Deathguards need capable hands, he sends untested recruits into the field. Deathguard Dillinger oversees security on Brill's western edge and has requested someone with martial skill for an urgent task. The Forsaken must constantly prove their martial dominance on Tirisfal Glades' front line. Near Brill's graveyard, Dillinger manages local incursions. Reporting to him tests your combat skill and loyalty to the newly forged Forsaken nation.

quest:1819.text: Ulag the Cleaver. In Tirisfal, a captive Scourge warrior tests the resolve of young Forsaken. Deathguard Dillinger sends you to release Ulag the Cleaver beneath a mausoleum north of Brill and face him in combat. After the Scourge swept across Lordaeron, the Forsaken captured an unusual undead warrior who called himself Ulag the Cleaver. His mind remained clear, yet the Lich King still held his spirit in psychic thrall. The Forsaken bound him beneath a mausoleum north of Brill with a magical seal. They hoped to learn how the Scourge chained a mind and to break the hold over him. The Forsaken failed to free Ulag from the Lich King's command. Deathguard Dillinger now uses the captive as a test of combat for rising Forsaken warriors. Disturbing the skull stone outside the crypt breaks the wards and frees Ulag from his prison. A warrior must face him with an axe, granting him release through death.

quest:182.text: The Troll Cave. In Coldridge Valley, young Frostmane trolls gather in caves along the southern ridge. Grelin Whitebeard sends willing recruits to thin their numbers while Ironforge faces a trogg invasion. Grelin Whitebeard watches the frozen valley from a bluff as Ironforge's soldiers fight troggs across the snowfields. The southern approaches still need watching. Grelin and his brother Senir came at the mountain authorities' command to learn whether the native ice trolls threatened the heartland. Grelin keeps watch alone and tracks their movements. Grelin found that the local Frostmane clan had begun settling in a deep cave along Coldridge Valley's southern ridge. He believes a full military mobilization would waste dwarven manpower, so he hires capable local volunteers to cull the aggressive whelps. Thinning their young fighters could disrupt the camp before the Frostmane launch coordinated raids against nearby dwarven homesteads.

quest:1820.text: Speak with Coleman. In Brill, Deathguard Dillinger sends proven fighters to Coleman Farthing for help. The tavern meeting opens the way to a private matter tied to the old Agamand lands. After you help contain grave threats near Brill, including Ulag the Cleaver, Deathguard Dillinger trusts your strength. He watches the roads into town and decides which fighters can take on work beyond the usual patrols. When he sees you are ready, he points you toward people who need specialized help. Not every fight in Tirisfal Glades comes from orders in the Undercity. The surviving undead of Lordaeron carry grudges over the lands, families, and fortunes they left behind. Coleman Farthing waits in the Gallow's End Tavern, hoping to find a fighter who can strike at threats near former settlements such as the Agamand Mills.

quest:1821.text: Agamand Heirlooms. At Agamand Mills, Coleman Farthing seeks the family's heirlooms from their crypt. He blames the Agamands for his death and wants their ancestral weapons taken from them. Coleman Farthing served the wealthy Agamand family at their mills in Tirisfal Glades before the Third War devastated Lordaeron. Whatever happened as the estate fell, Farthing blames his former lords for his death. Raised into undeath among the Forsaken, he takes spiteful satisfaction in the Agamands' downfall. The once-proud family has become mindless minions enslaved to the Lich King. Farthing sends you into the Agamand Family Crypt beneath the northern bluffs of the mills. Restless dead and lingering Scourge wander its stone halls. He wants you to take four relics: the Agamand family sword, axe, dagger, and mace. Their loss would strip the bloodline of its remaining honor.

quest:183.text: The Boar Hunter. Talin Keeneye asks for help in Coldridge Valley, where crag boars threaten the trails. The dwarf hunter wants young recruits to thin their numbers so seasoned hunters can track in peace. Coldridge Valley gives young mountaineers and scholars of Ironforge a quiet, protected place to train. In the harsh winter, its wildlife can grow restless and numerous. Talin Keeneye, a veteran hunter stationed outside Anvilmar, has seen small crag boars multiply across the valley. Their attacks threaten anyone walking the snowy trails. Hunting gives dwarves meat, hide, and practice in the field. When game grows numerous and attacks on sight, its numbers must be cut. By thinning the crag boars across the valley slopes, young adventurers show they can handle a fight. Their work also gives local hunters room to pursue game without being overwhelmed.

quest:184.text: Furlbrow's Deed. The Furlbrows flee their farm as Defias bandits carry their land grant through Elwynn Forest. Returning the deed to Farmer Furlbrow near the Westfall border preserves the couple’s claim to their stolen homestead. Defias bandits in Elwynn carry a land deed signed by Theodore and Verna Furlbrow. A crude note on its back says they drove the elderly farmer from his property, then carried the document across the river into Elwynn to copy it and forge claims to other seized land. The note says the Furlbrows were stranded just over the border, beside the road, after their wagon broke. The Defias have driven dozens of families from their ancestral land in Westfall. With Stormwind’s army absent and the realm’s resources strained, the Brotherhood uses force and false claims to seize the kingdom’s breadbasket. Theodore and Verna are leaving their farm for safety, but their lawful deed preserves their claim if order ever returns to the province.

quest:1858.text: The Shattered Hand. In Orgrimmar, Therzok tests rogues seeking a place in the Shattered Hand. He asks them to open Tazan's recovered satchel with a key taken from an unwitting accomplice. After retrieving Tazan's locked satchel, you find it useless without the key. The Shattered Hand demands skill, not brute force against the complex lock. Therzok sends you to Gamon, a tauren drunkard who frequents Orgrimmar's tavern. Gamon is easily distracted and once helped Tazan, making him a fitting mark for quiet theft. Take the key from Gamon without alerting the tavern, then open the satchel and claim Tazan's logbook. Bring the stolen contents to Therzok in the Cleft of Shadow to meet the Shattered Hand's standards. A clean job earns you formal recognition as one of its operatives.

quest:1859.text: Therzok. In Orgrimmar, Therzok waits for a promising rogue from Durotar. Kaplak has seen your skill with violence and stealth and sends you to the Cleft of Shadow to meet a Shattered Hand operative. Kaplak draws promising young rogues aside when they begin making a name for themselves in Durotar. The new Horde honors Thrall, but not all its servants fight openly beneath his banner. Word of a fighter skilled in violence and stealth, willing to bend the rules of open warfare, reaches the underground guild in Orgrimmar. Kaplak sends you beneath Orgrimmar's red stone cliffs to the Cleft of Shadow. Therzok waits in its gloom, out of sight of the city's grunts. There, lone cutpurses and ambushers are brought into the Shattered Hand, the Horde's covert network of daggers in the dark.

quest:1860.text: Speak with Jennea. In Goldshire, Zaldimar Wefhellt sends novice mages to Stormwind for further instruction. He directs apprentices who have advanced beyond basic training in Elwynn Forest to Jennea Cannon in the Wizard's Sanctum. Zaldimar Wefhellt sends you from Goldshire to Stormwind City as your training advances. Your time learning elementary spells from local tutors in Elwynn's hamlets has run its course. In the Mage Quarter, the Wizard's Sanctum is where the kingdom's senior mages pursue arcane study and instruction. They coordinate magical matters across the realm. Zaldimar says your report concerns the security of Elwynn Forest and Stormwind, not only your studies. In Stormwind, you report to Jennea Cannon, a mage who oversees local assignments. She is cautious about sharing grand secrets with a newly arrived apprentice, but your report begins your service to the wizarding order.

quest:1861.text: Mirror Lake. Novice Alliance mages in Stormwind's Mage Quarter are sent to sample Mirror Lake's waters for magical contamination. Jennea Cannon sends them southwest of the city gates to test the waterfall spray. Azeroth's arcane currents were shaken by conflicts from the opening of the Dark Portal through the Third War and the battle at Mount Hyjal. Those shocks tore ancient currents from their stable channels. In Stormwind's Wizard's Sanctum, magi like Jennea Cannon watch the changes closely. They fear that displaced arcane power could reach the wilderness and corrupt local ecosystems. Mirror Lake lies beneath the cliffs southwest of the Stormwind gates and is a primary natural reservoir fed by mountain falls. The surrounding countryside depends on its waters. Jennea sends novice mages with a glass flask to the waterfall's base, where they collect fresh spray. The Sanctum can then use scrying and reagent tests to learn whether wild magic is seeping into the public water supply.

quest:1879.text: Speak with Bink. In Dun Morogh, Magis Sparkmantle sends novice mages to Ironforge at Bink's request. Bink needs an arcane specialist for her studies in the Hall of Mysteries. Magis Sparkmantle sends word from his colleague Bink to mages training near Kharanos. She asks for an arcane specialist and will trust the matter only to someone who can wield magic. When an apprentice has outgrown the early exercises, Sparkmantle directs them to answer her call. You travel to Ironforge's Mystic Ward, where scholars, priests, and arcanists gather in the Hall of Mysteries. Bink studies there and watches each arriving apprentice closely. Raw potential is only a beginning; without discipline, a spellcaster can become a danger in arcane work.

quest:1881.text: Speak with Anastasia. In the Undercity, Cain Firesong sends a promising Forsaken mage to Anastasia Hartwell. Her summons calls you to the Magic Quarter for work among the Forsaken magi, with investigations in Tirisfal Glades ahead. Cain Firesong trains young Forsaken mages in Brill, then sends those with promise to the Undercity. In its Magic Quarter, the Forsaken magi pursue arcane study and plan defenses across Lordaeron. Cain judges which students are ready to serve more experienced practitioners. Those who show real talent are sent to Anastasia Hartwell, who needs capable hands in the field. Anastasia Hartwell is one of the Undercity's prominent mage instructors. She puts promising students to work for the Forsaken's practical and territorial interests instead of leaving them to study incantations in safety. Answering her call marks a step into service for the Forsaken's mages and their pragmatic magical work in the years after the Scourge.

quest:1882.text: The Balnir Farmstead. In eastern Tirisfal, snapdragons at the Balnir Farmstead may show how far the Scourge's corruption has spread. Anastasia Hartwell sends young Forsaken mages to gather them for study in the Undercity. Forsaken mages watch the borderlands for signs of magical corruption. Anastasia Hartwell sends novice spellcasters to the Balnir Farmstead in eastern Tirisfal Glades to gather snapdragons from its gardens. The flowers absorb magical energies from the soil and air. By examining them, arcane scholars in the Undercity can judge whether corruption from the Lich King's domain has reached Tirisfal. The Balnir Farmstead lies near the edge of the glades, close to the blighted wilderness of the Western Plaguelands. The Forsaken know the Lich King's plague rots the land, while Scourge corruption threatens their borders and security. The Forsaken wield dark arts of their own, but Anastasia plans to pass the snapdragons to the apothecaries for study. Mages and alchemists can examine the danger together and help defend Lordaeron's reclaimed heartland.

quest:1885.text: Mennet Carkad. In the Undercity, Marion Call sends you to report to Mennet Carkad. He waits deep in the Rogues' Quarter, where promising operatives are tested for the Deathstalkers. Marion Call has a summons for you from Mennet Carkad. In the Undercity, covert operatives draw the notice of higher leadership, and Marion passes along word when a scout or assassin is invited to report. The Forsaken's intelligence apparatus has a lethal reputation, so ignoring its orders is no real choice. Mennet Carkad waits in the Rogues' Quarter, watching recruits and judging whether they are ready. Those who answer his call are tested for entry into the Deathstalkers, the Forsaken's feared arm of espionage and assassination. Obedience is the first test for anyone who seeks to serve the Dark Lady from the shadows.

quest:1886.text: The Deathstalkers. In the Undercity, Mennet Carkad tests hopeful Deathstalkers with a demand for ruthless initiative: intercept a traveling messenger. The trial opens the way into the covert order serving Lord Varimathras. The Deathstalkers serve Varimathras as the Forsaken's secret police and elite assassination corps. In the Rogues' Quarter, handler Mennet Carkad sets a trial for anyone seeking a place among them. A hopeful agent must show cunning, discretion, and the will to eliminate a target. Carkad's test is meant to turn away the weak and those troubled by too many scruples.

quest:1898.text: The Deathstalkers. In the Undercity, the Deathstalkers move against suspected treason in the Forsaken's own ranks. Under Lord Varimathras's orders, you pose as an expected messenger and question a merchant who may be aiding an outside faction. Deathstalker Mennet Carkad sets an infiltration in motion at Lord Varimathras's urging. The Deathstalkers watch the Forsaken's own citizens as closely as they guard against outside threats. With Astor Hadren's letter of introduction, forged or acquired, you approach the local merchant Andron Gant and try to pass as the courier he expects.

quest:1899.text: The Deathstalkers. In the Undercity, the Deathstalkers turn Andron Gant's trust against him. Still believing you are the messenger he expected, Gant gives you a ledger for his secret contacts. You carry it to Mennet Carkad in the Rogues' Quarter, opening the way to deeper covert work for the Forsaken state. Andron Gant works from the Undercity, keeping names and information in a personal ledger. Believing you are the courier he expected, he hands it over for delivery to the secret contacts he serves. Gant asks that the same courier carry future messages, unaware that the ledger is bound for the Deathstalkers.

quest:1918.text: The Befouled Element. Around Mystral Lake, you find glowing globes of tainted water among the slain elementals. You carry a specimen to Mastok Wrilehiss at Splintertree Post to learn what has poisoned the lake and its spirits. Mystral Lake lies in south-central Ashenvale, and its water elementals have grown violently aggressive and visibly corrupted. When slain, they leave strange, intensely glowing spheres of putrid fluid instead of pure elemental essence. The globes hold the corruption that has settled over the lake, showing that something more than natural territorial aggression is at work.

quest:1941.text: Manaweave Robe. In Stormwind, Wynne Larson presents the Manaweave Robe as a proud showcase for her family’s shop. She has woven the enchanted garment from fine materials for a commission that is now complete. Larson Clothiers serves spellcasters in Stormwind’s Mage Quarter with garments made to channel volatile energies. Fine magical robes call for rare materials, careful needlework, and threadwork that holds through mystic resonance. Wynne Larson takes pride in each piece that leaves her shop, where every robe worn into the field carries the Larson name. The manaweave robe offers comfort, mobility, and practical resilience for travel through contested lands. Once the needed components are delivered, Wynne Larson weaves the final stitch herself and presents the finished garment as a fine example of Larson tailoring, meant to draw admiration and spread the shop’s name across the kingdom.

quest:1959.text: Report to Anastasia. Horde mages from across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms are called to the Undercity. Anastasia Hartwell has sensed an unknown magical disturbance there and needs capable spellcasters to investigate. Horde mages hear of trouble in the Undercity. Those studying atop the bluffs of Thunder Bluff, in the dusty heat of Durotar, or among the ruins of Lordaeron receive the same call if they have enough skill. The Undercity's mages have sensed an unexplained disturbance within their domain and need help investigating it. Anastasia Hartwell oversees arcane matters in the Undercity's Magic Quarter. She confirms that mages have detected strange energies within the city. No one knows whether the magic is harmless or hostile. Anastasia needs a capable mage to investigate quietly, beginning in the Apothecarium.

quest:1960.text: Investigate the Alchemist Shop. An arcane disturbance has brought invisible creatures into Algernon's shop in the Undercity. Anastasia Hartwell sends Horde mages to reveal and contain them before they can cause harm. Anastasia Hartwell sends arcane initiates to investigate a disturbance in the Apothecarium. Invisible magical creatures have been wandering through Algernon's alchemy shop, among its cauldrons and reagents. The Undercity's mage instructor suspects a breach in the flow of magic. The creatures must be contained before they cause serious damage. Anastasia gives her students a Cantation of Manifestation to reveal the invisible creatures, along with sturdy containment coffers. Ordinary tracking cannot find beings made entirely of raw arcane force. Once visible, the rift spawns must be weakened and sealed in the coffers before they can unravel further or harm the alchemists at work.

quest:1961.text: Gathering Materials. In the Undercity, Anastasia Hartwell sends aspiring Horde mages to Silverpine Forest for Dalaran mana gems. They also need linen to make their first true mage's robes. Undercity initiates gather the materials for their first true robes: a bolt of simple linen and potent Dalaran mana gems. The robes mark their station and personal worth, and Anastasia Hartwell directs the novices to harvest these raw components for an enchanted weave. The mana gems cannot be bought or conjured. Dalaran mages are stationed across Silverpine Forest, especially near Ambermill, and the gems must be taken from them. Anastasia Hartwell says Dalaran's arcane philosophies mirror those of the Forsaken, but sentiment has no place in the Undercity. To the Forsaken, wizards too weak to defend their relics forfeit both their treasures and their lives. Josef Gregorian, a tailor in the Undercity's Magic Quarter, receives the gathered cloth and gems. He admits he lacks the magical talent to judge the pristine quality of Dalaran's enchanted stones, but he has the rare artisan skill to weave their raw power into the robes.

quest:1962.text: Spellfire Robes. In the Undercity, Spellfire Robes mark a young Horde mage's rite of passage. Josef Gregorian, a tailor, completes the robes after the apprentice gathers rare components from across the realm. In Lordaeron, you seek more than ordinary cloth to channel and shield your growing magic. Josef Gregorian works as a tailor in the Undercity's Magic Quarter, where he weaves magical garments from specialized materials gathered by promising Horde spellcasters. The final stitching marks your passage beyond basic incantations toward mastery of arcane and fire magic. Josef Gregorian needs alchemical and arcane components to make robes that focus powerful magic. You gather those supplies through dangerous trials and bring them to his sanctum in the Undercity. There, Gregorian weaves them together, giving you a sign of growing status and protection as an aspiring mage.

quest:1963.text: The Shattered Hand. Therzok tests rogues in Orgrimmar who seek entry to the secretive Shattered Hand. Their trial sends them after Tazan, a troll smuggler, and his locked satchel. The Shattered Hand works from the Cleft of Shadow beneath Orgrimmar. The order of assassins and thieves follows old orcish traditions. Warchief Thrall rules the young Horde with honor, diplomacy, and caution, but the Shattered Hand's leaders believe restraint weakens their people. They seek to restore martial supremacy through covert violence, using knives and poison when a battlefield charge may fail.

quest:1978.text: The Deathstalkers. In Undercity, the Deathstalkers bring a new operative into their ranks. You carry Andron's Ledger to Varimathras, proof of the Syndicate's covert activities. Mennet Carkad welcomes you into the Deathstalkers after you uncover records from Andron Gant. The order serves Lady Sylvanas as eyes, ears, and daggers throughout Lordaeron. Its agents use intelligence networks, ruthless efficiency, and stealth to remove threats before they surface. Recognition by the order marks a step into service for the Forsaken. You deliver the sensitive ledger directly to Varimathras in the Royal Quarter of Undercity. The nathrezim commander oversees Forsaken tactical intelligence under Sylvanas Windrunner. Pleased by the Deathstalkers' initiative, Varimathras welcomes your demonstrated ability and says his intelligence division can use someone who delivers results.

quest:199.text: A Dark Threat Looms. At the Stonewrought Dam, sabotage threatens a vital barrier in Loch Modan. A barrel hidden near the water holds strange smelling powder, and you bring a sample to Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII. Whispers of sabotage have drawn attention to the shoreline around the Stonewrought Dam. Near the water's edge, an out-of-place barrel holds strange, pungent powder that has no place among the dam's maintenance supplies.

quest:1998.text: Fenwick Thatros. In the Undercity, Mennet Carkad sends promising rogues after Fenwick Thatros on Lord Varimathras's orders. Thatros is suspected of organizing independent undead forces along Silverpine Forest's shores. Killing him proves an operative's mettle to the Deathstalkers and opens the way to advanced trade training. In the Undercity's Rogues' Quarter, Mennet Carkad handles Deathstalker contracts and training. The Deathstalkers are the Forsaken's secretive intelligence wing. Lord Varimathras has named Fenwick Thatros as a priority target, a charge too serious for novice recruits. Thatros has established a foothold among rogue undead in Silverpine Forest. If left alone, their independent leadership could threaten Forsaken control across Lordaeron's old holdings. Deathstalker scouts report Fenwick Thatros near a decrepit dock on Lake Lordamere in Silverpine Forest. Reaching him means crossing wilderness claimed by feral beasts, Rot Hide gnolls, and Scourge remnants. Varimathras demands proof of the kill: Thatros's severed head. Bringing it back can earn an operative entry into deeper covert operations.

quest:2038.text: Bingles' Missing Supplies. Bingles Blastenheimer is stranded on Loch Modan's southeastern shore after troggs steal his gear. He needs his tools and Blastencapper explosives to repair his gyrocopter and return to the fight for Gnomeregan. Bingles Blastenheimer crashes his gyrocopter into Loch Modan's cold waters. He survives and drags himself ashore, but troggs from the lake's central islands swarm the dazed pilot and steal his most valuable belongings. Troggs scatter Bingles' gear among their island camps. His missing supplies include a wrench, screwdriver, and hammer, along with the Blastenheimer Blastencapper, his volatile, high-yield invention. Losing ordinary tools is troublesome; leaving explosives in a region crawling with troggs puts travelers in immediate danger. Bingles fights for the liberation of his fallen homeland, Gnomeregan. It is overrun by subterranean troggs and irradiated leper gnomes, and he imagines a decisive aerial assault to break their hold. Without his tools and Blastencappers, he cannot rebuild his flying machine, and his campaign remains grounded in the reeds.

quest:2039.text: Find Bingles. In Ironforge, Gnoarn worries that Bingles Blastenheimer has been missing for more than a week. The gnome aviator vanished during a flight toward fallen Gnomeregan, and Gnoarn sends searchers to the shores of Loch Modan. There, Bingles is alive and needs mechanical salvage. Gnome aviator Bingles Blastenheimer was sent from Tinker Town in Ironforge on an aerial reconnaissance flight over the irradiated ruins of Gnomeregan. More than a week has passed without word, and Gnoarn fears Bingles may have blown himself out of the sky, a danger of gnome engineering. The last report placed the eccentric flyer somewhere above Loch Modan's waters. Searchers find Bingles alive along the Loch Modan shoreline, far from a tragic pile of wreckage. He is unfazed by his long absence and takes slight offense that anyone doubted his piloting. Rather than return promptly to report to Gnoarn, Bingles enlists his rescuer to recover tools and Blastencapper explosives stolen by troggs. He wants them so he can resume his duties for the gnomish movement.

quest:2041.text: Speak with Shoni. Alliance travelers in Ironforge are sent south to find Shoni the Shilent in Stormwind. She leads an underground assault unit preparing to support the effort to reclaim Gnomeregan. After Gnomeregan fell to radiation, surviving gnomes made an exile quarter in Ironforge. Engineers, tinkers, and strategists there keep planning how to breach their lost home. Central planning remains in Tinkertown, but preparations reach far beyond Khaz Modan. Adventurers in the mountain city are directed south to Stormwind, where specialized military hardware is being prepared for fighting underground. Shoni the Shilent commands an elite underground assault crew in Stormwind's Dwarven District, among its anvils and forges. Her sappers need gyrodrillmatic excavationators to burrow toward sectors held by troggs. The Deeprun Tram now links Ironforge directly to Stormwind beneath the mountains, making the journey to Shoni straightforward.

quest:21.text: Skirmish at Echo Ridge. In Northshire Valley, recruits strike at kobolds in Echo Ridge Mine. Marshal McBride ordered the attack after scouts found the mine overrun. Marshal McBride sends recruits against the kobolds in Echo Ridge Mine. Scouts found the mine overrun, and the garrison fears the creatures will strengthen their hold if left alone. The kobolds dig through the tunnels, gather stolen resources, and multiply. Recruits must thin their numbers to protect Northshire Valley, with its farms and spiritual retreat. New recruits are sent into the mine because the Stormwind Army is stretched thin. Garrison forces guard the southern borders, while unrest is rumored across Elwynn. Officers like McBride must call on willing hands. A recruit who proves reliable at Echo Ridge earns the army’s respect and is ready for more difficult work elsewhere in the kingdom.

quest:2118.text: Plagued Lands. Corruption is spreading through Darkshore, where Tharnariun Treetender hopes to save the afflicted wildlife. He asks travelers to calm a rabid thistle bear with an enchanted relic and bring it back alive. A creeping sickness twists Darkshore’s beasts into maddened, aggressive versions of themselves. Thistle bears suffer most, their rabid frenzy threatening travelers and the coast’s fragile balance. Night elf sentinels often answer with steel, while druids seek to understand the sickness and heal its cause. Tharnariun Treetender refuses to kill the corrupted beasts without first trying to save them. He made a trap called Tharnariun’s Hope. Set on the forest floor, its soothing light briefly calms a raging thistle bear. Pacified, the bear follows the traveler back to Tharnariun’s outpost for study.

quest:2138.text: Cleansing of the Infected. In Darkshore, Tharnariun Treetender faces a hard choice over the infected thistle bears. His attempt to cure one has failed, and he asks you to kill the rabid beasts before they harm other creatures or spread the sickness. Tharnariun Treetender has searched for a remedy to the sickness spreading through Darkshore's wildlife. He tried to cleanse a captured bear, but the thistle bears remain diseased and violent. Now he asks you to put them down. He fears they will maul other creatures and carry the sickness farther into the ancient woodlands.

quest:2139.text: Tharnariun's Hope. In Darkshore, Tharnariun Treetender's work against the wildlife sickness reaches a grim turning point. After travelers put down infected beasts across the woodlands, he sends an Alliance champion after the rabid Den Mother northeast of Auberdine. After the Third War, an unnatural rabid sickness began afflicting Darkshore's wild creatures. Tharnariun Treetender, stationed in Auberdine, spent days asking travelers to put down infected beasts and ease the forest's suffering. But killing rabid thistle bears treated only a symptom. Tharnariun decided the source among the local bears had to be removed: their matriarch, the Den Mother. After the Den Mother's death, Tharnariun offers profound thanks, though melancholy shadows his words. For the kaldorei, raising weapons against woodland creatures is agonizing. Dark forces press against their new home, and many despair or seek shelter. The defenders of Auberdine accept the heavy moral burden of protecting their wilderness.

quest:214.text: Red Silk Bandanas. Scout Riell sends the People's Militia after Red Silk Bandanas in the Deadmines. Their fine weave marks the Defias leaders who direct the uprising in Westfall. Scout Riell and the People's Militia have learned that cloth marks rank in the Defias Brotherhood. Common cutpurses and highwaymen across Westfall tie coarse red cloth over their faces. Senior conspirators and inner-circle operatives wear fine red silk. Bringing back their bandanas strikes at the experienced officers coordinating Edwin VanCleef's uprising. The senior outlaws gather deep in the Deadmines beneath Moonbrook. Sentinels and scouts outside Sentinel Hill depend on freelance champions to enter the contested tunnels. Each silk bandana recovered means one fewer lieutenant organizing ambushes, guarding weapon caches, or enforcing VanCleef's rule across Westfall.

quest:2159.text: Dolanaar Delivery. Travelers leave Shadowglen with a parcel of herbs bound for Dolanaar. Porthannius, occupied with the druids, asks them to carry it south, marking their first venture beyond the sheltered glade. Porthannius asks travelers heading south from Shadowglen to carry a bundle of freshly harvested herbs along the forest path. He is occupied with pressing business alongside the druids tending the glade, and cannot leave to handle the errand himself. The bundle goes south as young adventurers prepare to leave the training grounds for the wider reaches of Teldrassil. The southern road from Shadowglen leads to Dolanaar, a foremost night elf settlement on Teldrassil's great boughs. Innkeeper Keldamyr oversees hospitality, rest, and supplies for wanderers, sentinels, and druids. When he receives the herbs on Porthannius's behalf, he urges young adventurers to rest their minds and spirits before facing the corruption spreading across the world tree.

quest:2160.text: Supplies to Tannok. A crate bound for Tannok Frosthammer waits at the mouth of Coldridge Pass. Hands Springsprocket asks travelers to carry the inn supplies from Coldridge Valley to the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, since troggs have cut off the usual trade routes. Troggs have overrun Coldridge Pass, straining Coldridge Valley’s ties to the rest of Dun Morogh. The valley has long sheltered young Ironforge dwarves and Gnomeregan survivors in exile. Now the mountain pass is perilous to cross. Mountaineers are spread thin guarding settlements and defensive perimeters, so scheduled supply escorts can be delayed for days. At the mouth of Coldridge Pass, the gnome tinkerer Hands Springsprocket waits with a crate of supplies for the inn in Kharanos. He cannot safely carry it there himself. Travelers preparing to cross the pass can take the cargo to Tannok Frosthammer, the assistant at the Thunderbrew inn. Kharanos marks your arrival in the wider lands of Dun Morogh. Tannok Frosthammer receives the supplies and says word from Anvilmar has been scarce since troggs disrupted travel through the pass. The delivery restores a fragile link of communication and trade between the two isolated dwarf communities.

quest:2161.text: A Peon's Burden. Ukor waits on the trail outside the Valley of Trials with a load he cannot carry home. The recruits in the red canyon refused his provisions, and now he asks travelers to return them to Razor Hill. Ukor set out from Razor Hill with provisions for the fresh recruits training in the red canyon. He believed they needed the food, but the taskmasters turned him away. They keep supplies lean because they believe meager rations teach young Horde warriors discipline and endurance. Innkeeper Grosk later explains that this hardship is part of their training. Ukor reached the pass, but fears the return trip across Durotar. Scorpids, venomous spiders, and prowling boars haunt the rocky trail. He has no weapons or armor, and lacks the fighting spirit expected of an orcish grunt. Waiting along the path, he asks travelers leaving the proving grounds to carry his heavy provisions back to the inn in Razor Hill.

quest:217.text: In Defense of the King's Lands. Captain Rugelfuss sends you after the Stonesplinter troggs’ leader in Loch Modan. Scouts have traced their attacks to Chieftain Grawmug, deep in Stonesplinter Valley. His death may break the pack’s resolve and help reclaim the King’s Lands. Captain Rugelfuss’s scouts have found that the Stonesplinter troggs follow a chieftain named Grawmug. Their attacks threaten the King’s Lands in southern Loch Modan. You are sent into their lair to kill Grawmug and his personal bruisers, in hopes of breaking the pack’s cohesion and stopping its advance. Grawmug holds a cavern in the southeastern cliffs of Stonesplinter Valley, with his trusted brutes Gnasher and Brawler beside him. The three pose a danger to a lone soldier. Defeating them could throw the remaining troggs into disarray and give the beleaguered Mountaineers time to fortify the roads and drive the beasts back underground.

quest:2178.text: Easy Strider Living. In Auberdine, Alanndarian Nightsong offers to share her strider stew recipe with hunters who bring her foreststrider meat. Auberdine's coastal folk make use of the wildlife around them. Alanndarian Nightsong has her own recipe for hearty strider stew, made from the tall foreststriders that roam Darkshore's woods. She asks you to hunt the birds and bring back their meat before she shares her cooking. Foreststriders range through the woodlands and beaches north and south of Auberdine. Their sharp beaks and quick tempers make them dangerous when provoked, but their meat makes a rich stew. Bring fresh meat to Alanndarian, and she will share her recipe.

quest:218.text: The Stolen Journal. In Coldridge Valley, Grelin Whitebeard needs his stolen journal back. The Frostmane troll leader Grik'nir the Cold took it into the troll cave, and Grelin cannot finish his appraisal of the troll threat without his notes. Grelin Whitebeard has watched the Frostmane trolls press into Coldridge Valley and recorded their habits and sudden aggression. In the unrest, an imposing troll stole his personal journal and fled into the depths of the trolls' den. The loss matters beyond sentiment: the notebook holds most of Grelin's reconnaissance. Until it is recovered from the cavern, his assessment of the threat remains unfinished. Grik'nir the Cold took Grelin's journal. The powerful Frostmane troll, marked with distinctive paint on his body and face, holds court in the heart of the valley's troll cave. Defeating Grik'nir breaks the cave trolls' immediate leadership and secures the journal. With it back, Grelin can finish his findings and judge the troll situation in Coldridge Valley manageable. He sends the completed report to his brother Senir.

quest:22.text: Goretusk Liver Pie. At the Saldean Farm in Westfall, Salma Saldean prepares a pie amid hard times. Bandits have ravaged the breadbasket of the kingdom, and local homesteaders hunt aggressive boars to feed their families. Westfall was once Stormwind's fertile breadbasket, but hard times have fallen on the land. Neglected roads, roving outlaws, and overgrown fields make daily life a struggle for the few settlers who remain. At the Saldean Farm, Salma Saldean works to keep a sense of home despite the dangers around her. A traditional meat pie offers one of the few modest comforts for homesteaders trying to preserve their way of life. Goretusks roam Westfall's plains in great numbers, their tough hides and vicious tusks making them dangerous. They threaten lone farmhands, yet provide vital meat to families cut off from regular trade. Salma's recipe calls for crushed rosemary, minced garlic, chopped dill, and simmering gravy. With careful preparation, the pungent organs of these hardy beasts become a rich, savory meal.

quest:2205.text: Seek out SI: 7. In Goldshire, Keryn Sylvius sends new rogues toward SI: 7. A sealed package carried to Stormwind City brings them before Master Mathias Shaw, who leads the crown's covert intelligence network. At the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire, rogue trainer Keryn Sylvius wastes no time praising newcomers. She thinks fresh initiates look more like cheese delivery hands than covert agents, yet gives them a sealed delivery for the capital. The trip tests their reliability as couriers and quietly vets scouts for wider service to the realm. SI: 7 works from the southeastern corner of Old Town in Stormwind City. The worn district holds the command center of Stormwind Intelligence, Section 7, where Master Mathias Shaw oversees the kingdom's covert operations. Shaw receives the package with dry skepticism and judges whether the traveler has the grit for real espionage.

quest:2206.text: Snatch and Grab. Master Mathias Shaw sends agents to Jerod's Landing for shipping intelligence. The Defias Brotherhood uses the river dock to move supplies in secret. Master Mathias Shaw tests aspiring operatives who seek a place in Stormwind's covert intelligence wing. He asks for finesse and stealth, not brute force. SI:7 agents take down key figures quietly and recover important papers without drawing the realm into open scandal. Each new operative must prove they can work unseen. Jerod's Landing lies on the river in southern Elwynn, south of Goldshire and just east of the Maclure Vineyards. The Defias Brotherhood seized the once-quiet dock and made it an illicit route. Smuggled arms, supplies, and contraband cross the water from Redridge toward Westfall, beyond the reach of royal road patrols. Master Mathias Shaw warns agents that capture, compromise, or death leaves them without the Crown's support. Stormwind and its spymasters will deny knowing they ever existed. Recovering the Defias Dockmaster's schedule gives SI:7 proof of the Brotherhood's supply lines while keeping Stormwind's official involvement hidden.

quest:224.text: In Defense of the King's Lands. At the southern watchtower, In Defense of the King's Lands rests on Mountaineer Cobbleflint and those who answer his call. Stonesplinter troggs press toward the Valley of Kings while Ironforge's forces serve on distant fronts. Mountaineer Cobbleflint and the guards at the southern watchtower face a growing trogg invasion. The great dwarven monuments of the Valley of Kings look down on a garrison under strain. King Magni Bronzebeard has sent much of his regular army abroad to support the Alliance. Local patrols and hired blades must keep the province from being overrun. Stonesplinter Valley cuts through Loch Modan's southern peaks, and the troggs have burrowed up from its depths. Their scouts and warriors have built camps along the valley floor. If left unchecked, their parties threaten the roads to the southern passes, leaving the Mountaineers to fight them without pause.

quest:2242.text: Destiny Calls. Syurna sends you to learn what Sethir the Ancient knows of Teldrassil's corruption. The satyr waits near the Oracle Glade, beyond the reach of those who tried force or diplomacy. Teldrassil's growing sickness troubles the night elf leaders in Darnassus. Syurna, the rogue trainer, needs someone subtle; armed patrols have died trying to reach Sethir the Ancient. The satyr roosts on a remote bough near the Oracle Glade and has turned away force and diplomacy alike. To learn what he knows, you need to enter his lair and take his personal possessions.

quest:2259.text: Erion Shadewhisper. Jannok Breezesong sends promising rogues from Teldrassil to Darnassus. At the Cenarion Enclave, Erion Shadewhisper points them toward work beyond the forests. Jannok Breezesong sends you from Teldrassil to find Erion Shadewhisper in Darnassus. You need not worry about being sent to the exacting trainer Syurna. Erion waits in the Cenarion Enclave, where he handles work that calls for a quieter touch. Erion Shadewhisper marks a change for rogues in night elf lands. Teldrassil's forests can no longer contain your duties. Erion sends capable hands into a wider, more dangerous world, toward work across the sea.

quest:2260.text: Erion's Behest. Across the Great Sea, Erion's Behest carries a summons to promising night elf rogues in Darnassus. Erion Shadewhisper sees their growing skill in stealth and sends them to Stormwind City to report to Stormwind Intelligence. Night elf rogues in Teldrassil's shadow train under mentors such as Erion Shadewhisper. When one shows exceptional talent, word reaches beyond the World Tree. Through Erion, Stormwind Intelligence, known as SI:7, invites the rogue across the Great Sea to the human capital. The journey leads from northern Kalimdor through the docks of Darkshore or the Wetlands to Stormwind City. In the capital, you make your way to SI:7 headquarters in Old Town and report to Renzik "The Shiv." He assesses newcomers and opens the way to advanced espionage, poison mastery, and covert operations for the Alliance.

quest:2281.text: Redridge Rendezvous. Promising Alliance rogues are sent east from Stormwind’s intelligence headquarters to train in Lakeshire. SI:7 wants them ready for dangerous field work under seasoned operatives. Renzik 'The Shiv', SI:7’s second-in-command in Stormwind, warns that untrained rogues rarely survive dangerous operations. Sending raw recruits into hostile territory brings casualties instead of intelligence. SI:7 sends promising agents east to the Redridge Mountains, where they train under Lucius, stationed among Lakeshire’s docks. Lakeshire offers an ideal ground for clandestine training. Gnolls and Blackrock orcs threaten the frontier town, while its piers give Lucius cover to test a rogue’s stealth, reflexes, and lockpicking without attracting townspeople or guards.

quest:2300.text: SI:7. In Goldshire, Keryn Sylvius sends promising young rogues toward Stormwind's hidden ranks. Recruits report to Renzik "The Shiv" in Old Town, where they enter Master Mathias Shaw's service. Keryn Sylvius watches local recruits from the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire. When a rogue proves cunning and capable against the growing Defias threat, Sylvius passes along a message from headquarters. The order is plain: report to Renzik "The Shiv" without delay. The recruit leaves Elwynn's fields for the covert heart of Stormwind. Behind an unassuming barracks in Old Town, SI:7 keeps its headquarters. Master Mathias Shaw commands the agency, whose work includes covert operations, reconnaissance, and assassination across the kingdom and beyond. Renzik "The Shiv," Shaw's sharp-tongued second-in-command, assesses promising agents before sending them into dangerous work beyond the reach of the kingdom's formal military.

quest:233.text: Coldridge Valley Mail Delivery. At Anvilmar, Coldridge Valley Mail Delivery carries news to scouts beyond the frozen lake. Snow and nearby troggs can leave the valley's defenders cut off, so correspondence keeps them connected. In Coldridge Valley, news from the rest of Dun Morogh reaches Anvilmar by mountain pass. Winter couriers bring the mail, and the letters soon gather in the hall. Sten Stoutarm manages supplies and security, so he depends on recruits to carry the bundles down the western road. Without them, important messages would remain at Anvilmar. Talin Keeneye watches the frozen lake to the west, keeping an eye on trogg movements and dangerous wildlife. Even at a cold outpost, news from Ironforge and the surrounding camps matters. The mountain conditions make sorting mail difficult, and letters for different scouts can end up together in one bundle.

quest:234.text: Coldridge Valley Mail Delivery. Talin Keeneye's dispatch is bound for Grelin Whitebeard's camp in Coldridge Valley. Carrying it down the southeastern road keeps the mountaineers in touch with Ironforge. Couriers carry news through Coldridge Valley, where field scouts and sentries need word from the high passes and Ironforge. Anvilmar is the valley's administrative heart, but those posted along the trails rely on foot messengers to carry their dispatches. Grelin Whitebeard keeps a small camp southeast of Talin Keeneye's post. Veteran mountaineers at these remote watchpoints face freezing drifts and trogg harassment, and depend on regular letters to follow affairs across Dun Morogh and the kingdom beyond.

quest:2378.text: Find the Shattered Hand. In Orgrimmar, the Shattered Hand awaits a promising Forsaken rogue from Tirisfal Glades. The Deathstalkers send the initiate across the sea to Durotar to learn specialized arts from the clan. Mennet Carkad has seen a rogue prove their worth in Tirisfal Glades. The Forsaken train their own covert order, the Deathstalkers, and their alliance with the Horde opens a path to learn darker arts. He directs promising rogues to seek the Shattered Hand in Orgrimmar, joining Lordaeron’s undead operatives with Kalimdor’s orcish assassins. The journey ends beneath Orgrimmar in the Cleft of Shadow, where warlocks, rogues, and demon-binders work out of sight. Shenthul, a Shattered Hand trainer, awaits there. The gruff troll judges the newly arrived undead agent with harsh skepticism. Reputation alone will not satisfy him; he wants to see whether the envoy has real cunning or has wasted the voyage across the Great Sea.

quest:2379.text: Zando'zan. In Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow, promising rogues begin training with the Shattered Hand. Trainer Shenthul sends his chosen initiate to meet Zando'zan and enter the Horde's covert ranks. Orgrimmar's rulers know brute strength cannot win every war. Beneath the city, the Cleft of Shadow houses the Shattered Hand, a covert guild that handles espionage, sabotage, and theft for the Horde. When rogue trainer Shenthul sees promise in an initiate, he sends them to report to Zando'zan for dedicated operative training. Zando'zan does not grant respect to every inexperienced rogue who enters the cavern. Meeting him marks a formal initiation into the finer clandestine arts, beginning with stealth, subterfuge, and thievery. His training bridges the distance between rough street cutpurses and organized intelligence operatives, preparing rogues for fieldwork beyond the safety of the capital's red canyon walls.

quest:2380.text: To Orgrimmar!. Kaplak sends a young rogue from Razor Hill to Orgrimmar. There, you are to find Shenthul in the Cleft of Shadow and enter the Shattered Hand's network. Kaplak sends you north from Razor Hill to Orgrimmar. Your budding skills have caught the notice of more prominent handlers, though they remain unpolished. The red crags of Durotar are behind you as you make for the capital.

quest:2381.text: Plundering the Plunderers. Wrenix the Wretched sends new Shattered Hand rogues against the Southsea Freebooters near Ratchet. Aboard the Tide Razor, they face pirates, locked strongboxes, and a dangerous guardian before claiming the Southsea Treasure. Wrenix the Wretched, a goblin contact in Ratchet, tests aspiring Shattered Hand operatives. He sends rogues south along the Barrens coast to a cove where the Tide Razor lies at anchor, crewed by Southsea Freebooters. They must board without being seen, enter the pirates’ den where cutpurses train, pick the strongboxes in the hold, and bring back the plunder.

quest:2382.text: Wrenix of Ratchet. In Orgrimmar, Wrenix of Ratchet draws Horde rogues toward a goblin port far to the south. Zando'zan sends them to aid Wrenix the Wretched, a disreputable goblin in Ratchet. In Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow, the rogue guild works out of winding crevices, largely unseen. Zando'zan, a troll who speaks in wild ramblings, greets operatives with ominous portents. His visions include Warchief Thrall struck down by poison and blade. He gives no explanation for the prophecy, and quickly sends agents south to the port town of Ratchet in the Barrens. Ratchet lies on the Barrens coast, east of the Crossroads. Scoundrels, mercenaries, and tinkerers gather in the neutral port, where Wrenix the Wretched makes his home. Wrenix has little patience for Zando'zan's eccentric ways. He says the troll's earlier recruits met grim ends in the bay, among its hungry predators.

quest:239.text: Westbrook Garrison Needs Help!. Marshal Dughan sends available adventurers west to Westbrook Garrison, the outpost at Elwynn Forest's border with Westfall. Stormwind's army is stretched thin across the kingdom, while Deputy Rainer and his guards face growing pressure from Riverpaw gnolls and wandering thieves without regular reinforcements. Westbrook Garrison guards the western edge of Elwynn Forest, where settled woodland meets Westfall's troubled plains. Gnoll warbands and bandits grow bolder along the waterways and western roads, and the small garrison has asked for more men. Marshal Dughan and Goldshire's administration have no Stormwind soldiers to spare. Local commanders must hire traveling mercenaries and wandering adventurers. Deputy Rainer and his men face the Riverpaw gnolls, whose raiding parties harass travelers and nearby homesteads. The pack operates in the borderlands between Elwynn and Westfall. With Stormwind distracted by political and military troubles, the gnolls press deeper into inhabited territory. Westbrook Garrison guards against their unchecked advance into the heart of the forest.

quest:2399.text: The Sprouted Fronds. At Denalan's garden by Lake Al'Ameth, the planted frond has taken root and sprouted. Travelers can see the new growth among the garden beds. You find Denalan's garden near Lake Al'Ameth, where the botanist studies Teldrassil's peculiar plants. After a shimmering frond is planted, new fronds rise from the soil in his planter, ready to be gathered and examined. Teldrassil is young and vast, and its plant life grows quickly. Night elf herbalists find that growth fascinating and troubling. The shimmering fronds and their offshoots show how quickly life takes hold on the World Tree's boughs, though its vitality can be hard to predict.

quest:2438.text: The Emerald Dreamcatcher. In Dolanaar, Tallonkai Swiftroot asks you to recover a cherished heirloom from his abandoned home in Starbreeze Village. Gaerolas Talvethren, the druid warden, gave him the Emerald Dreamcatcher, which he left behind when corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs overran the settlement. Recovering it keeps its gentle nature magic from falling into foul hands. Gaerolas Talvethren gave Tallonkai a rare druidic talisman. The warden watches over the sleeping druids within Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Crafted to channel the serene currents of the Emerald Dream, the amulet draws on that pure spiritual energy to bring peace and fortune to its bearer. Such gifts go only to a trusted few whose lives are bound to the forest's care. Starbreeze Village was peaceful until the Gnarlpine furbolgs succumbed to violent madness. They drove the villagers from their ancestral homes. During the fearful flight, Tallonkai left his most treasured possession hidden inside his dresser in the village's southeastern quarter. He could not reclaim it on his own.

quest:244.text: Encroaching Gnolls. Gnolls have reached the western road into Redridge, and Lakeshire fears being cut off. Guard Parker spots camps near the border and sends word to Deputy Feldon. The warning confirms the town’s fear that the beastmen may isolate Redridge. Guard Parker watches the western border trail, where the road runs from Elwynn Forest into Redridge Mountains. Stormwind’s forces have thinned, leaving the route with few defenders. Parker keeps the gravel road open for supply wagons, but his scouts find gnoll warbands advancing from the crags to the north and east. Their camps lie alarmingly close to the road. Deputy Feldon receives the warning near the Lakeshire bridge and sees how much danger the town faces. Redridge gnolls are raiding near Lakeshire, and their camps near the Elwynn border could let them encircle the town and push into the kingdom’s heartland. Stormwind has ignored pleas for reinforcements, leaving Lakeshire’s watch unready for threats from both sides.

quest:2459.text: Ferocitas the Dream Eater. Tallonkai Swiftroot in Dolanaar sends you after a stolen emerald in northern Teldrassil. The jewel was pried from his damaged heirloom dreamcatcher by Gnarlpine furbolgs north of Starbreeze Village, and now hangs from their leader, Ferocitas the Dream Eater. Tallonkai Swiftroot felt relief when the dreamcatcher recovered from the corrupted wilds came back to him, then dismay at its ruined state. The sacred artifact had been vandalized, its emerald centerpiece pried from the woven frame. Night elves spoke of Gnarlpine mystics north of Starbreeze Village, fallen under the influence of a furbolg leader named Ferocitas the Dream Eater. He wore a brilliant green stone around his neck. In Ferocitas's clutches, the sacred gem was useless and perverse, so Tallonkai sent defenders to take it back. The Gnarlpine furbolgs in Teldrassil's northern reaches were once peaceful neighbors. Corruption seeping into the World Tree drove them into frenzy and madness. Their mystics once practiced harmonious nature rites, but began drawing on distorted magical energies. Travelers can track down Ferocitas by cutting through the mystics guarding his woodland enclave. The jewel can then be returned to Tallonkai, so his dreamcatcher may be made whole and balance restored to the woods.

quest:246.text: Assessing the Threat. Deputy Feldon needs a measure of the gnoll threat near Lakeshire. With the garrison stretched thin and Stormwind withholding reinforcements, he hires travelers to thin the packs and learn their strength. Lakeshire faces Blackrock orc warbands from the heights and aggressive gnoll packs in the valleys. Its defenders are too few for ordinary scouting patrols. When reports confirmed gnolls pressing toward the border, Deputy Feldon sought help from travelers. He pays champions to test the enemy in the wild, rather than send guards the town cannot spare. You scout along Redridge's southern road, striking the camps of Redridge Mongrels and Poachers. Each fight thins the gnolls' forward scouts and disrupts their supply lines. It also reveals whether the packs are roaming scavengers or an organized force threatening Lakeshire. The fighting gives Feldon numbers he can use to plan the town's strained defense.

quest:2498.text: Return to Denalan. At Lake Al'Ameth, Return to Denalan carries Rellian's alarming news to the botanist studying corruption in Teldrassil. After examining the mossy tumors on timberlings, you head south to help Denalan with his discovery. Rellian Greenspyre studies the mossy tumors afflicting Teldrassil's timberlings when urgent word arrives from his colleague Denalan. At his camp beside Lake Al'Ameth, Denalan has finally isolated the cause of these unnatural growths on the forest's nature spirits. Rellian recognizes the gravity of this discovery and sends you south at once to lend a hand.

quest:2499.text: Oakenscowl. Along Lake Al'Ameth, blight spreads from a corrupted timberling called Oakenscowl. Denalan asks you to end the threat. The maddened creature dwells in a cave on the lake's southern bank. Timberlings tend the boughs of Teldrassil, and Oakenscowl once led them. Now corruption runs through the world tree, reaching humble wildlife and ancient protectors alike. A massive growth swells across Oakenscowl's bark, driving the timberling mad. Where it once guarded the forest, blight now takes hold. Oakenscowl hides in a cavern on Lake Al'Ameth's southern shore. Its presence poisons the nearby water and woodland beasts. Denalan cannot face the creature alone, so he seeks its destruction to cut off the corruption and study the strange growth afflicting the lake's spirits.

quest:250.text: A Dark Threat Looms. Dark Iron attacks in the Wetlands have Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII fearing for the Stonewrought Dam. With much of its garrison sent to the Alliance Front, you investigate sappers near the eastern ramp. The Stonewrought Dam holds back Loch Modan's waters, a great feat of Ironforge engineering. As conflicts spread across Khaz Modan and beyond, much of its security detail has been reassigned to the Alliance Front. Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII and his small remaining crew now face the threat of an attack with little protection. Dark Iron attacks in the Wetlands have given Hinderweir reason to worry. The dwarves struck the Thandol Span and pillaged the fortress town of Dun Modr. Now known Dark Iron sappers lurk near the dam's eastern ramp. Hinderweir fears the clan has turned its attention to the lifeline of Loch Modan.

quest:2518.text: Tears of the Moon. At the Temple of the Moon, Priestess A'moora mourns Lady Sathrah's madness. Once cherished by Elune, the great spider has become dangerous, and the Sisterhood seeks to end her suffering and recover her sacred spinnerets. In Darnassus's Temple of the Moon, Priestess A'moora grieves for Lady Sathrah. Sathrah was once blessed by Elune. Beneath the night sky, she wove delicate silver webs that caught the evening mist on Teldrassil's boughs. The Sisterhood of Elune gathered and kept the shimmering dew from those webs, which held healing powers for their sacred ministrations.
