quest:2519.text: The Temple of the Moon. In Darnassus, Sister Aquinne calls for aid to a suffering ancient creature in Teldrassil. The Sisterhood of Elune needs help, and this is the opening call to a solemn ritual of mercy. Sister Aquinne asks for help in the Temple Gardens. As a devoted servant of Elune, she speaks for her order: a venerable forest creature is suffering, and the Sisters cannot attend to it alone. Sister Aquinne sends you southeast to the Temple of the Moon. Priestess A'moora coordinates the rituals and practical duties needed to address Teldrassil's troubled wildlife, preparing allies to carry out a sorrowful act of mercy.

quest:2520.text: Sathrah's Sacrifice. At the Temple of the Moon, Sathrah's Sacrifice gives a fallen creature's spirit a final rite. You carry Lady Sathrah's spinnerets to Elune's sacred waters, where the Priesthood seeks to cleanse her soul of corruption. Priestess A'moora asks you to perform a final rite after Lady Sathrah is slain. The great spider fell to the dark madness spreading across Teldrassil, which twisted her peaceful nature into mindless aggression. The Priesthood of Elune seeks to redeem her fallen essence, not treat her death as a simple culling. You place her silvery spinnerets in the fountain at the heart of the Temple of the Moon. Its consecrated waters wash away the corruption and grant her release.

quest:2541.text: The Sleeping Druid. Oben Rageclaw lies asleep in Ban'ethil Barrow Den, but his spirit is caught in the Emerald Dream. Gnarlpine shamans have drawn it from his body and set his flesh moving through the den. Night elf druids sleep in barrow dens across Kalimdor while their spirits wander the Emerald Dream. Their bodies rest in stone alcoves, safe through centuries of slumber. Teldrassil's corruption has driven the Gnarlpine furbolgs to desperate savagery. In Ban'ethil Barrow Den, Gnarlpine shamans found a way to breach Oben Rageclaw's sacred rest and draw his living spirit from his sleeping body.

quest:255.text: Mercenaries. In Thelsamar, Magistrate Bluntnose hires passing fighters as Mo'grosh ogres press into northeastern Loch Modan. Ironforge's promised soldiers are months away, leaving the valley's settlements, excavations, and Stonewrought Dam exposed. Ironforge has taken months to send help to Loch Modan. Two months passed before it promised a handful of soldiers for the valley's defense, and another two months will pass before they arrive. With Thelsamar's guards stretched thin and hostile forces gathering beyond the valley, Magistrate Bluntnose cannot wait. Mo'grosh ogres have fortified a camp in the hills northeast of the loch. Their growing presence threatens Thelsamar, the Ironband Excavation Site, and the Stonewrought Dam. If the dam is attacked or damaged, the destruction downstream would be catastrophic. Without official mountaineer detachments, Bluntnose hires independent fighters to thin the ogre ranks and buy the valley time against ogres and troggs.

quest:2561.text: Druid of the Claw. Oben Rageclaw’s spirit waits in the barrows beneath Teldrassil, unable to rest. The Gnarlpine furbolgs have bound his body with a dark enchantment, and you can break that bond by destroying his soulless shell. Oben Rageclaw was resting in the barrows beneath Teldrassil when the corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs laid a voodoo enchantment over his sleeping body. The magic tore his spirit from his mortal flesh and trapped it in the Emerald Dream. Now his spirit lingers nearby, unable to rest or reclaim his body.

quest:257.text: A Hunter's Boast. At Farstrider Lodge, A Hunter's Boast puts your skill to a timed test. Daryl the Youngling challenges you to slay six mountain buzzards in Loch Modan before fifteen minutes pass. Daryl the Youngling boasts of his skill at Farstrider Lodge. He calls himself Daryl the Bold and dismisses travelers as greenhorns who cannot match his hunting prowess. To prove it, he wagers that you cannot kill six local mountain buzzards within fifteen minutes. Mountain buzzards scavenge and prey on smaller wildlife around Loch Modan's crags and hillsides. Daryl's timed hunt tests your speed, patience, and aim. If you bring down six before time runs out, his pride takes a blow. He reluctantly gives up one of his ranged weapons, then sets further hunting dares.

quest:258.text: A Hunter's Challenge. At Farstrider Lodge, A Hunter's Challenge tests your speed across Loch Modan's rugged highlands. Daryl the Youngling, a brash human, wagers his shirt that you cannot track and kill five elder mountain boars within twelve minutes, against rough ground and dangerous wildlife. Daryl the Youngling lives among the seasoned huntsmen of Farstrider Lodge, but he has none of their quiet patience. He makes up for his youth with bluster and tall hunting tales, including rambling stories of how he earned his “famous” scar. Unwilling to admit anyone else is skilled, he continually gets his fellow hunters’ names wrong. He also devises strict trials to humble newcomers and restore his inflated standing among the lodge’s residents. The elder mountain boars that roam Loch Modan’s crags and hillsides are massive, thick-skinned, and dangerous when provoked. Daryl gives you twelve minutes to find five, kill them, and confirm each kill. Finish in time, and the loudmouthed youngster retreats awkwardly, pretending he knows nothing of the extravagant wager he made so casually.

quest:26.text: A Lesson to Learn. Mathrengyl Bearwalker sends young druids from Darnassus to Moonglade to learn the ways of water. There, they meet an elder of the Cenarion Circle and begin training in their aquatic aspect. Mathrengyl Bearwalker guides young night elf druids as they practice among Darnassus’s boughs. When an initiate shows a firm bond with nature and readiness for greater responsibility, Mathrengyl sends them toward mastery of the waters. Cenarius’s gifts demand focus, and learning to cross the depths without drowning calls for guidance from the Cenarion Circle’s elders. The initiate leaves Darnassus for Moonglade, an ancient sanctuary beneath Mount Hyjal. In Nighthaven, Dendrite Starblaze waits as an elder mentor of the Cenarion Circle. Starblaze judges whether young shapeshifters are ready for the trials that lead to aquatic form. Mastering water takes both physical resilience and mental resolve.

quest:263.text: In Defense of the King's Lands. At the Southern Guard Tower, Mountaineer Wallbang calls travelers to help defend Loch Modan from the Stonesplinter troggs. With Ironforge's reserves sent to distant fronts, the southern pass is thinly held. Wallbang sends seasoned recruits into Stonesplinter Valley to strike at the clan's shamans and bonesnappers. Loch Modan's defenses are stretched thin. Ironforge's regular reserves have been summoned to distant fronts across Azeroth, leaving outposts such as the Southern Guard Tower short-handed. Mountaineer Wallbang and his few comrades face constant pressure from the Stonesplinter clan. They depend on Alliance travelers passing through to help hold the southern pass. The fighting reaches beyond stray scouts to the Stonesplinter clan's strength. Its bonesnappers provide brutal force, while its shamans use earthen magic to rally their kin. Slaying twenty of these targets weakens the clan's incursions into the lowlands and serves King Magni Bronzebeard's defense of the realm.

quest:264.text: Until Death Do Us Part. In Silverpine Forest, Until Death Do Us Part brings Clarice Foster’s old grief to Yuriv’s grave. From the Pools of Vision beneath Thunder Bluff, the Forsaken asks you to leave her keepsake pendant on the tomb of the husband who abandoned her and their children. Clarice Foster remembers her mortal marriage without fondness. As Lordaeron crumbled, Yuriv left her and their children to join a crusade against the rising undead, declaring service to the Holy Light paramount. His devotion saved neither his family nor himself. Clarice was raised into undeath, while Yuriv lies beneath a defaced stone. She wants the last tangible reminder of his broken promises cast away. Yuriv’s tomb lies in the graveyard around the Sepulcher, marked by gashes, rubbish, and weeds. Set Clarice’s pendant on the relief of his sculpted hands, and no grand magic or spiritual closure follows. The gem grows dull, and a cold, silent gust passes over the tombs, leaving the old resentments of Lordaeron’s fallen people.

quest:267.text: The Trogg Threat. At Loch Modan’s Southern Gate, Captain Rugelfuss faces a growing trogg threat with too few defenders. The Ironforge Reserve has been called away to support Alliance battlefronts, leaving the remaining garrison stretched thin. Rugelfuss asks travelers to thin the troggs in the hills and bring back their stone teeth. Captain Rugelfuss guards Loch Modan’s southern approach with only a small garrison. The dwarven mountaineers and Ironforge Reserve have been sent to reinforce Alliance battlefronts, leaving the Southern Gate guard tower short of troops. Rugelfuss is under strict orders to hold the gate, so he cannot lead an attack into the highlands. Nearby settlers and travelers remain exposed to ambushes. Troggs in the nearby crags threaten Khaz Modan, and their numbers grow quickly when left unchecked. They could overrun dwarven outposts. To buy time and thin their ranks, Rugelfuss asks travelers to strike at the troggs in their hillside warrens and bring back their stone teeth as proof.

quest:27.text: A Lesson to Learn. In Thunder Bluff, Turak Runetotem sends young tauren druids north to study the waters. Their road leads to Nighthaven in Moonglade, where the Cenarion Circle guides their training. After learning the bear form and its physical might, your studies turn to adaptability. Azeroth's waterways bring hazards that landbound travelers cannot face easily. Turak Runetotem watches his students and sends those devoted to nature north to learn the aquatic form. Turak Runetotem sends you beyond Mulgore for guidance in shaping yourself for the waters. You travel to Moonglade, the sanctuary beneath Mount Hyjal, and reach Nighthaven. There, night elf mentors of the Cenarion Circle welcome tauren students. They set factional strife aside to preserve the shared teachings of Cenarius. Dendrite Starblaze waits for you in Nighthaven, where your training begins. The night elf elder says mastery over the waters must be earned. Two trials await: one tests your endurance and composure under water, and the other calls for deep spiritual understanding of the aquatic aspect.

quest:273.text: Resupplying the Excavation. In Thelsamar, Jern Hornhelm sends you after the slow powder wagon bound for Ironband's Excavation Site. The dwarves haul blastpowder south along the Loch's shore. Ironband's Excavation Site in southern Loch Modan needs blastpowder to break through hard rock. After the powder reaches Thelsamar, quartermaster Jern Hornhelm sends Huldar, Miran, and Saean south with three barrels. The cargo slows their pack team along the lakeside road, giving travelers in Thelsamar time to catch up and help along the way.

quest:274.text: A Dark Threat Looms. At the Stonewrought Dam, suspicious powder puts Loch Modan and Ironforge in danger. Ashlan Stonesmirk in Dun Modr identifies it as unstable Seaforium, which can explode catastrophically when it touches water. Ashlan Stonesmirk recognizes the silver crystals and distinct odor in samples from the Stonewrought Dam as Seaforium. It stays inert while dry, but moisture makes it react violently. An unchecked explosion could blow Ironforge out of the mountain, Ashlan warns.

quest:2751.text: Barbaric Battlements. In Orgrimmar, Orokk Omosh seeks someone to carry on his family's forge craft. With no heirs, he asks an aspiring smith to prove a sure hand with bronze before sharing his knowledge. Orokk Omosh works the anvils of Orgrimmar under the weight of his family's past. For twenty generations, the Omosh line has shaped ore into weapons and armor for the Horde. Orokk has no kin and cannot sire children, and he sees himself as a failure to that line. With the family craft at risk of ending, he sets bloodline pride aside and seeks an apprentice to carry its smithing traditions forward. Orokk will not share his secrets with an untested smith. He asks for two patterned bronze bracers, two bronze greatswords, and two sharp beast claws as proof of basic skill at the anvil. To him, blacksmithing is no idle luxury: its highest honor is armor and steel stained with enemy blood. Meeting his demands may persuade the old smith that the Omosh legacy can live on through an apprentice, and earn a chance to learn more of the craft.

quest:2753.text: Trampled Under Foot. In Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor, Orokk Omosh puts smiths through an advanced blacksmithing trial. Forging green iron armor tests their endurance and teaches them to make heavy iron boots, with the Omosh bloodline's secret techniques at stake. Orokk Omosh trains armorsmiths in Orgrimmar through hard physical trials. He sees metalworking as more than heating ore and shaping it; the work honors his ancestral clan and tests a smith's endurance. This is the third trial in his chain, and repeated crafting of tempered green iron armor is meant to build muscle and discipline. Smiths who bring Orokk the requested green iron gear earn rare praise from the gruff armorsmith. He compares an artisan who endures the work to his grandfather, Chief Gorokk of Omosh. In exchange for the armor, Orokk teaches the ancestral design for sturdy iron boots, made so Horde warriors can crush their enemies beneath their heels.

quest:2755.text: Joys of Omosh. After an adventurer's great help, Orokk Omosh shares a family tradition in Orgrimmar. The veteran blacksmith brushes off his tears as soot, then performs the Omosh dance of joy to pass down an unusual piece of family heritage. Near Orgrimmar's scorching forge, Orokk Omosh is known for heavy hammer blows, not tears. The burly blacksmith has received great help from you, and the kindness overwhelms him. He stubbornly blames a stray bit of soot in his eye rather than admit he is weeping. Before you part, Orokk says he must share one last secret of the Omosh family. He performs the vigorous, exhausting Omosh dance of joy for his apprentice, then teaches the apprentice to strike with an iron fist.

quest:278.text: A Dark Threat Looms. The Stonewrought Dam faces a suspected Dark Iron plot, and Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII needs rare reagents from Loch Modan. You gather them so he can make a mixture to defuse explosives beneath the dam. Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII needs a strange mixture to stop Dark Iron explosives. It takes Forest Lurker venom, a tear from a crocolisk in the Loch, and a Mo'grosh crystal. Together, these reagents can render the dwarven charges inert. You search Loch Modan's dangerous reaches for the ingredients. Forest Lurker spiders and crocolisks pose natural hazards, while Mo'grosh crystals lie in the ogres' stronghold in the northeastern hills. The ogres guard their mined crystals jealously, so reaching one means facing their encampments.

quest:280.text: A Dark Threat Looms. In Loch Modan, Dark Iron saboteurs threaten the Stonewrought Dam. Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII needs the charge disarmed before the loch floods the lowlands. Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII saw Dark Iron Insurgents swim toward the base of the Stonewrought Dam with a keg of explosive Seaforium. No Mountaineers were nearby to stop them, and the infiltrators fastened the keg against the dam’s underwater foundation. If the dam breaks, the loch will pour into the lowlands, flooding the region and crippling dwarven trade and travel.

quest:282.text: Senir's Observations. Grelin Whitebeard sends you east from Coldridge Valley with his report for Senir Whitebeard in Kharanos. The tunnel out is overrun by troggs, and Mountaineer Thalos guards the way. Grelin Whitebeard has documented troll activity around Coldridge Valley. After Frostmane trolls stole his journal and it was recovered, he decided the report was too important for an inexperienced apprentice to carry. He sends you directly to his brother, Senir Whitebeard, who works outside the valley in Kharanos. The eastern tunnel is the road from Coldridge Valley to the rest of Dun Morogh, but troggs have overrun it. Mountaineer Thalos stands outside the passage to keep civilians from entering danger. He lets travelers through only when they carry urgent official business.

quest:287.text: Frostmane Hold. In the peaks above Iceflow Lake, Frostmane trolls guard their cavern stronghold. Senir Whitebeard, stationed in Kharanos, sends scouts inside to kill headhunters and bring back intelligence for his reports. Senir Whitebeard tracks the Frostmane threat across Dun Morogh from Kharanos. The mountaineer and scout followed the aggressive tribes to their main cavern southwest of Brewnall Village, but armed trolls crowd its entrance. Senir is falling severely behind on his official reports, and he will not enter alone. He hires passing adventurers to scout the icy cavern in his place. Carved into the western peaks above Iceflow Lake, the stronghold is a freezing refuge packed with hostile ice trolls. Scouts must fight through its underground tunnels, kill the Frostmane Headhunters stationed along the ledges, and map the interior. The survivors' findings give Senir the intelligence he needs to complete his report for Ironforge's military commanders.

quest:291.text: The Reports. Senir Whitebeard sends an urgent report from Kharanos to Senator Barin Redstone in Ironforge. He warns that the senator is sour and asks you to keep the scout who gathered the information unnamed. Senir Whitebeard needs you to carry an urgent report from Kharanos to Senator Barin Redstone in Ironforge. The mountaineer’s account details the growing Frostmane troll threat facing Dun Morogh, drawn from reconnaissance deep inside Frostmane Hold. Senir asks you not to mention who helped gather the information from the snowy crags.

quest:2948.text: Gnome Improvement. In Ironforge, Talvash del Kissel hopes to restore his craft with a ring from Gnomeregan. He offers to improve the old band for an adventurer who brings silver and moss agate. Talvash del Kissel fled Gnomeregan after troggs brought the city down and radiation followed. He now lives in Ironforge's Mystic Ward, short on coin and materials. The gnome jeweler and tinkerer is determined to prove his skills remain sharp, even in exile. Talvash recognizes the ring he once made in Gnomeregan, now cleaned by the Sparklematic 5200. Rather than send the adventurer away with a plain band, he offers to improve it. Silver and moss agate, worked into a delicate lattice, turn the old ring into a finer piece.

quest:2950.text: Nogg's Ring Redo. In Orgrimmar, Nogg works to improve a ring recovered from Gnomeregan. He asks for rare materials and information about Dark Iron dwarves, eager to prove goblin craft superior to gnomish design. You bring a cleaned gold ring from Gnomeregan to Nogg's workshop in the Valley of Honor. The goblin engineer takes one look at its modest gnomish craft and offers a bargain. Bring raw materials and a modest fee, and he will add an intricate lattice of silver and moss agate to the band, meant to amplify the magic within it.

quest:298.text: Excavation Progress Report. In Loch Modan, Ironband sends an excavation report to Thelsamar. Prospector Ironband asks you to carry his latest dispatches and renewed explosive supply orders to Jern Hornhelm. Prospector Ironband's dig in Loch Modan depends on supplies from nearby settlements. Excavation takes picks, workers, and plenty of blasting powder to break through bedrock. Ironband sends runners with regular reports and supply requests to Jern Hornhelm, his local contact in Thelsamar.

quest:2997.text: Tome of Divinity. In Dun Morogh, Azar Stronghammer calls young dwarven paladins away from their field duties and sends them to Ironforge. He directs each initiate to Tiza Battleforge in the Hall of Mysteries for guidance, beginning deeper trials in service to the Holy Light. Dwarven initiates begin by guarding Dun Morogh's snowbound villages and roads. When Azar Stronghammer sees that a defender is ready for deeper spiritual instruction, he sends the promising candidate from field duties to Ironforge. There, the initiate can seek guidance from the city's holy elders. The summons leads you to the Mystic Ward, then up to the Hall of Mysteries. Tiza Battleforge waits there, upstairs among sacred relics and solemn study. A respected dwarven champion of the Light, she tests whether you are ready for self-sacrifice, mercy, and the moral duties of your calling.

quest:2998.text: Tome of Divinity. A summons bearing the Tome of Divinity calls promising paladins from Elwynn to Stormwind. Answering Brother Wilhelm's call begins the sacred trials needed to master resurrection through the Holy Light. Novice paladins in Elwynn Forest spend their early days helping locals and testing their strength against wolves, Defias bandits, and kobolds. When an initiate shows martial discipline and devotion to the Holy Light, mentors such as Brother Wilhelm send a personal summons. Leaders of the paladins take note of promising students and direct them to leave the local chapels behind and report straight to the kingdom's spiritual heart. In Cathedral Square, Stormwind's Cathedral of Light is the supreme sanctuary of the kingdom's priesthood and the Knights of the Silver Hand. Duthorian Rall resides there and oversees those sworn to the Order. Beneath its soaring vaulted ceilings, high-ranking paladins set formal trials from the Tome of Divinity before each initiate. The challenges test compassion, fortitude, and a willingness to sacrifice.

quest:2999.text: Tome of Divinity. In Ironforge, young dwarven paladins begin a rite of passage beyond basic martial training. Brandur Ironhammer sends them upstairs in the Hall of Mysteries to seek Tiza Battleforge and take up the deeper duties and sacred vows of the Holy Light. Young paladins first defend Anvilmar and Kharanos from troggs and frost trolls. When their martial discipline is proven, Brandur Ironhammer, their paladin trainer in Ironforge's Hall of Mysteries, sends them upstairs for guidance. Senior paladins there prepare initiates for the order's spiritual duties. Tiza Battleforge is a revered paladin among Ironforge's dwarves. She teaches initiates the burdens of the Light beyond swordplay and hammer blows: compassion, justice, and self-sacrifice. Seeking her begins formal study of the Tome of Divinity, a sacred path toward the power to resurrect the fallen.

quest:3000.text: Tome of Divinity. In Stormwind, Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker sends dwarf paladins back to Ironforge. There, Tiza Battleforge guides them toward the sacred trials of the Tome of Divinity. Dwarf paladins often aid Stormwind and travel through human lands, but their spiritual and martial roots lie in Khaz Modan. When Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker judges that a dwarf has gained enough field training, he sends them to Ironforge. Their own people there guide the spiritual duties expected of a full Knight of the Silver Hand. In Ironforge, you are directed to the Mystic Ward and the Hall of Mysteries. Tiza Battleforge waits on its upper level, where she mentors young dwarven paladins. She prepares them to bear the burden of the Holy Light through sacred trials recorded in the Tome of Divinity.

quest:301.text: Report to Ironforge. Ironband’s report is bound for Ironforge from Thelsamar in Loch Modan. It carries news from the excavation site to Prospector Stormpike in the Assembly of Explorers, where the stalled dig and missing blastpowder need attention. The Explorers' League funds, supplies, and oversees archaeological expeditions across Khaz Modan. Prospector Ironband's dig in southern Loch Modan has run short of blasting supplies, and its overseers cannot simply requisition more nearby. At the Thelsamar inn, Jern Hornhelm entrusts you with Ironband's written report. You carry it over the mountain passes to Prospector Stormpike at the League's headquarters in Ironforge.

quest:302.text: Powder to Ironband. A shipment of blasting powder is bound for Prospector Ironband's dig in southern Loch Modan. After Prospector Stormpike approves the request in Ironforge, the powder is sent to Thelsamar for the journey to Ironband's Excavation. The Explorer's League sends blasting powder from Ironforge to Prospector Ironband's expedition in southern Loch Modan. When the dig runs short, word reaches the League's leadership. Prospector Stormpike approves the request and directs the runner to coordinate with Jern Hornhelm in Thelsamar, the valley's main supply hub.

quest:3065.text: Simple Tablet. In the Valley of Trials, a marked parchment sends you to Frang after you prove yourself against local beasts. The warrior trainer waits outside the Den. After you prove you can face the Mottled Boars, Gornek hands you a parchment marked specifically for you. Durotar is harsh, and the Horde quickly gives its fighters guidance. The parchment directs you to Frang, the veteran warrior trainer outside the Den. Frang shelters in the shade outside the Den and watches recruits arrive from the red scrubland. With a seasoned eye, he judges each new arrival before teaching the fundamentals, whether with a heavy axe or a spear. He prepares each recruit to defend the young Horde's fragile settlements.

quest:307.text: Filthy Paws. Mountaineer Stormpike needs the Filthy Paws supplies back from Silver Stream Mine. The Miners' League stored equipment there after the ore ran dry, but kobolds have overrun the tunnels. Stormpike wants the tools recovered before his warriors attack. Silver Stream Mine lies in the hills of northern Loch Modan, east of Algaz Station. Its last silver veins ran dry long ago. The dwarven Miners' League turned the empty shafts into a depot for spare excavation gear, picks, and staging materials. Across Khaz Modan, sturdy tunnels make good storehouses, as long as they stay guarded and locked against the wilderness. Kobolds have slipped into the mine as dwarven vigilance across Loch Modan has thinned. The dark shafts and gleaming iron tools drew the scavengers, and they soon made the depot their warren. Mountaineer Stormpike is ready to lead warriors in and drive them out, but their heavy boots and sweeping blows could smash the crates. You can slip or fight your way inside to recover the League's supplies before the assault begins.

quest:308.text: Distracting Jarven. Jarven Thunderbrew watches the cellar stores at Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. Forbidden to touch the barrels, he asks a passing traveler to bring him a mug of Thunder Ale from upstairs, hoping it will sharpen his wits on duty. In Kharanos, Jarven Thunderbrew keeps watch over the deep stores of Thunderbrew Distillery. His family forbids him to drink from the stock while on guard, though the finest stout in Dun Morogh surrounds him. The temptation wins out, and he asks passing travelers to fetch a pint of potent Thunder Ale from the taps upstairs. Jarven says a good drink will hone his senses and strengthen his watch. Whether a guard should drink on duty remains an open question. Few hardy dwarves in Dun Morogh can fault a Thunderbrew for wanting a taste of the brew made by his own kin.

quest:3082.text: Etched Tablet. Gornek sends a carved tablet to hunters in the Valley of Trials. It bears Jen'shan's mark and calls them to begin training in the wilderness. Gornek brings novice hunters a carved tablet after they prove themselves against the boars near the Den. The stone bears Jen'shan's mark. She is a skilled troll huntswoman stationed nearby, and the message shows that seasoned hunters have noticed the young recruit's grit. The lesson now moves beyond surviving the local dangers and toward disciplined training in the wild. Jen'shan teaches that orcs and trolls have a long history within the Horde. Orcs brought renowned traditions of warriors and shamans, while the Darkspear trolls carried ancient skills in stalking, tracking, and survival. Those skills helped the orcs endure life on Azeroth. As Jen'shan trains new hunters, the two peoples continue to share what they know, bound by respect for the hunt.

quest:3083.text: Encrypted Tablet. In the Valley of Trials, Gornek gives a coded summons to aspiring rogues. It sends them to Rwag in the Den, where rogue instruction meets the Shattered Hand. Gornek gives an Encrypted Tablet to each initiate who proves their mettle against the local wildlife. Its message is written in cipher, a fitting test and precaution for those trained in stealth, poison, and subterfuge. The summons directs the recruit into the Den to meet Rwag, who trains the Horde’s rogues, thieves, and cutpurses. Inside the Den, initiates find Rwag, an agent aligned with the Shattered Hand. He tells new rogues the guild will not dictate their every breath, but the Hand holds him accountable if an apprentice fails to perform. The fledgling Horde is surrounded by foes and relies heavily on silent scouts and agile cutpurses to gather intelligence and eliminate threats from the shadows.

quest:3084.text: Rune-Inscribed Tablet. In the Valley of Trials, new shamans receive a summons from Shikrik. It calls promising initiates to formal training in the spirits and the elements: earth, fire, water, and air. Gornek gives fledgling shamans a carved stone tablet after they prove their early discipline in the dusty training grounds of the Valley of Trials. Its runes carry an invitation from Shikrik, the local shaman trainer. The summons tells each initiate they are ready to look beyond physical combat and heed the deeper currents of the natural world. Shamanism holds a sacred place in the revitalized Horde. Shikrik teaches that shamans draw power from the four elements and strength from ancestral spirits. They follow Warchief Thrall's example as spiritual guides and sources of wisdom for their communities. Across Durotar, they protect the settlements taking root.

quest:3085.text: Hallowed Tablet. In the Valley of Trials, a message from Ken'jai reaches young priests after their first test. The tablet calls them to learn how Darkspear priests commune with the spirits. After you prove yourself against the boars under Gornek's watch, he gives you an inscribed stone called the Hallowed Tablet. Its message bears Ken'jai's mark. The Darkspear mystic waits outside the Den, where he watches over newcomers drawn to faith and spiritual magic. Darkspear priests among the Horde seek communion with spirits and loa, unlike human and dwarven priests who follow the Holy Light across the sea. Ken'jai welcomes you to Durotar and teaches that your power grows through spiritual discipline. He will instruct you in greater rites as your bond with the spirits matures.

quest:3086.text: Glyphic Tablet. In the Valley of Trials, a Glyphic Tablet sends young Horde mages to Mai'ah. Gornek passes it to them after they prove their strength, and the troll trainer waits outside the Den. You have proved your strength against the Valley of Trials' wildlife, and Gornek gives you an inscribed tablet. Mai'ah, the valley's mage trainer, sent it. She asks you to find her by the Den's entrance when you are ready to begin your arcane studies. Mai'ah speaks plainly about the power mages wield and the danger that comes with it. She warns that their greatest threat is magic's unseen pull toward corruption, not rival warriors or enemy races. Humility and patience matter, she says, because unchecked sorcery can make a mage believe they have mastered more than they have.

quest:3087.text: Etched Parchment. In the Valley of Trials, Etched Parchment calls a young hunter to Jen'shan. Gornek delivers it after the initiate's first blooding, opening the way to wilderness training in Durotar. After proving themselves against mottled boars, hunters in the Valley of Trials receive an etched parchment from Gornek. Jen'shan, a skilled Darkspear hunter, sent the note after watching new arrivals from the edges of the encampment. It welcomes the initiate to formal training and recognizes the instincts needed to master Durotar's untamed beasts and harsh land. Reporting to Jen'shan marks the move from recruit to dedicated stalker. She warns that hunting is no easier than the arcane arts or ancestral shamanism. Mastering Durotar's predators, maintaining ranged weapons, and surviving on unforgiving land all demand discipline. Jen'shan sends her apprentices to aid the valley's other inhabitants and test their abilities before returning to learn more advanced survival techniques.

quest:3088.text: Encrypted Parchment. In the Valley of Trials, Encrypted Parchment sends proven novice orc rogues into the Den. Its cipher points them to Rwag, an agent of the Shattered Hand. Gornek passes the coded parchment to novice orcs who have proved themselves against the local wildlife. Other trainers recruit pupils openly in the clearing, but rogue instructor Rwag sends his summons by cipher. The message directs you beyond the sunlit camp and deep into the cavern called the Den. Inside the Den, you find Rwag keeping watch among the rock. Warlocks lurk deeper in the cave, and he tells you he watches recruits for the Shattered Hand. While orcish society prizes open honor and glory in battle, the Shattered Hand works as the Horde's hidden network of spies, cutthroats, and gatherers of intelligence.

quest:3089.text: Rune-Inscribed Parchment. At the Valley of Trials, a rune-marked summons calls new shamans to Shikrik. Gornek delivers the parchment, which begins their formal training in communion with spirits and elements. After proving their survival skills against local wildlife, new orc shamans receive a rune-inscribed parchment from Gornek, overseer of the Valley of Trials. Its mystical writing comes from Shikrik, the valley's shaman trainer, who asks to meet the newly arrived initiate. Meeting Shikrik begins a shaman's sacred duty to the Horde. She teaches that shamans serve as conduits for ancestral spirits and wielders of elemental wrath. Under her guidance, new shamans learn to channel spiritual energies, mend wounds, and call upon Kalimdor's natural forces.

quest:309.text: Protecting the Shipment. In southern Loch Modan, Miran carries blasting powder toward Ironband's Excavation Site. Prospector Ironband needs it to keep his dig moving, but the road is dangerous. Prospector Ironband's dig in the hills of southern Loch Modan needs blasting powder to cut through stone. Supply lines have failed, and threats to the courier wagons leave Miran stranded on the road with a heavy load. You guide him along the uneven roads to the excavation site, where the powder can keep Ironband's work from stalling.

quest:3092.text: Etched Note. At Camp Narache, a summons calls a young tauren hunter to train with Lanka Farshot. The message marks the start of study in the ways of the wild. Grull Hawkwind passes the etched message to a young tauren with a gift for marksmanship and tracking. The novice has been training among the bluffs of Red Cloud Mesa. Lanka Farshot has taken notice of the youth's bloodline and raw ability, and calls them to study under his watch. Among the Shu'halo, hunters do more than scout or fight. They feed the tribes with their quarry, guard nomadic camps, and keep close to the beasts of Kalimdor. Lanka's training begins with weapons and the creatures of Mulgore. In time, the novice may learn the ancient art of taming wild companions.

quest:3094.text: Verdant Note. At Camp Narache, a summons calls promising young tauren to seek Gart Mistrunner. Grull Hawkwind delivers the message on Gart's behalf. On the Red Cloud Mesa, Grull Hawkwind gives young tauren a message from a messenger sent by Gart Mistrunner. The summons calls those showing natural gifts to take up their responsibilities. It invites them to enter the ancient practice of tauren druidism and turn from simple village errands toward the balance of the plains. Gart Mistrunner warns that ancestral and natural spirits have grown restless across Mulgore. Tauren druids act as living avatars of nature, keeping harmony with the Earthmother's will despite distant rivalries. Night elves practice druidic arts too, but Gart says their pride blinds them to the tauren's deep bond with the natural realm.

quest:3096.text: Encrypted Scroll. At Deathknell, a sealed message sends a newly awakened Forsaken rogue to David Trias. Shadow Priest Sarvis passes it on once the recruit has proved ready. Newly raised Forsaken fight mindless zombies in the cemetery as Deathknell's leaders watch for those drawn to stealth and subterfuge. Once you have proved your readiness, Shadow Priest Sarvis gives promising scouts a sealed parchment. David Trias's discreet seal marks it as an early link to the covert network beneath Forsaken leadership. David Trias watches Deathknell's crossroads and inn for prospects in future covert operations. The Forsaken need disciplined agents, not common thieves or reckless cutpurses, to serve their fledgling kingdom. Trias says capable rogues may draw the notice of the Shadowstalkers, a Forsaken cadre that prizes cunning, precision, and absolute loyalty to the Dark Lady.

quest:3097.text: Hallowed Scroll. In Deathknell, the Hallowed Scroll calls newly risen Forsaken priests to the chapel. Shadow Priest Sarvis gives the summons, sending each novice to Dark Cleric Duesten to learn how the Forsaken wield faith after death. Newly awakened undead stagger from Deathknell’s graves, their minds reeling from plague, death, and freedom from the Lich King's grip. For those who followed the Holy Light in life, death leaves deep confusion. As fledgling undead fight the mindless Scourge at the settlement’s edge, Shadow Priest Sarvis receives messages. A summons marked by Dark Cleric Duesten calls newly risen priests away from their wandering and into the desecrated town chapel. At the chapel, Dark Cleric Duesten teaches a harsh faith. He says the Holy Light abandoned the Forsaken in death, ancestral spirits are hollow tales, and demons have no care for their plight. Forsaken clergy teach that willpower and self-reliance are their only sources of salvation. Under Duesten’s guidance, newly risen priests learn to wield divine discipline and shadow through conviction in their own survival, not devotion to distant gods.

quest:3098.text: Glyphic Scroll. In Deathknell, Isabella summons newly awakened Forsaken mages to her in the ruined church. Her sealed scroll calls them to hone their volatile arcane powers. Isabella calls newly awakened Forsaken mages to the ruined church in Deathknell. After you show an affinity for arcane magic while fighting the mindless Scourge nearby, the scroll bearing her arcane sigil bids you to report to her. Isabella trains local mages, and she knows that untrained magic can endanger the Forsaken as much as their enemies. In Deathknell’s ruined chapel, Isabella teaches new Forsaken mages that undeath has not ended the dangers of arcane magic. Their bodies have lost the frailties of life, but magic remains volatile and corrupting. For the Forsaken, mastering the arcane is more than study. It can help them survive, seek vengeance, reclaim their destiny, and destroy those who threaten their fragile return to Lordaeron.

quest:31.text: Aquatic Form. In Thunder Bluff, a young Horde druid returns to master the waters. After proving worthy in Moonglade and attuning to the sea lion aspect, the druid comes home for formal recognition and Aquatic Form. Dendrite Starblaze sends the aspiring tauren druid back to Mulgore after the trials in Moonglade. The Pendant of the Sea Lion bears proof of balance and dedication through Kalimdor's waters. Carrying it shows the initiate has honored the ancient traditions needed to take an aquatic aspect. At Thunder Bluff's heights, the traveler presents the pendant to Turak Runetotem, their mentor. Pleased that the initiate has honored their ancestors and kept the balance of nature, Turak teaches the secret of the aquatic form. The druid can then move beneath rivers and oceans, breathe freely, and navigate the depths as a sea creature.

quest:310.text: Bitter Rivals. In Dun Morogh, the Barleybrews and Thunderbrews compete for renown. Marleth Barleybrew sends you to the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos to replace a cask of Thunder Ale with her family's brew. Ale stirs fierce pride in Khaz Modan. The Barleybrews have long resented the fame of the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. Marleth Barleybrew admits that Thunderbrew makes a respectable ale, but she cannot accept that it alone is renowned in Dun Morogh. She plans to shake up the local palate by replacing a cask of Thunder Ale with her own fiery Barleybrew Scalder. The plan takes you into the distillery cellar, beneath the kitchen in Kharanos. Aging casks wait in the basement storeroom, and a guard watches near the Thunderbrews' most prized reserve. You need to draw him away before secretly switching the barrels.

quest:3103.text: Hallowed Letter. The Hallowed Letter is a formal summons given to promising young priests by Marshal McBride on behalf of Northshire Abbey's resident trainer, Priestess Anetta. It marks the start of a fledgling priest's formal mentorship in the tenets of the Holy Light amidst a troubled and vulnerable world. After proving their mettle against the kobold camps around Northshire, novitiate priests are handed a missive bearing the sacred seal of Priestess Anetta. Delivered through Marshal McBride, the letter serves as an invitation to begin serious study of the Holy Light within the abbey's quiet halls. When presented with the letter, Priestess Anetta impresses upon her new pupil the grim state of the realm. Lingering threats from the Burning Legion cast long shadows across Azeroth, while the continents struggle with fresh wounds and unrest. In her eyes, taking up the mantle of a priest is not merely an academic devotion, but an urgent moral responsibility to bring healing and solace to a suffering world.

quest:3104.text: Glyphic Letter. A sealed summons reaches novice human mages in Northshire Valley, sent by Marshal McBride. Khelden Bremen calls promising spellcasters to Northshire Abbey to begin their arcane tutelage. Marshal McBride gives the rune-marked letter to an aspiring apprentice who has proved capable by helping him against local vermin. Khelden Bremen, Northshire's resident mage trainer, wrote it. He watches new recruits arriving at the abbey for signs of magical discipline and talent. Northshire Abbey has long been a sanctuary of the Holy Light, but Stormwind's dangers call for practitioners of every discipline. The letter brings you upstairs to Khelden Bremen. He offers no easy praise. Instead, he warns that mastering arcane power means defying natural limits, earning both profound respect and deep fear from ordinary folk.

quest:3105.text: Tainted Letter. At Northshire, Tainted Letter calls novice human warlocks away from the Abbey guards for instruction in the fel arts. Drusilla La Salle entrusts it to Marshal McBride, who delivers it to her recruits. Novice warlocks receive a letter from Marshal McBride after proving themselves against the kobold menace. While priests and paladins study openly in Northshire Abbey, warlocks must tread carefully. Drusilla La Salle's insignia marks the letter, which directs each fledgling spellcaster to her secluded post outside the abbey's main walls before taking on other duties. Drusilla warns that warlocks walk a precarious path under the watchful eyes of Stormwind's guards, whom she calls 'pathetic mundanes.' Drawing power from the Twisting Nether and communing with demons always risk corruption. She counsels patience, prudence, and firm self-control when handling those dark energies, but says caution must not extinguish a warlock's ambition.

quest:3106.text: Simple Rune. At Anvilmar, new dwarven warriors receive a call to begin their training. Sten Stoutarm carries it from Thran Khorman, the trainer inside the hall. Young recruits prove their grit around Coldridge Valley as they clear pests, while veteran scouts watch for promising fighters. Sten Stoutarm brings them an inscribed stone from Thran Khorman. The simple rune summons them from the snowy valley paths into Anvilmar's warm forge-hall, where they can pledge themselves to the warrior's trade. Thran Khorman speaks plainly about the troubles reshaping Dun Morogh. Gnomes displaced after catastrophic explosions destroyed Gnomeregan seek refuge, while some dwarves take up foreign arcane arts or follow the human faith in the Holy Light. Troggs, disturbed deep underground, claw at the mountain borders. Thran believes firm martial discipline is the bedrock needed to withstand these threats.

quest:3107.text: Consecrated Rune. At Anvilmar, a summons reaches fledgling dwarven paladins through Sten Stoutarm. Bromos Grummner calls them to join the Knights of the Silver Hand. Sten Stoutarm gives young paladins an inscribed rune and sends them to Bromos Grummner inside Anvilmar. Around Coldridge Valley, local leaders watch closely for those gifted in divine martial prowess. The summons marks a formal induction, where raw potential must meet discipline. The Knights of the Silver Hand began among the humans of Lordaeron, but Ironforge dwarves embraced the Holy Light with fierce devotion. Bromos Grummner welcomes new members and reminds them that dwarven paladins share the solemn duty of protecting Azeroth. The order is grounded in sacrifice, tradition, and martial virtue; recruits take up hammer and faith in equal measure.

quest:3108.text: Etched Rune. In Coldridge Valley, novice dwarf hunters receive a carved summons from Sten Stoutarm. It directs them to Thorgas Grimson inside Anvilmar for training in the hunt. As you help Sten Stoutarm face threats around Coldridge Valley, he gives you the Etched Rune. Dwarven mentors favor carved runes for formal messages, rather than spoken orders or plain parchment. The stone tells you to take stock of your early work and report indoors at Anvilmar for deeper instruction in the hunt. At Anvilmar, the Etched Rune marks a hunter's entry into formal discipline. Thorgas Grimson teaches that mountaineering and survival in Khaz Modan demand respect for the harsh land. Hunters learn to read tracks in bitter snowdrifts, care for their weapons and ammunition, and understand the wild beasts roaming the crags. The rune marks a hunter's first step from a lone wanderer with a gun to an apprentice among Anvilmar's veteran pathfinders.

quest:3109.text: Encrypted Rune. At Anvilmar, Solm Hargrin sends a coded message to young rogues in Coldridge Valley. Sten Stoutarm passes it to them, and the rune directs them indoors to meet their trainer. Sten Stoutarm gives the etched stone to rogues who help him in Coldridge Valley's snowy passes. He says someone slipped it to him for delivery and suspects Solm Hargrin sent it. The rune tests a novice's discretion and calls them inside, where Solm can meet them without announcing his need for scouts and scoundrels across the courtyard. Inside Anvilmar, Solm Hargrin welcomes the new rogues and offers to teach them the maneuvers, strikes, and subtle arts that keep them alive and earn them coin. He also reminds dwarf rogues to look after their displaced gnomish allies, who are still recovering from Gnomeregan's catastrophic fall.

quest:311.text: Return to Marleth. Marleth waits in Brewnall Village for the Thunder Ale brought from Kharanos. You return with proof that her Scalder reached the Thunderbrew cellar. Marleth Barleybrew of Brewnall Village wants proof that her Scalder was slipped into the Kharanos cellar, where the distillers make Thunder Ale. You bring back a barrel of their brew, taken from beneath their noses. The prize proves the switch succeeded and gives Marleth a trophy from her rival. You haul the heavy keg over the snowy ridges to Brewnall Village, where Marleth is thrilled by the caper. She delights in having outsmarted Kharanos's guards and cellar masters. The stunt puts the fierce pride dwarven families take in their signature recipes on display across Dun Morogh.

quest:3110.text: Hallowed Rune. In Coldridge Valley, Hallowed Rune brings a young dwarf priest to Anvilmar. Sten Stoutarm carries Branstock Khalder’s inscribed prayers and guidance to the novice, who is summoned inside to deepen their bond with the Holy Light. A young priest earns Sten Stoutarm’s notice while helping clear threats outside Anvilmar. Branstock Khalder, the settlement’s spiritual guide, gives Sten a rune inscribed with prayers and guidance for the novice. The young priest is called inside Anvilmar’s sturdy halls to begin sacred studies. Dwarven life prizes martial strength and heavy plate, yet the Holy Light remains central to Ironforge society. In Coldridge Valley, holy casters stand with warriors and hunters to protect the enclave from trogg incursions and dangerous wildlife moving through the snow.

quest:3112.text: Simple Memorandum. In Coldridge Valley, a message calls new gnome warriors to Anvilmar. Sten Stoutarm passes along Thran Khorman’s summons, inviting trained fighters to learn the arts of war and prepare to reclaim Gnomeregan. As you help Sten Stoutarm drive off troggs and boars in Coldridge Valley, he receives a short message for a young gnome warrior. Thran Khorman, a veteran trainer in Anvilmar, sees promise in the refugee fighter. He calls the newcomer to the central hall to begin martial instruction. Dwarven trainers may tease gnome warriors about their size, but Thran Khorman takes their loss seriously. He asks them to imagine how dwarves would feel if Ironforge fell to the Dark Irons. Thran has pledged to help the exiled gnomes, and he will teach them the arts of war until they are ready to reclaim their home.

quest:3113.text: Encrypted Memorandum. In Coldridge Valley, a folded note reaches new gnome rogues through Sten Stoutarm. It directs them to Solm Hargrin inside Anvilmar. As you help the mountaineers face trogg threats in Coldridge Valley, Sten Stoutarm gives you a folded piece of parchment. It was passed to him in confidence and made to look like an official memorandum. The note invites you to meet Solm Hargrin, the rogue trainer inside Anvilmar. Gnomeregan's sudden fall has left its gnome survivors far from home, sharing close quarters with their dwarven hosts in Dun Morogh. Solm Hargrin knows that rogues draw suspicion when items vanish. He calls for quiet solidarity among those who practice the craft, so they can help one another endure.

quest:3114.text: Glyphic Memorandum. In Coldridge Valley, a memorandum calls novice mages to Anvilmar. Mountaineer Sten Stoutarm passes it to new arrivals, who are invited to meet its author, Marryk Nurribit, and begin their spellcraft studies. Mountaineer Sten Stoutarm has a memorandum for the new mages he assists in Coldridge Valley. He hands it to you and advises you to read it, then go inside Anvilmar to meet the gnome who wrote it. Inside Anvilmar, gnome mage trainer Marryk Nurribit gives newcomers plain advice before teaching them. Stay out of serious trouble, save coin for training and tavern drinks, and keep clear of fallen Gnomeregan and its radioactive danger. Marryk is ready to teach you the arcane arts.

quest:3115.text: Tainted Memorandum. A quiet message draws a young gnome warlock toward the shadows of Anvilmar. Sten Stoutarm passes it along, and Alamar Grimm calls the neophyte to learn dark power and rely on it rather than their dwarven hosts. In Coldridge Valley, the dark arts meet deep suspicion. While you help Sten Stoutarm deal with local threats, he slips you a note. His reluctance shows the uneasy truce that lets warlocks practice in Alliance lands. He warns you to watch yourself because your kind is not trusted around these parts. Inside Anvilmar, Alamar Grimm speaks plainly about the gnomes' plight. He believes conventional tinkering and ordinary magic failed Gnomeregan, bringing their people near extinction and leaving them as second-class refugees dependent on dwarven goodwill. He urges you to rely neither on the Holy Light nor on dwarven politics. Instead, he teaches you to summon and master fiends, whose obedience is unconditional.

quest:3116.text: Simple Sigil. In Shadowglen, Alyissia calls young night elf warriors to defend their people. Conservator Ilthalaine carries her summons as the Kaldorei face changes across Teldrassil and beyond. After you prove your basic survival skills against Shadowglen's restless wildlife, Conservator Ilthalaine gives you an inscribed sigil. The token formally marks your move into combat training. It carries a request from Alyissia, the warrior trainer at Aldrassil, asking you to dedicate your strength to defending your people. Alyissia sets your training against a time of rapid change and danger. In only a few years, the night elves have raised the World Tree Teldrassil, seen a taint spread through forest beasts near and far, and reconnected with ancient lands once thought lost, including Feralas. The Kaldorei need capable defenders against these perils. Alyissia prepares young Kaldorei for more than combat. She urges you not to judge outsiders who arrive on Teldrassil by their race. Some travelers may not act from pure generosity, but allies are vital to the Kaldorei's defense. As you take up the work of protecting your people, she asks you to offer them reasonable trust.

quest:3117.text: Etched Sigil. In Shadowglen, the Etched Sigil calls young night elf hunters to Aldrassil. Through Conservator Ilthalaine, Ayanna Everstride summons them to meet their trainer and begin learning archery and beastcraft. After young kaldorei hunters help defend Shadowglen, Conservator Ilthalaine gives them an inscribed token. A messenger brought it from their mentor, Ayanna Everstride. The sigil directs each novice up into Aldrassil’s high boughs, where the trainers watch over the canopy. Meeting Ayanna begins a hunter’s training on Teldrassil. She teaches novices marksmanship and how to understand Kalimdor’s wild creatures. A hunter must respect their beast companions and meet the world’s unseen dangers with awareness and humility.

quest:3118.text: Encrypted Sigil. In Shadowglen, a coded summons calls new night elf rogues to begin their training. Conservator Ilthalaine carries it for Frahun Shadewhisper, who also warns of the fragile peace across Kalimdor. While young night elves study nature's balance under Conservator Ilthalaine, those drawn to stealth receive a quieter summons. A runner brings the Encrypted Sigil from Frahun Shadewhisper, Shadowglen's rogue mentor. Its ciphers are meant for initiates of the trade. The bearer is to decipher the message and find Frahun near the roots of Aldrassil to begin instruction. Frahun's message also warns of Kalimdor's uncertain peace. The Third War has ended, but the truce between the Alliance and the emerging Horde remains fragile. Rogue scouts and informers in Shadowglen are urged to sharpen their eyes and ears early. They watch for threats and covert provocations that could renew war across the borders.

quest:3119.text: Hallowed Sigil. In Shadowglen, young night elf priests are called to begin their training in Aldrassil. Conservator Ilthalaine passes along Shanda's message as novices learn to wield Elune's grace. Night elf priests serve Elune as handmaidens and servants of the moon goddess. When a young kaldorei in Shadowglen shows devotion and an affinity for the divine light, Conservator Ilthalaine gives them a hallowed sigil. Shanda, the priest trainer, sent the token by messenger as an invitation to come to Aldrassil and begin spiritual training. Shanda tells the young acolyte that unusual change has reached Teldrassil's sheltered sanctuary. Travelers fill the World Tree's boughs, including members of the wider Alliance who have leave to meet with the kaldorei. The wider world calls, but Shanda urges novices to first attend to the troubles facing Shadowglen before turning to conflicts beyond it.

quest:312.text: Tundra MacGrann's Stolen Stash. In Dun Morogh, Tundra MacGrann needs his winter stores back from Old Icebeard. The injured hunter cannot reach the yeti's cave himself. Tundra MacGrann had salted away a month's worth of dried meat for the cold season. He lives beyond the warmth of Kharanos and Ironforge, where surviving winter takes careful preparation. To keep hungry bears from his provisions, he locked them in a thorium-reinforced meat chest. Old Icebeard carried the whole chest away rather than trying to open it. Old Icebeard stole the chest while MacGrann was away hunting deer and dragged it to a cave in the jagged hills. MacGrann believes the yeti cannot break through solid thorium, but his injured leg keeps him from retrieving the stores. Anyone entering the cave must face the beast or slip inside while it prowls the snowdrifts.

quest:3120.text: Verdant Sigil. A summons reaches newly awakened night elf druids in Shadowglen. Conservator Ilthalaine passes the Verdant Sigil to fledgling shapeshifters, directing them to Mardant Strongoak within Aldrassil. The token marks the start of their formal training in nature and the Emerald Dream. When a young night elf shows promise in keeping Shadowglen's balance, the order calls for a formal introduction. A runner brings the Verdant Sigil to Conservator Ilthalaine, who entrusts it to the initiate. The token shows that the circle in Aldrassil has taken notice and invites the young druid to begin formal training. Presenting the sigil to Mardant Strongoak inside Aldrassil brings the initiate into the fold. Deeper communion with the Emerald Dream and mastery of animal forms lie ahead. For now, Mardant becomes their first guide, teaching them to read nature's spirits and channel the raw power of the woods.

quest:313.text: The Grizzled Den. In Dun Morogh, Pilot Stonegear tests a recruit's grit in the Grizzled Den. From Steelgrill's Depot near Kharanos, he sends them west to hunt wendigos for thick pelts to warm his siege engine, Trollplow. Pilot Stonegear, stationed at Steelgrill's Depot near Kharanos, claims to have the nerves and constitution needed to operate a massive dwarven siege tank in freezing mountain air. He makes newcomers prove they share his grit. The test sends them into the frozen hills to face the native beasts. Pilot Stonegear's siege engine bears the name Trollplow, and its iron-plated cabin is cramped and cold in Dun Morogh's bitter climate. He seeks a practical remedy in wendigo pelt. Thick manes from the ferocious wendigos of the Grizzled Den can make a warm, durable rug for Trollplow's deck, while helping keep the local beasts in check.

quest:314.text: Protecting the Herd. At Amberstill Ranch in Dun Morogh, Rudra Amberstill faces the loss of mountain rams to Vagash. With Ironforge's forces spread thin, the breeders need passing fighters to defend their herd. Vagash has taken two mountain rams from Amberstill Ranch. The ranch supplies the Bronzebeard dwarves with riding and working beasts, and the herd matters to Dun Morogh's rustic economy. The savage predator prowls the crags above the ranch, hunting local livestock. Ironforge's forces are spread thin across the realm, supporting the Alliance on distant frontiers. With no military patrol on the ridgelines, Rudra Amberstill asks independent fighters to hunt Vagash and bring back one of the beast's deadly fangs as proof.

quest:317.text: Stocking Jetsteam. At Steelgrill's Depot, Pilot Bellowfiz prepares Jetsteam for a long deployment with the Ironforge Siege Brigade. The crew needs boar meat and bear pelts for the journey. Pilot Bellowfiz prepares Jetsteam at Steelgrill's Depot, just outside Kharanos. The siege tank is bound for a long operation with the Siege Brigade. Master engineer Beldin Steelgrill is tuning its mechanisms, while the crew needs a month's provisions for Dun Morogh's sub-zero cold. Beldin Steelgrill is occupied beneath Jetsteam's hood, leaving Bellowfiz unable to leave the vehicle to gather food and insulation. Snowy plains south of the Grizzled Den hold boars and bears. Their meat can feed the crew, and their pelts can line the tank's bedding.

quest:318.text: Evershine. At Steelgrill's Depot near Kharanos, Pilot Bellowfiz needs a potent brew from Brewnall Village. Rejold Barleybrew's Evershine can warm a traveler or fuel Bellowfiz's siege engine. Rejold Barleybrew brews Evershine in Brewnall Village, where his experiments push past ordinary dwarven brewing. The drink is strong enough to knock all but the hardiest dwarves flat. In Dun Morogh's bitter cold, its heat makes it prized despite its force. Pilot Bellowfiz works from Steelgrill's Depot outside Kharanos, where Evershine serves two purposes. A nip helps him endure the freezing winds, and the volatile alcohol can fuel his siege engine, Jetsteam. Poured into its furnace, the brew gives the engine an explosive surge of emergency power when Bellowfiz is in a tight spot.

quest:319.text: A Favor for Evershine. Pilot Bellowfiz needs Evershine from Brewnall Village for his siege engine at Steelgrill's Depot. Brewer Rejold Barleybrew will part with a cask only after the predators near the village are driven off. Rejold Barleybrew has the cask of Evershine Pilot Bellowfiz needs, but he will not give away his prized brew. Instead of asking for coin, Rejold asks you to thin the wild beasts of western Dun Morogh. Ice Claw Bears, Elder Crag Boars, and Snow Leopards roam close to Brewnall Village, bringing danger to the locals. Rejold insists that no self-respecting dwarf cowers before wild animals. Still, dealing with predators around the village takes valuable hours. With the beasts thinned, the villagers can focus on distilling and smithing without keeping watch on the tree line.

quest:3221.text: Speak with Renferrel. At the Sepulcher, Apothecary Renferrel needs to discuss the tainted wolf hearts. High Executor Hadrec sends you back to the Royal Apothecary Society researcher with your findings. After you help the Deathstalkers across Silverpine Forest, High Executor Hadrec gives you an urgent message from Apothecary Renferrel. Renferrel has studied the discolored wolf hearts gathered from local wildlife and needs you at once. Apothecary Renferrel works for the Royal Apothecary Society in a laboratory inside the Sepulcher crypt. He studies how dark magic and disease are changing Silverpine's beasts, bringing alchemical research together with military reports from the front.

quest:3261.text: Jorn Skyseer. In the southern Barrens, seasoned Horde hunters seek guidance from Jorn Skyseer. After you hunt local raptors for Sergra Darkthorn, she sends you south to Camp Taurajo, where an elder tracker offers deeper lessons. You have hunted the cunning sunscale and scytheclaw raptors stalking the northern savannah, earning Sergra Darkthorn's respect at the Crossroads. She knows martial skill must be joined with understanding of the land's great beasts. With her mentorship complete, she sends you south. Follow the Gold Road south through increasingly rugged plains to Camp Taurajo, a vital tauren settlement near the southern wilds. Jorn Skyseer waits there, an elder tracker ready to teach hunters how to pursue elusive, legendary quarry across the Barrens.

quest:3281.text: Stolen Silver. Gazrog at the Crossroads sends you after payroll silver stolen by raptors. Rumors of their cunning lead you south of Ratchet, into the Raptor Grounds. The garrison needs its wages back. Gazrog needs the Crossroads guards paid, and the raptors have taken their wages. You are sent to recover the stolen coin, not simply punish the beasts. When raptors ambushed the payroll shipment, Gazrog first sought vengeance. But killing the pack would not restore the missing money. The Horde must learn how the raptors carried off heavy crates of coin, and where they took them. Scouts found a raptor nest between two craggy peaks, south of Ratchet and northwest of Northwatch Hold. The creatures dragged the intact lockbox into their territory, where they guard it alongside eggs and fresh kills. Tales of raptor cunning and hoarding now seem true to Gazrog. Ordinary beasts rarely stash metallic valuables.

quest:33.text: Wolves Across the Border. Eagan Peltskinner asks you to hunt wolves prowling Northshire Valley and bring him their meat. He waits outside Northshire Abbey, where the valley’s needs continue despite the guards’ focus on Defias bandits. Eagan Peltskinner waits by Northshire Abbey’s walls with a grudge against the local timber wolves. Marshal McBride and the Stormwind guards have limited strength to defend the abbey from Defias bandits, while tradesfolk still have daily needs. Eagan asks you to thin the wolves’ numbers and bring back their tough meat for his cooking. Wolves roam closer to Northshire Abbey as patrols weaken. The Kingdom of Stormwind has too few troops and is strained by missing leadership. Young wolves and timber wolves now prowl the abbey’s paths and orchards. Hunting them supplies Eagan’s pantry and makes nearby trails safer for novitiates, laborers, and newly arrived defenders.

quest:3301.text: Mura Runetotem. You carry a snapjaw shell from the Barrens across the sea to Mura Runetotem in Silverpine Forest. Its strange vitality may help the tauren healer aid the Forsaken. Tonga Runetotem notices something peculiar about altered snapjaws while investigating the magically changed wildlife around the Barrens oases. Their shells pulse with resilient energy despite their corruption. He asks you to carry one across the Great Sea to his clanmate, Mura Runetotem, who is stationed in the Eastern Kingdoms. Mura Runetotem is at the Sepulcher, a Forsaken outpost in Silverpine Forest. She made the arduous journey there to help the Horde's newest allies cleanse and renew their ailing, blighted woodland. Mura hopes the shell's inner glow and enduring spark of life will reveal ways to restore vitality to the northern continent.

quest:332.text: Wine Shop Advert. In Stormwind, Renato Gallina draws passersby to his family's wine shop. He offers a voucher for a free bottle of vintage wine from their canal-side storefront, a small sign of trade in the reconstructed capital. Everyday life in Stormwind revolves around brisk commerce. Renato Gallina walks the Trade District's cobbled streets, promoting Gallina Winery, the small shop he runs with his sister, Suzetta. He hands flyers to thirsty travelers and locals, each offering a free tasting. The Gallina family offers a bottle of their famous pinot noir. Follow the ticket to the winery entrance near the canals, where Suzetta Gallina hands over the bottle. The family hopes a taste of their signature wine will bring newcomers back.

quest:333.text: Harlan Needs a Resupply. Harlan Bagley, a Stormwind merchant, cannot keep sturdy clothes and armor in stock. As demand surges, he sends an urgent cloth order to Rema Schneider at the Canal Tailor and Fit Shop, unaware of the conflicts brewing beyond the city walls. Across Stormwind City, Harlan Bagley's shelves are emptying fast. Citizens and wandering adventurers are buying reinforced tunics, traveling clothes, and battle-ready armor. Harlan wonders if people are preparing for a harsh season or winter, but the rush has left his shop short of finished cloth. Harlan sends a runner across the city's waterways to Rema Schneider, a seamstress at the Canal Tailor and Fit Shop. She is glad of his trade, yet the sudden demand for protective clothing troubles her. Rumors of tension spread through the kingdom, and Rema wonders whether the House of Nobles is hiding talk of open war from ordinary people.

quest:334.text: Package for Thurman. In Stormwind City, Rema Schneider needs her son Thurman’s tailoring supplies at Larson Clothiers in the Mage Quarter. He left home without his shears and needles, and Rema asks you to carry them to his workshop. Rema Schneider worries that Thurman will fall behind in his tailoring work without his shears and needles. He left home in a rush, and his mother asks you to carry the tools across Stormwind’s canals to his workshop.

quest:3361.text: A Refugee's Quandary. Following the disastrous fall of Gnomeregan to troggs and radiation, displaced gnomes have fled into the snowy wilds of Dun Morogh. Outside Anvilmar, an engineer named Felix Whindlebolt lost his vital belongings and tools to Frostmane troll scavengers during the panicked evacuation. When subterranean troggs overran the high-tech city of Gnomeregan, High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque and his advisors authorized the release of radioactive gas in a desperate bid to eradicate the invaders. The gambit backfired catastrophically, slaying thousands of innocents, mutating survivors into mindless leper gnomes, and forcing the remaining populace into a frantic exodus across Dun Morogh. Fleeing engineers and tinkerers carried whatever prized tools and blueprints they could save. However, the icy mountain passes between Gnomeregan and Coldridge Valley are prowled by indigenous Frostmane trolls. As Felix Whindlebolt scrambled toward the sanctuary of Anvilmar, Frostmane raiders snatched his tool chest, lockbox, and bucket of bolts, carting them off to their camps southwest of town.

quest:3364.text: Scalding Mornbrew Delivery. Nori Pridedrift sends you across Coldridge Valley with hot mornbrew for Durnan Furcutter. The drink must reach Anvilmar before the mountain cold takes its heat. Nori Pridedrift has just sent a delivery to Grelin Whitebeard. Now he has no time to carry another fresh cup to Anvilmar before it freezes into slush. Rather than leave his customer waiting, Nori asks a swift traveler to brave the snow with the mornbrew. Durnan Furcutter waits inside Anvilmar's warm mountain hall and is particular about his refreshments. Chilled mornbrew will not do. A hot cup gives the weary dwarf a needed break from his duties, and Nori expects his favorite mug back in one piece.

quest:3365.text: Bring Back the Mug. Durnan Furcutter sends you back across Coldridge Valley with Nori Pridedrift's empty mug. Returning it brings the Mornbrew delivery to a close. Durnan Furcutter has finished warming himself with the Mornbrew you delivered across Dun Morogh's snowdrifts. Now he sends you back with the empty tankard. In the biting cold, dwarven hospitality depends on mutual respect, and good dishware must not be left behind. Your return to Coldridge Valley completes the delivery for Nori Pridedrift. Sturdy drinkware does not grow on trees, especially in the dwarven homeland's subzero crags. Bringing the empty vessel back in one piece shows that you can be trusted in the local community.

quest:3376.text: Break Sharptusk!. Brave Windfeather sends you east from Red Cloud Mesa to face the raids on Mulgore. Sharptusk Thornmantle leads the Bristleback quilboar in Brambleblade Ravine, and his death could strike a hard blow against their attacks. Red Cloud Mesa is home to young tauren learning the hunt and the ways of the Earth Mother. East of the mesa, Brambleblade Ravine lies in the hands of the Bristleback quilboar. They see the tauren as invaders taking sacred ground, and their skirmishes threaten the tribes trying to make a stable home in Mulgore. The Bristleback attacks on Red Cloud Mesa follow the command of Chief Sharptusk Thornmantle. Deep in Brambleblade Ravine, he directs his warriors and geomancers against the Shu'halo from a fortified makeshift village. Brave Windfeather knows the raids will continue while Sharptusk lives. She sends you into the ravine to kill him and bring back his severed head as proof. Brave Windfeather teaches that hunting an enemy who can hunt back tests more than skill. For young tauren and their allies, the hunt for Sharptusk demands courage, awareness, and discipline. His death brings justice for fallen kin and marks a hunter's readiness to travel across Mulgore's wider plains.

quest:35.text: Further Concerns. Marshal Dughan sends an Alliance courier east from Goldshire to check reports of danger. You cross Elwynn Forest to speak with Guard Thomas, who watches the river crossing toward Redridge. Rumors tell of hostile aquatic creatures creeping along Elwynn's riverbanks. Marshal Dughan commands the Goldshire garrison, where banditry and vermin already trouble the center of the forest. He will not dismiss the reports, but he cannot spare guards from town. Instead, he sends you east to consult Guard Thomas, the sentry at the bridge over the river toward Redridge. Guard Thomas has held the bridge outpost for more than a week and has seen what Goldshire's leaders only feared. Hostile, semi-intelligent murlocs have made camps along the waterways of eastern Elwynn. Stormwind's army is absent, while local garrisons protect town walls and supply lines. That leaves rural bridge posts like Thomas's isolated before the growing danger.

quest:3519.text: A Friend in Need. Iverron lies bitten and in danger in Shadowglen. The young night elf calls for Dirania Silvershine, whose help may save him from Githyiss the Vile's venom. Iverron lies weakened after a bite from Githyiss the Vile. He ignored warnings and went too near the webwood caverns, where the vicious spider struck. Dizziness and failing strength leave him unable to reach safety alone. Iverron sends passersby toward Aldrassil's central tree to find Dirania Silvershine. She looks out for him and knows the dangers of Shadowglen. His life may depend on her preparing an antidote before the venom proves fatal.

quest:3521.text: Iverron's Antidote. Iverron's Antidote is an urgent task in Shadowglen to save a poisoned night elf scout. By gathering wild mushrooms, lilies, and spider ichor, adventurers help Dirania Silvershine brew a remedy before the venom takes full hold. While scouting the boughs of Shadowglen, young Iverron fell victim to the poisonous fangs of the local Webwood spiders. Collapsed and dying, his survival depends entirely on the herbal knowledge of Dirania Silvershine at Aldrassil. With the youth fading fast, she must quickly prepare a specialized concoction to neutralize the aggressive venom coursing through his blood. Dirania's recipe relies on the restorative flora of Teldrassil balanced against the venom itself. Hyacinth mushrooms, favored by the thieving grell to the south, provide an earthy base, while delicate Moonpetal lilies gathered from tranquil forest pools offer purifying qualities. To finish the draft, a sample of Webwood ichor must be extracted directly from the spiders prowling near Shadowthread Cave to tailor the cure to their specific poison.

quest:3522.text: Iverron's Antidote. In Shadowglen, Iverron waits for medicine before its strength fades. Poisoned by Webwood spiders, the night elf scout depends on Dirania Silvershine's brew, which must reach him within five minutes. Dirania Silvershine brews the cure from fresh venom sacs, lily roots, and hyacinth fungi. The unstable mixture keeps its strength for only five minutes after it is distilled. Whoever carries the vial must sprint straight from the glade toward the northern heights without hesitation. Webwood spiders around Shadowglen's barrows and caves have poisoned Iverron. He admits he has a habit of stumbling into danger and often depends on Dirania's herbal skill to save him. Even after drinking the antidote, his recovery is fragile. The hostile spiders still guard his way home, and he remains wary of them.

quest:3524.text: Washed Ashore. Along Darkshore, Washed Ashore begins an inquiry into the many sea creatures dying on its shore. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde starts it in Auberdine for the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, where priestesses fear the strandings may be an ill omen. Darkshore has seen great sea creatures beach themselves from time to time, a tragic but occasional sight. Now the strandings come in growing numbers along the coast. The Priestesses of Elune in the Temple of the Moon see more than a natural oddity in these deaths. They fear the pattern may bring ill omens to northern Kalimdor. The Temple of the Moon sends scholar Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde to the port town of Auberdine to learn why the great beasts are coming ashore. She gathers biological samples to send by hippogryph to Darnassus for close examination. But Greymist murlocs swarm the carcasses in the surf, scavenging the remains and keeping researchers from the bones without armed protection.

quest:353.text: Stormpike's Delivery. Grimand Elmore sends travelers north with an axe for Mountaineer Gringer Stormpike. The road leads from Stormwind's Dwarven District to an Ironforge outpost in Loch Modan. Grimand Elmore has been asked to make a weapon for Mountaineer Gringer Stormpike. The Stormpike clan is respected in Ironforge for its discerning taste and martial pride. Elmore turns to trustworthy travelers to carry the axe north, across the distance between Stormwind and the dwarven borderlands. At Loch Modan's northern guard tower, Mountaineer Stormpike watches over lands troubled by wandering troggs and burrowing kobolds. The southern human kingdoms face rumors of unrest and banditry, while the dwarven frontier has dangers of its own. Stormpike needs a new blade to help keep the mountain passes secure.

quest:354.text: Deaths in the Family. Coleman Farthing, once a mill worker, seeks vengeance from Brill against the Agamand family. During the Third War, he stayed to defend their estate with his fellow workers, and they died beside their stubborn masters. The Agamands rose again as mindless thralls of the Lich King. Before the Third War, the Agamands were Tirisfal Glades' wealthiest and most influential farming family. Their mills and fertile pastures yielded grain through the labor of dozens of tenant farmers and millers. When the Plague of Undeath crossed Lordaeron, the family refused to flee or abandon its ancestral lands. They believed their stone walls and loyal workers could hold back the horrors advancing from the east. Coleman Farthing and the other workers trusted their lords' assurances and stayed to defend the estate. The Scourge overwhelmed them. The Agamands and their workers were slaughtered, then raised into undeath where they fell. Farthing eventually broke free through Sylvanas Windrunner's liberation. The Agamand patriarchs and heirs remained under the Lich King's mental grip, wandering the ruined mills as mindless Scourge sentries. Coleman Farthing now lives in Brill, still bitter toward the masters whose pride cost him his mortal life. Seeking vengeance and closure, he sends Forsaken champions to Agamand Mills to destroy Gregor, Nissa, and Thurman Agamand. He hopes his former masters kept enough awareness behind their rotting faces to feel terror as their unlife came to an end.

quest:355.text: Speak with Sevren. In Brill, Magistrate Sevren calls you north after Coleman Farthing's reckoning at Agamand Mills. The undead there threaten the settlement's northern border. Coleman Farthing wanted revenge on his former neighbors, the Agamands, and sent travelers north to kill the undead around their flour mills. After you delivered the remains, Coleman saw that his private grudge touched a wider danger. The Agamand estate still crawls with aggressive Scourge minions, close to Brill. Magistrate Sevren oversees Brill's civic and military security for the Dark Lady. Reports say you survived deep incursions into the haunted farmlands, and Sevren now directs you toward the source of the infestation: the ancient Agamand family crypt.
