quest:860.text: Sergra Darkthorn. Having proven their basic tracking and stalking skills in the rolling hills of Mulgore, young tauren are directed outward into the arid wilderness of the Barrens. Melor Stonehoof sends aspiring hunters north of the border to report to Sergra Darkthorn at the Crossroads. This journey marks the hunter's formal transition from local trials to the demanding predatory hierarchy of Kalimdor's broader plains. For a novice tauren hunter, completing initial rites in Mulgore is only the beginning. The lush valleys of their ancestral homeland are protected and familiar, nurturing beasts that test patience rather than sheer survival. Melor Stonehoof recognizes when a hunter's spirit has grown enough to require harsher trials. He instructs his pupils to pack their gear, leave the safety of Bloodhoof Village, and venture east across the mountain pass into the baked scrublands of the Barrens. The path through the red rock canyons leads straight into the wide, sun-scorched savanna where the young Horde stakes its claim. At the intersection of Kalimdor's central trade routes lies the Crossroads, a fortified settlement bustling with orcs, trolls, and tauren. There waits Sergra Darkthorn, an experienced orc shaman renowned for her unforgiving standards. She acts as a mentor to any bold enough to stalk the Barrens' fierce fauna, promising to temper raw eagerness into hardened wilderness discipline.

quest:861.text: The Hunter's Way. In Mulgore, Skorn Whitecloud guides aspiring trackers through the Hunter's Way. To prove their skill and respect for the wild, you hunt flatland prowlers and bring their claws to Melor Stonehoof on Thunder Bluff's Hunter Rise. For the tauren, hunting is among the highest honors. It calls for patience, attention to the Earth Mother's balance, and respect for the beasts across the plains. Elder Skorn Whitecloud has spent decades tracking across Kalimdor and now rests in Mulgore. He sees young adventurers eager to roam and gives them a traditional trial to shape their ambition into discipline. Flatland prowlers test a candidate's tracking skill. These great cats move swiftly and quietly, hiding in Mulgore's high grass before ambushing their prey. Bring four sets of claws to show you can spot a predator before it catches you, then turn its ferocity against it. After gathering the claws, you climb the wooden towers and bridges to Thunder Bluff's Hunter Rise. Melor Stonehoof receives the trophies there. A master tracker who values Skorn Whitecloud's ancient wisdom, Melor accepts them as proof that you have the spirit to learn more of Kalimdor's hunting ways.

quest:863.text: The Escape. You help Wizzlecrank flee the Venture Company drill site at the Sludge Fen in the northern Barrens. Trapped in a stolen prototype shredder, the goblin pilot needs protection from company mercenaries as he climbs from the industrial pit. Afterward, you report to his contact, Sputtervalve, in Ratchet. Wizzlecrank struggles to control the stolen shredder at the Sludge Fen. He has lit the prototype deep inside the Venture Company drill site, but knows little of its levers and switches. The heavy machine lurches across the muddy quarry floor, and its erratic driving and roaring joints alert nearby laborers and armed guards. A stealthy escape becomes a running battle up the excavation pit’s western ramp. The Venture Company sends mercenaries to stop the stolen prototype. As the machine claws up the slope toward open ground, squads move to intercept and disable it. The shredder lashes out, but cannot withstand their sabotage without your protection. It clears the rim and staggers from the main drilling depression, though the machine soon suffers a critical failure.

quest:8642.text: Silvervein the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, Silvervein the Elder appears on the hills above Thelsamar in Loch Modan. Travelers honor him and the ancient ties among Azeroth’s elder peoples, and he grants an ancestral blessing in return. Above Thelsamar, Silvervein watches the ridges in silence. During the Lunar Festival, travelers honor him as a keeper of memories from ages past. Below, Loch Modan faces trogg invasions and local disputes, while the elder spirit remains peaceful on his overlook. Travelers who seek Silvervein find gratitude for their homage to Azeroth’s olden races. His greeting honors those who remember the ancient peoples, and he offers them a commemorative token.

quest:8646.text: Hammershout the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, Hammershout the Elder appears in Stormwind's Park. Travelers honor the old races and receive a ceremonial token from him. During the Lunar Festival, revered ancestor spirits appear across Azeroth with wisdom and blessings for travelers who pay their respects. Hammershout the Elder appears in Stormwind's Park district. His presence near the heart of human civilization recalls the ancient races who walked the land before today's kingdoms rose. Hammershout the Elder asks for no trial or oath, only acknowledgment of the past. He is relieved and grateful when people still honor the old races. In return, he gives travelers a ceremonial token, a sign of the bond between the living and the spirits who came before.

quest:8649.text: Stormbrow the Elder. Near Goldshire, Stormbrow the Elder waits beside the water during the Lunar Festival. Travelers honor ancient traditions and the olden races of Azeroth, and receive a token of remembrance in return. A quiet pond lies just behind the smithy in Goldshire, where Stormbrow the Elder appears. Guards, tradesfolk, and weary travelers pass through town on their way into the forest. Beneath Elwynn Forest's canopy, the honored spirit welcomes anyone who comes to honor the realm's long history. During the Lunar Festival, spirits of great ancestors return to walk among the living. Stormbrow the Elder commends travelers who remember those who came before. For honoring the wisdom and legacy of the elder peoples, he grants a blessing and a commemorative coin for the season.

quest:865.text: Raptor Horns. In Ratchet, Mebok Mizzyrix wants intact raptor horns for a scheme of his own. The goblin believes the cunning of Barrens raptors lies in their horns and hires travelers to hunt Sunscale Scytheclaws. Mebok Mizzyrix looks for fortune in Ratchet, where goblins chase one scheme after another. He has watched the Barrens raptors act with unusual craft and coordination compared with beasts elsewhere. Mebok decided their intelligence must be held in their horns. He has no formal inquiry in mind; he wants to put this idea to profit. Mebok wants undamaged horns from Sunscale Scytheclaws, among the Barrens' deadliest predators. They prowl the southern stretches of the Barrens and the northern borders near Ashenvale. The raptors hunt in packs and defend their territory fiercely, so bringing down one and taking its horns intact calls for considerable skill in battle.

quest:8652.text: Graveborn the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, Graveborn the Elder waits near Brill in Tirisfal Glades. Travelers seek him among the blighted groves to honor Azeroth’s ancient forebears, and receive his blessing and a holiday token. In Tirisfal Glades, the Forsaken live among ruined manors and grave sites. During the Lunar Festival, a spirit from ancient times appears just outside Brill. Elder Graveborn welcomes pilgrims who pause to honor the old ways, even in a land shattered by the Scourge and reclaimed by the undead. During the Lunar Festival, spirits from long-past eras return with wisdom and gratitude. When you approach Elder Graveborn, he says it heartens him that Tirisfal’s people still honor their ancestors despite the land’s decay. He gives a Coin of Ancestry to those who greet him.

quest:8653.text: Goldwell the Elder. At Kharanos during the Lunar Festival, Elder Goldwell welcomes travelers and offers a chance to honor the ancestors. He keeps this old tradition alive across the snowy dwarven lands. Beside the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, Elder Goldwell watches the busy trade path leading to Ironforge's gates. During the Lunar Festival, he welcomes weary travelers, adventurers, and locals. His presence carries the long memory of ancient days, when early mortals walked beneath Azeroth's stars. In Dun Morogh's winter winds, a visit to Elder Goldwell offers a moment to reflect. He is relieved and glad that mortals still remember the ancient races and their deeds. He thanks all who pause their journeys to show respect, and gives a Coin of Ancestry as an emblem of his blessing.

quest:867.text: Harpy Raiders. Witchwing harpies strike supply caravans on the northwestern trails of the Barrens. Darsok Swiftdagger at the Crossroads sends you to hunt their raiders and roguefeathers, taking their talons as proof. Witchwing harpies strike caravans crossing the Barrens. From rocky crags in the northwest, they swoop on merchant trains and supply wagons. They kill pack animals and seize goods bound for orcish outposts, making each journey through the region dangerous. Darsok Swiftdagger, an orc rogue, has spent days watching the flock's habits and ranks. He believes an unfocused assault on their mountain roosts would scatter them. His plan is to break the Witchwing from the lowest rank upward, starting with the raiders before turning to their commanders.

quest:8670.text: Runetotem the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, travelers in Durotar can honor Runetotem the Elder, an ancestral spirit. She waits in Razor Hill beneath a beam of heavenly light, offering blessings and festival tokens to those who remember the past. During the Lunar Festival, spirits of ancient elders appear across Azeroth to commune with the living. Elder Runetotem waits inside Razor Hill, just past the southern entrance. A beam of starlight falls on her as she watches over the orcish settlement. Travelers can pause there to honor the wisdom of those who came before. When you pay Elder Runetotem homage, she gives you a festival token of fortune and tells you where other spirits can be found. Her directions point toward Elder Darkhorn and Elder High Mountain elsewhere across the continent.

quest:8673.text: Bloodhoof the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, travelers honor Bloodhoof the Elder just north of Bloodhoof Village. The ancestral spirit appears near the bridge and offers a Coin of Ancestry in return. During the Lunar Festival, spirits of heroes and elders from ages past return to Azeroth. Elder Bloodhoof appears just north of Bloodhoof Village, near the bridge. Travelers honor the sacrifices of the past by approaching the elder, who offers words of encouragement and a Coin of Ancestry. On Mulgore's ancestral lands, Elder Bloodhoof links the living tauren tribes with the memory of their forebears. Honoring the dead is central to tauren spiritual life. It keeps the Earth Mother, the ancestors, and those walking the plains in harmony.

quest:8675.text: Skychaser the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, Skychaser the Elder appears atop Sentinel Tower in Westfall. Travelers climb to honor her and receive her blessing in return. Sentinel Hill holds against Defias raiders and roving scavengers in Westfall's troubled scrublands. During the Lunar Festival, an ancestral spirit named Elder Skychaser appears on the open platform atop Sentinel Tower. From above the dust and wind, she watches over the weary soldiers and beleaguered settlers below. Anyone may climb the tower and pay her respect. Across Azeroth, the Lunar Festival honors wisdom, heritage, and the deeds of ancient spirits who walked the earth before today's struggles. When you approach, Elder Skychaser recognizes the living spark within you. She accepts your homage and gives you a token of her favor, a bond between the living and the honored dead.

quest:8677.text: Darkhorn the Elder. At the Lunar Festival, Darkhorn the Elder receives travelers in Orgrimmar. Honored among the ancestors, she embodies age, survival, and ancestral pride. During the Lunar Festival, revered ancestors appear across Azeroth to share wisdom with the living. Elder Darkhorn rests within Orgrimmar’s fortified ramparts, watching the young warrior city. You can approach her to honor those who walked the earth generations ago, whether you fight for the Horde or brave the gates as an Alliance traveler. Travelers greet Elder Darkhorn and pay her reverence, and she recognizes the spark of life in them. For honoring the old ways, you receive a Coin of Ancestry and her blessing. The tokens celebrate victory over ancient perils and remind the living to cherish the strength handed down through unbroken bloodlines.

quest:8678.text: Proudhorn the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, Proudhorn the Elder receives visitors atop Thunder Bluff. Tauren honor him as an ancestral spirit and pay respect to the wisdom of those who watch over Mulgore and the Horde. During the Lunar Festival, Proudhorn the Elder appears high on Thunder Bluff's windblown mesas. Tauren hold their ancestors' voices in the highest regard. They believe ancient leaders and sages remain as spirits, offering guidance and strength to the living. Travelers who climb Thunder Bluff's heights to honor Elder Proudhorn are welcomed as vital flames of life. In return for their homage, he gives them a Coin of Ancestry, a sign of communion between the enduring past and the living champions who fight for the world's future.

quest:86784.text: Sticks and Bones. Deathguard Bartholomew asks travelers in Tirisfal Glades to gather dry branches for Eleanor Shackleton. The experienced survivalist camps in the western hills, far from the settlements. Deathguard Bartholomew pauses between patrols to help an acquaintance in Tirisfal Glades. Deathguards guard against the Scourge and Scarlet crusaders, but Bartholomew also looks out for Eleanor Shackleton. She spends her unlife in the harsh elements, so he asks you to gather dry branches for her campfire. Eleanor Shackleton survives alone in Tirisfal's blighted wilderness. Though undead, the Forsaken still feel the damp, bitter chill rolling off the northern moors. Eleanor's rule for gathering wood is simple: when you think you have enough firewood, gather five times more. Grateful for the extra timber, she lets you keep Bartholomew's basket and shares the warmth of her fire.

quest:8680.text: Windtotem the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, Windtotem the Elder receives travelers on a bluff above Ratchet. She welcomes those who honor the wisdom of ages past and offers an ancestral blessing and guidance to other elders across Kalimdor. On a grassy hill just northwest of Ratchet’s flight master, Windtotem the Elder watches over the goblin docks and open sea. Iron, gunpowder, and coin pass through the harbor below, while quiet Barrens winds and a shaft of celestial light reach the elder. During the Lunar Festival, Windtotem the Elder guides wandering mortals, as do the other ancestral spirits. Those who seek her receive her blessing and a token of her favor, along with whispers pointing to nearby elders across the continent, including Elder Runetotem and Elder Bloodhoof.

quest:869.text: Raptor Thieves. A raptor has stolen the guards' payroll from the Crossroads tower, leaving the defenders baffled. Gazrog calls for a cull to keep the beasts from striking again. The Crossroads depends on mercenary and grunt guards to keep trade routes open across the Barrens. Their pay matters to morale and discipline. When silver vanished from the guard tower, leaders expected Centaur raiders or Quilboar scavengers. Instead, a raptor was caught stealing in the dead of night, leaving the settlement stunned and short of coin. Gazrog does not know why wild beasts would hoard shiny coins, and he has no interest in studying their behavior. The guards are restless without their pay, so he calls for blood and deterrence. He sends hunters to take a dozen raptor heads from across the savannah, hoping to curb the predators' boldness before a full search for the silver begins.

quest:87.text: Goldtooth. Near Fargodeep Mine, Auntie Bernice Stonefield's necklace is missing, and the Stonefield and Maclure families blame each other. Billy Maclure admits he lost it while playing nearby, and you follow the trail to the kobold Goldtooth. Auntie Bernice Stonefield's missing necklace has stirred up trouble between the Stonefield and Maclure families. Bernice suspects her rivals, but Billy Maclure lost the trinket while playing near Fargodeep Mine. He tries to hide his guilt, saying he only found the necklace before a creature snatched it away. Billy says a large kobold with gleaming fangs took the shiny necklace and ran to a den above Fargodeep Mine. Goldtooth actually lurks on the mine's lower level. Slaying the kobold brings Bernice's necklace back, settles the families' dispute, and earns you an old campaign keepsake left by Bernice's late husband.

quest:870.text: The Forgotten Pools. At the Forgotten Pools, life surges through the dry Barrens for reasons the Cenarion Circle cannot explain. Tonga Runetotem at the Crossroads sends Horde adventurers to inspect the oasis northwest of the settlement, where druids sense unseen forces beneath the earth. The Barrens once flourished as fertile land before ages of war and the Sundering shattered the continent. The region became sun-baked scrubland, but lush oases have recently begun taking root in its dry basin. Druids of the Cenarion Circle find this sudden growth unnatural. They sense powers beneath the earth pressing upward, stirring vegetation and wildlife into life in scattered pockets across the wastes.

quest:871.text: Disrupt the Attacks. Thork needs the Crossroads defended as Razormane quilboar cut its supply roads. Their ambushes have halted caravans from Durotar, and the outpost is running short on food and gear. You strike at the quilboar while scouts search for the one directing their warband. The Crossroads guards a key junction for Horde traffic through central Kalimdor. Freight wagons and caravans bring food, iron, and equipment west from Durotar, and the outpost depends on those supplies. Razormane ambushes along the northeast trails have stopped the deliveries. Stores are running low, and Thork cannot wait for peaceful talks. Thork sends you against the quilboar bramble dens northeast of the settlement before they can assault the town walls. Striking their Water Seekers, Thornweavers, and Hunters weakens the Razormane scouting perimeter and deprives raiding parties of magical and logistical support. These skirmishes buy time while Horde trackers search the brush for the one organizing the raids.

quest:8717.text: Moonwarden the Elder. At the Crossroads, Moonwarden the Elder receives travelers beneath a beam of light. During the Lunar Festival, people honor ancestral spirits and seek his wisdom and directions to elders across Kalimdor. At the Crossroads, a column of light falls around Elder Moonwarden. He is one of the ancient spirits honored during the Lunar Festival, when mortals set aside their conflicts to seek the wisdom of generations past. Elder Moonwarden looks to the stars for answers to earthly mysteries. He offers ancestral blessings and directs seekers to other elders across Kalimdor, including Elder Bloodhoof, Elder High Mountain, Elder Morningdew, and Elder Runetotem.

quest:8718.text: Bladeswift the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, Bladeswift the Elder's ancient spirit is honored in Darnassus. In the Cenarion Enclave, travelers seek his wisdom beneath the stars and a blessing tied to night elven tradition. During the Lunar Festival, revered ancestral spirits appear across Azeroth to share wisdom and bless travelers. In Darnassus, Bladeswift the Elder appears among the boughs of the Cenarion Enclave. This ancient spirit turns his gaze to the night sky and its mysteries, while the living face the trials of the present. Night elves have long looked to the heavens as reflections of Elune and signs of deeper truths. Bladeswift urges the wise and fortunate to seek answers among the stars. Those who honor him receive a Coin of Ancestry and join a ceremony that links the living with spirits of the past.

quest:872.text: The Disruption Ends. Thork orders a strike against the Razormane raids on the Horde road. Kreenig Snarlsnout leads the attacks from the northern Barrens, and his death is meant to break the warband's hold on the route between Durotar and the Crossroads. The road between Durotar and the Crossroads carries provisions and reinforcements through the northern Barrens. Razormane quilboar ambushes have kept it under threat. Scout reports name their leader as Kreenig Snarlsnout, whose raiding party organizes the attacks. Thork orders a strike against Kreenig, hoping to break the warband's unity and secure the road. Kreenig's war party is entrenched in craggy hills northeast of the Crossroads. Hardy Razormane Defenders and geomancers who manipulate the arid earth shield his position. Thork's order is to break through that guard and strike Kreenig in his redoubt, sending a warning across the plains. His tusk will prove the leader's death and show that the Horde will not accept attacks on its lifelines.

quest:8721.text: Starweave the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, Elder Starweave receives visitors in Auberdine. Travelers come to honor Kalimdor's ancestral spirits and seek her wisdom and blessing. During the Lunar Festival, ancestral spirits appear across Azeroth beneath pillars of celestial light. Elder Starweave joins the night elves in Auberdine, a harbor on Darkshore's coast. Travelers come to honor her and seek guidance from ages past. Elder Starweave looks to the heavens above Kalimdor. She tells visitors that the stars hold answers to mortal doubts and worldly riddles. Those who seek her counsel are urged to look skyward for truth and receive ancestral favor, along with tidings of other wandering spirits across the wild frontier.

quest:8725.text: Riversong the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, pilgrims seek Riversong the Elder beneath a shrine in Astranaar. The night elf spirit offers wisdom and points them toward other honored ancestors across Kalimdor. In Astranaar, Riversong the Elder waits beneath an open night elf shrine. A shaft of light falls through the Ashenvale canopy onto her spirit. During the Lunar Festival, pilgrims gather there to honor those who came before. Riversong the Elder recalls how night elves read truth and mystery in the stars. She urges patience and contemplation, then guides pilgrims toward other spirits, including Elder Starweave.

quest:875.text: Harpy Lieutenants. At the Crossroads, Darsok Swiftdagger sends Horde champions against the Witchwing coven in the northern Barrens. In the Dry Hills, the aim is to kill the flock’s front-line officers and break its chain of command. After the first clashes with Witchwing raiders, Darsok Swiftdagger turns the offensive toward the harpies roosting in the Dry Hills. Horde scouts are sent after the Witchwing Slayers who lead the flock. These officers keep the lesser harpies in line and coordinate raids against Horde supply paths. Their deaths are critical to securing the northern approaches of the Barrens. Witchwing Slayers lead through strength and dominance, and only the most vicious among them carry ornate rings that mark their authority within the matriarchy. Taking the rings proves the lieutenants are dead, disrupts the roost’s coordination, and sends the coven a clear message: attacks on Horde territory will meet decisive retribution.

quest:877.text: The Stagnant Oasis. Tonga Runetotem sends you southeast from the Crossroads to search the Stagnant Oasis. He wants to know if the hidden fissure beneath the Forgotten Pools has a match in its murky waters. Tonga Runetotem sends you to the Stagnant Oasis after a strange fissure is found beneath the Forgotten Pools. He suspects the sudden patches of lush growth across the Barrens have a cause beneath the earth. You search the oasis's murky shallows for another opening, among predators that haunt the water.

quest:88.text: Princess Must Die!. At Stonefield Farm, Ma Stonefield wants Princess Must Die! before Princess ruins the harvest. The enormous prize-winning sow from Brackwell Pumpkin Patch keeps raiding the Stonefields’ vegetables, and Ma wants the family to gather their crops in peace. Princess has put the Stonefield harvest at risk. The prize-winning sow belongs to the Brackwells, but she has grown enormous by crossing onto the Stonefield plots and devouring their vegetables. Ma Stonefield has had enough of the sow eating the crops she worked to grow. She wants Princess put down before the pig ruins the season’s yield. Princess does not roam alone. At Brackwell Pumpkin Patch, east beyond the Maclure homestead, protective boars surround her. To prove the sow will trouble the Stonefield fields no more, you need to get past her guards and bring back the distinctive brass collar from her neck.

quest:880.text: Altered Beings. At the Crossroads, Tonga Runetotem studies strange changes in the Barrens' oasis waters. Fissures beneath the pools may be changing the creatures that live there, and he asks you to bring him shells from altered snapjaws. Tonga Runetotem is searching for the cause of strange changes in the Barrens' oases. Though the savanna is dry, a handful of pools support fertile ground. Tonga found peculiar fissures beneath those waters, sending out potent energies. He does not know whether the force came from outside or rose from deep within the earth. Now he studies the creatures that drink from and live in the pools, hoping to learn what the fissures are doing to them. You are sent to the Lushwater Oasis and the Stagnant Oasis to gather altered snapjaw shells. Snapjaws live in the shallows, where they take in the strange essence through food and exposure. Their carapaces have changed, offering Tonga a sign of how the fissures affect local wildlife. He hopes the shells will help him understand the disturbance before it spreads farther across Kalimdor.

quest:881.text: Echeyakee. At the Crossroads, hunters prepare to face Whitemist in the northern Barrens. Sergra Darkthorn sends young Horde hunters to summon the legendary white lion and test their strength. Across the central plains, a white-maned lion rules the savannah cats. Taur-ahe speakers call him Echeyakee, or Whitemist. Legend says he moves so silently that he seems like morning mist gliding over the red earth. His strikes come swiftly, leaving prey no time for fear or suffering. Local hunters revere him as a sign of mercy and swift death. At the Crossroads, Sergra Darkthorn trains fledgling warriors. The experienced orc shaman sends her pupils to challenge the king of beasts after they have proven themselves against lesser savannah prowlers. With a special horn, you travel northeast past the mountain ridges to a graveyard of massive kodo bones. Sound the horn to challenge Echeyakee and draw the elusive predator from hiding for a test of strength and cunning.

quest:882.text: Ishamuhale. At Camp Taurajo, Jorn Skyseer sends you to face Ishamuhale, the fiercest sunscale raptor in the Barrens. The hunt tests your skill and respect for nature's deadliest predators. Sunscale raptors hunt the Barrens in cunning, vicious packs, but none inspires more dread than Speartooth. Jorn Skyseer says Ishamuhale kills by instinct and passion, not for food or territory. He hunts because killing is his nature. To face him is to test whether you can withstand a predator's unbridled ferocity. Ishamuhale will not be found resting in a nest. To draw him out, you follow the plains' natural rhythm. Jorn tells you to kill a fresh zhevra and carry its carcass to a lone, withered dead tree on the plains northwest of Ratchet. The scent of blood on the arid wind brings Ishamuhale swiftly to claim his prey. When you bring Ishamuhale's fang back to Camp Taurajo, Jorn Skyseer sees it as a profound spiritual milestone, not merely a sign of victory. Tauren belief holds that overcoming so fierce a predator lets you absorb some of its raw strength. The test then turns inward: you must carry that might with temperance, honor, and restraint, rather than surrender to blind bloodlust.

quest:8827.text: Winter's Presents. In Ironforge, revelers are gathering for the Feast of Winter Veil. They point travelers toward Greatfather Winter beside the Smokywood Pastures stalls, where gifts wait beneath the holiday tree. Ironforge fills with Feast of Winter Veil cheer as winter settles over Khaz Modan. Revelers and holiday enthusiasts send passersby toward the decorated tree near the Smokywood Pastures vendors. Smokywood Pastures, a goblin enterprise, shares the season with Greatfather Winter. He greets visitors while goblin merchants remind gift recipients that their festive treats and seasonal wares make gifts for friends and family.

quest:8828.text: Winter's Presents. In Orgrimmar, Winter's Presents await beneath the festive tree during the Feast of Winter Veil. Holiday organizers and goblin apparatus tenders direct Horde heroes to Great-father Winter, where gifts have been prepared for them. The Feast of Winter Veil brings a pause for celebration to Orgrimmar as the chill winds of late year sweep across Durotar. Promoters from Smokywood Pastures and holiday enthusiasts spread word through the capital that gifts wait beneath the decorated tree. Warriors, hunters, and wanderers resting in the city are all invited to share in the season’s generosity. Great-father Winter sits among holiday ribbons and packaged cartons near the Smokywood Pastures market. The ancient figure marks the season’s renewal, while goblin merchants nearby offer seasonal wares and festive treats to visitors.

quest:8846.text: Five Signets for War Supplies. In Ironforge, Field Marshal Snowfall gathers provisions and equipment for the Grand Alliance's war effort. Champions can trade commendation signets for field rations, bandages, and combat supplies. The stockpiles keep those working on the home front equipped for coming conflicts. Field Marshal Snowfall organizes the flow of materials as one of the Alliance's primary quartermasters in Ironforge. Armies need more than courage; they also need steady supplies for the fronts. Couriers and heroes bring commendation signets earned through civic service, and Snowfall trades them for survival rations and tactical gear. Royal heralds offer public honor and civic standing for commendation signets. Snowfall offers another choice: trade five signets for field gear, without pomp, glory, or official recognition. The exchange gives soldiers and volunteers practical goods to help keep them alive when marching into hostile lands.

quest:8851.text: Five Signets for War Supplies. Orgrimmar's stores gather supplies for the Horde's campaign across Kalimdor. Workers earn commendation signets for their contributions, and Warlord Gorchuk exchanges them for supplies to equip the fighters. Across Kalimdor, the Horde gathers raw goods, weapons, and provisions for a vast campaign. Gatherers and tradesfolk bring bandages, metals, and herbs into the cities, where military overseers award commendation signets for their work. The tokens mark each contribution to the stockpile growing along Orgrimmar's central avenues. Warlord Gorchuk knows the wider war effort needs supplies, but each warrior also needs gear and provisions to survive the march into battle. Fighters can trade their commendation signets back into the Horde's stores for field supplies and surplus materiel, giving up personal recognition for what they need on the front.

quest:886.text: The Barrens Oases. High on the Elder Rise of Thunder Bluff, Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem senses an unsettling surge of power flowing into the arid soils of the Barrens. To uncover the truth, he dispatches promising travelers eastward past Mulgore's gates to rendezvous with his kinsman, Tonga Runetotem, at the Crossroads. This mission marks the beginning of an investigation into the unnatural waters springing up across the sun-baked plains. While the plains of Mulgore flourish under the watchful gaze of the Earth Mother, the vast savannas of the Barrens to the east have remained harsh, scorched, and dry for generations. Recently, however, the tauren druids meditating atop Thunder Bluff's Elder Rise have detected strange currents of energy waking deep beneath the parched plains. Life is stirring where it ought not to be, and the Cenarion Circle fears that whatever force is causing this surge may harbor hidden peril for the land and its creatures. To investigate these strange occurrences, Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem dispatched Tonga Runetotem into the field. Recognizing that the vast wilderness holds dangers too great for one investigator alone, Hamuul enlists travelers leaving Mulgore to hasten after Tonga. Following the road east past Bloodhoof Village and through the mountain passes leads straight to the Crossroads—the dusty, bustling heart of Horde territory in the Barrens—where Tonga awaits answers.

quest:8866.text: Bronzebeard the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, travelers honor Bronzebeard the Elder in Ironforge. His greeting offers wisdom and a token of esteem. The people of Khaz Modan revere their forebears and their long-lived heritage. During the Lunar Festival, spirits and venerable elders appear across Azeroth to share wisdom with travelers who honor the past. In Ironforge, Elder Bronzebeard embodies the Bronzebeard clan’s stalwart resilience. When travelers come to pay their respects, he is quietly pleased that the people still honor the lineage of the old races. No great trial or perilous journey is needed. Travelers pause, acknowledge Elder Bronzebeard, and offer a greeting. He returns their good wishes and gives them a Coin of Ancestry, a festival token that recalls the living bond between the present and the generations who forged Khaz Modan from stone and fire.

quest:887.text: Southsea Freebooters. Along the Merchant Coast south of Ratchet, Southsea Freebooters strike goblin trading vessels. Gazlowe hires adventurers to attack their camp and curb the raids. Ratchet's trade suffers from pirates on the Merchant Coast. The port sits in central Kalimdor, where merchant vessels travel between Kalimdor and the eastern continents. South of town, Southsea Freebooters hold a fortified beach camp. From there, they attack goblin cargo ships arriving and departing, cutting into profits and disrupting local shipping lanes. Gazlowe blames the pirates and the Steamwheedle Cartel's naval leaders. The Trade Princes have spent immense sums on defensive fleets, yet Vice Admiral Grezzlik has failed to patrol the waters effectively. Frustrated by Undermine's slow response, Gazlowe hires independent mercenaries to thin the pirate brigands and cannoneers.

quest:888.text: Stolen Booty. Pirate cargo off Ratchet’s coast has left Gazlowe choosing what matters most. Stolen Booty brings him two vital goods: boots for local laborers and a delicate telescopic lens needed to complete his observatory. The Southsea Freebooters have troubled merchant lanes across the Great Sea for years. Their fortified camp just south of Ratchet brought them into direct conflict with Gazlowe. Pirates intercepted merchant vessels bound for the port and took valuable supplies from the Steamwheedle Cartel. Some goods could be written off as a cost of shipping. Specialized cargo mattered enough for Gazlowe to hire mercenaries to break into the pirate stronghold. Gazlowe has two practical priorities. Drizzlik sent a needed shipment of boots from Booty Bay for local laborers. The other item is specialized: a ground telescopic lens made for the observatory tower overlooking Ratchet. Its twin arrived safely by caravan through Durotar, but pirates seized this lens at sea. Until it is recovered, the observatory remains an empty frame.

quest:890.text: The Missing Shipment. In Ratchet, Gazlowe waits for goods sent from Booty Bay across the Great Sea. He sends couriers to Wharfmaster Dizzywig to check the dock records, while the Southsea Freebooters remain a possible cause of the delay. Ratchet is the Steamwheedle Cartel's trading port on Kalimdor. Ships cross the Great Sea from Booty Bay with manufactured goods, exotic supplies, and heavy freight for the town's building and trade. When cargo goes missing, business suffers. Chief Engineer Gazlowe keeps close track of every crate brought into port. The Southsea Freebooters haunt the coast south of Ratchet and often intercept merchant ships. Gazlowe checks his records before accusing the pirates or sending anyone into a fight. He sends his inventory ledger to Wharfmaster Dizzywig at the docks. Dizzywig oversees the unloading and storage of ship cargo, and can check whether goods were lost at sea or misplaced in a warehouse.

quest:892.text: The Missing Shipment. At Ratchet’s docks, Dizzywig’s ledger points away from harbor graft and toward the Southsea Freebooters. Gazlowe receives the records and prepares to reclaim his lost cargo. Ratchet’s trade and its port bring constant logistical headaches. When a shipment fails to arrive, Gazlowe suspects bad harbor accounts or foul play on the piers. Wharfmaster Dizzywig examines the manifest and insists his books are clean. The intake records account for everything, so the missing merchandise never made it onto the dock.

quest:894.text: Samophlange. At a Venture Company outpost in the northern Barrens, Sputtervalve wants a device called a samophlange. He sends you southwest of the Sludge Fen to find it. In the northern Barrens, Sputtervalve cannot explain what the Venture Company is building. The goblin engineer and tinker works in Ratchet, while the rival company experiments southwest of the Sludge Fen. Its people call one device a samophlange. Sputtervalve does not know its purpose or value, but wants to study its design before his competitors can profit from it. The Venture Company guards its research site with armed overseers, deforesters, and machinery. Sputtervalve gives you an intercepted operating manual to help shut down the rig safely. At the central control station, you find a locked console with levers, lights, and gauges. Three control valves keep the rig's pressure in order.

quest:895.text: WANTED: Baron Longshore. On Ratchet's docks, Chief Engineer Gazlowe posts a bounty for Baron Longshore. The pirate captain hails from Gilneas and commands vessels of the Southsea Freebooters. His presence along the Merchant Coast threatens goblin merchant shipping across the region. South of Ratchet, the Southsea Freebooters hold fortified camps along the Merchant Coast. Their pirates harass merchant vessels and disrupt the sea lanes the Steamwheedle Cartel relies on between Ratchet, Booty Bay, and points beyond. Under captains such as Baron Longshore, the raids drain the local goblin administration and threaten trade along the coast. Baron Longshore comes from Gilneas, the isolated human kingdom across the sea. On Kalimdor, he commands the pirate vessel Heedless and leads crews ashore just north of Northwatch Hold. Chief Engineer Gazlowe answers with a bounty, calling for Longshore's identifiable head.

quest:896.text: Miner's Fortune. Wharfmaster Dizzywig has heard of a fist-sized emerald at the Venture Company's Boulder Lode Mine. He hires you to take the Cats Eye Emerald from the mine's supervisors and share the profits. Wharfmaster Dizzywig hears the merchants who pass through Ratchet's harbor on the routes between Ratchet and Booty Bay. Word reaches him of a huge gem found deep in the Boulder Lode Mine. The Venture Company strips the northern Barrens for its own gain, so few are likely to ask questions if its finest recent find disappears. Northeast of the Sludge Fen, laborers fill the Boulder Lode Mine's rocky shaft. The Venture Co. Overseers and Enforcers have taken the Cats Eye Emerald, and an ordinary digger cannot claim a prize so rare. You need to face the armed managers, secure the stone, and bring it to Dizzywig. He can judge its value against the market in Undermine.

quest:900.text: Samophlange. At the Sludge Fen, Samophlange machinery keeps the Venture Company's digging rig running. Three valves must be sealed before the central apparatus can be shut down safely. At the Sludge Fen, the Venture Company's machinery is complex and dangerous. The central console makes clear that the core cannot be stopped with a single switch. Its feed lines must be handled by hand first, or the apparatus could fail or explode. Three valves control the flow into the rig: the Main Control Valve, the Fuel Control Valve, and the Regulator Valve. Each must be sealed by hand against high pressure. As they close, the console's green indicators fade to yellow, making it safe to engage the central shutoff.

quest:901.text: Samophlange. At the Sludge Fen, the Venture Company’s machinery waits with its valves shut and its pressure relieved. Tinkerer Sniggles holds the key to open the control unit and free the samophlange within. You have relieved the pressure by turning the auxiliary valves, and the dials and gauges have settled. The housing remains locked against tampering. Its key rests with the goblin engineer overseeing the drilling site. Tinkerer Sniggles oversees the Venture Company’s equipment at the Sludge Fen. He keeps the console key in a hut just northeast of the main rig. You need that key to open the housing and reach the samophlange.

quest:902.text: Samophlange. At the Venture Company console, you uncover the elusive samophlange and carry it to Ratchet. You have shut down the controls and their defenses; now the delicate device is ready for Sputtervalve to examine. Behind the Venture Company console's faceplate, wiring and purposeless tubing crowd around strange engineering. Deep inside lies the samophlange, a core component that has baffled engineers across the region. With a firm tug, you free the device from its housing and carry it back to the goblin who began the recovery effort.

quest:903.text: Prowlers of the Barrens. At the Crossroads, Sergra Darkthorn sends you after the savannah prowlers. Their claws will show whether you can face the Barrens' greatest beasts. Sergra Darkthorn tests hunters who have already faced the plainstriders and zhevras. Southwest of the Crossroads, savannah prowlers vanish into the central Barrens' gold and ochre scrub. These great cats hunt instead of grazing with the herds. They wait in tall grass, then ambush their prey, and unwary travelers can fall to them. Sergra warns you that prowlers know how to hunt. Read the grasses and strike before a cat leaps if you mean to claim its paws and claws. Bring back seven prowler claws to show you have the cunning and quick reflexes to survive against Kalimdor's deadliest wildlife.

quest:905.text: The Angry Scytheclaws. South of the Crossroads, Sergra Darkthorn sends hunters to face the savage scytheclaws stalking the Barrens. Bring sunscale raptor feathers to their breeding nests, and prove your courage in a land that gives little quarter. Sergra Darkthorn tests hunters against the beasts of the Barrens. After lesser trials, she sends you south of the Crossroads to hunt vicious sunscale raptors and take their feathers. Then you carry those feathers southwest of the Stagnant Oasis, into the heart of raptor territory. Placing them in the nests is the true test: it shows you can face the scytheclaws without fear. Three raptor nests lie southwest of the Stagnant Oasis, near the Gold Road. Red, blue, and yellow eggs mark the separate clutches. Scytheclaws defend their nests fiercely against anything that comes near. Place the feathers of fallen raptors among the eggs, and you make your challenge clear to the beasts. Return to the Crossroads after entering the nests, and Sergra can see you have faced the danger and lived. Walking out of a raptor den takes raw courage. The Barrens test every hunter; each fight may harden you, or leave your bones among the kodo ribs scattered across the dirt.

quest:907.text: Enraged Thunder Lizards. In the southern Barrens, thunder lizards roam the plains around Camp Taurajo. Jorn Skyseer calls hunters to face the great beasts and bring back their blood as part of a wider rite of passage. After defeating the raptor Ishamuhale, you return to Camp Taurajo. The tauren elder Jorn Skyseer now tests your strength against the largest grazers of the land. Stormsnouts and Thunderheads roam the southern Barrens, their heavy strides able to crush an unwary hunter beneath them. Tauren and orc hunters prize poise, position, and strength when facing a thunder lizard. Jorn asks you to bring back samples of their potent blood, proof that you stood in the path of the rumbling beasts and survived with your bones unbroken. The trophy opens the way to Jorn's final quarry in the skies.

quest:90902.text: Rediscovering the Light. In Deathknell, newly raised Forsaken paladins face the pain of calling on the Holy Light. Aramis Hammerhand teaches them to heal wounded Deathguards through the burning agony. Newly risen Forsaken paladins must face a hard truth: the Holy Light still answers them, but burns their withered bodies. Many were champions of the Silver Hand or knights of Lordaeron before they fell. Aramis Hammerhand teaches them that powers once used without thought now bring fierce pain. The Light clashes with the foul magic that sustains undeath, so calling on it takes resolve and endurance. Deathguards in Deathknell suffer grievous wounds fighting mindless zombies, and Forsaken paladins are called to heal them. Aramis teaches that pushing through the burning pain is like exercising an atrophied muscle. The paladins treat that agony as a badge of honor and proof that the Light has not forsaken them.

quest:91208.text: Coming to Terms. Offered by Aramis Hammerhand in Deathknell, this quest tasks newly risen paladins with reaching out to a fellow knight struggling to accept undeath. Fleeing into the hills in terror, the newly returned warrior faces the agonizing realization of becoming what she once fought against. Awakening from death into the ranks of the Forsaken is jarring for anyone, but for former paladins of the Silver Hand, the shock is visceral. Having dedicated their mortal lives to destroying the undead in service to the Holy Light, these individuals suddenly find their souls tethered back to decomposing flesh. While some adapt under the guidance of Aramis Hammerhand, others are overwhelmed by horror and confusion, fleeing into the Tirisfal wilderness rather than confronting their grim new existence.

quest:91209.text: Continue Your Training. Newly risen Forsaken paladins leave Deathknell for instruction in Brill. Aramis Hammerhand sends them east into Tirisfal Glades, where dangers and distrust await those who wield the Holy Light. After learning martial combat and channeling holy power in Deathknell's graveyard, you are sent east into Tirisfal Glades. Your destination is Brill, the regional outpost and administrative hub for central Tirisfal. There, Shari Stilwell oversees the training of those who follow the path of the paladin in undeath. Aramis offers parting advice about the peril of being an undead paladin. Lordaeron still needs defenders against threats from beyond, yet wielding the Holy Light under Sylvanas Windrunner's banner draws suspicion. Many Forsaken suffered agony or death at the hands of holy zealots, and the Light's presence breeds distrust among their undead kin.

quest:916.text: Webwood Venom. In Shadowglen, Gilshalan Windwalker studies the giant webwood spiders of Shadowthread Cave. He asks young night elves to gather venom sacs so he can learn how Teldrassil's growth has affected the forest's wildlife. Gilshalan Windwalker has come to Shadowglen to study the webwood spiders in Shadowthread Cave. They are far larger and more aggressive than their cousins elsewhere. He suspects Teldrassil's immense magical energies are changing the local wildlife. He asks for venom sacs to compare with those of ordinary spiders and learn what has changed. Webwood spiders live in and around Shadowthread Cave, where they threaten young night elves in the glen. Gathering their venom can help thin their numbers and give Darnassian researchers evidence of Teldrassil's effect on the wild.

quest:917.text: Webwood Egg. In Shadowglen, Gilshalan Windwalker seeks an unhatched Webwood Egg for his study of Teldrassil’s wildlife. After gathering venom samples, he needs a living specimen to examine the unnatural aggression afflicting the forest’s creatures. An egg can be studied safely without subduing a full-grown spider. Gilshalan Windwalker needs live subjects to understand the unnatural corruption affecting the Webwood spiders around Shadowglen. You have secured raw venom from the aggressive spiders, but carrying a thrashing giant out of the depths would be deadly for a novice. Gilshalan asks you to bring back an unhatched egg from the brooding clutches inside Shadowthread Cave. Webwood spiders brood in Shadowthread Cave, where the forest’s increasingly hostile arachnids make their nests. An intact egg gives scholars a controlled subject that can hatch under containment. Gilshalan plans to bundle it with his venom samples and send both to Darnassus for examination. With his local study complete, he directs recruits toward higher duties in the boughs of Aldrassil.

quest:918.text: Timberling Seeds. At Lake Al'Ameth, botanist Denalan studies the growing hostility of Teldrassil's nature elementals. He seeks to harvest Timberling Seeds and test whether enriched soil can help them grow calmer. His work is one quiet effort by night elf herbalists to understand the subtle afflictions troubling the World Tree. Timberlings are nature elementals native to Teldrassil's boughs, closely bound to the health and vitality of the surrounding flora. They are usually peaceful reflections of the forest's balance, but their recent hostility has alarmed the local night elves, and no cause is known. Botanist Denalan hopes to learn what has stirred them rather than simply cull them. Denalan suspects the blemish lies deep in the ground. He hopes to sprout fresh timberlings, a gentler generation of elementals, in enriched and carefully treated loam. By harvesting seeds from wandering timberlings near Lake Al'Ameth, he aims to learn whether the land's corruption can be countered from the roots up.

quest:919.text: Timberling Sprouts. Around Lake Al'Ameth, Timberling Sprouts are spreading across Teldrassil. Denalan asks you to uproot them before they grow into hostile timberlings. Corrupted sprouts are spreading along Lake Al'Ameth's banks. Denalan lives beside the lake and knows these young plants cannot be healed. Left alone, they quickly grow into aggressive, bark-covered timberlings that threaten wildlife and travelers. Uprooting the sprouts helps protect the grove. Denalan is troubled by how quickly new sprouts appear across Teldrassil. Their spread points to a sickness in the World Tree's roots and soil, and Denalan and the druids of Darnassus seek its cause.

quest:92.text: Redridge Goulash. In Lakeshire, Redridge Goulash helps feed a town under strain. Chef Breanna fed the active Stormwind garrison during the recent Blackrock orc uprising, emptying her pantry and leaving her to seek hearty ingredients from the mountains. Lakeshire remains under siege from Blackrock orcs, gnolls, and ferocious wild beasts. When the recent orc uprising began along the ridges, Chef Breanna took on feeding the entire brigade of Stormwind troops stationed in town. Keeping the active garrison fed quickly emptied her cupboards, though the town still had plenty of hungry mouths. With her cupboards bare, Chef Breanna looks to the dangerous wilderness beyond Lakeshire's gates. Her signature goulash calls for tough mountain condor meat, seasoned snouts from formidable Great Goretusks, and crisp leg meat from giant tarantulas that prowl the hills.

quest:920.text: Tenaron's Summons. In Shadowglen, Tenaron's Summons calls you to Aldrassil. After helping Gilshalan Windwalker with woodland dangers, you are asked to meet Tenaron Stormgrip high in the great tree. The call draws you from local troubles toward the spiritual afflictions touching Teldrassil. Your work against the venomous spiders and corrupted wildlife in the glen has reached Tenaron Stormgrip. Gilshalan Windwalker tells you the elder has asked for your presence. Even night elves, with their long lives, know better than to keep an elder waiting atop Aldrassil. Tenaron waits in Aldrassil's highest chamber, looking across Shadowglen's boughs. Meeting him brings you into wider concerns of stewardship, including the cleansing of Teldrassil's moonwells and the corruption spreading through the young World Tree's ecosystem.

quest:921.text: Crown of the Earth. At Aldrassil, Tenaron Stormgrip asks young night elves to draw sacred water before they leave Shadowglen. The rite recalls Mount Hyjal and the immortality their people gave up there. Before young night elves leave Shadowglen, their elders teach them what their people lost. At the Battle of Mount Hyjal, the kaldorei sacrificed the World Tree Nordrassil to defeat Archimonde and banish the Burning Legion. The blast cost them their ageless immortality and sacred shield. Tenaron Stormgrip teaches this history as he gives novices a rite, preparing them with humility and purpose for a changing world. To complete the rite, you draw water from the moonwell north of Aldrassil with a crystal phial. Moonwell waters carry remnants of the ancient Well of Eternity. Druids channel their restorative power into the wild, while Sentinels honor the wells as tranquil shrines to Elune. The kaldorei remain wary: arcane sorcery is forbidden, and the wellspring that sustains their land recalls the reckless magic that nearly broke the world.

quest:92124.text: Book Inventory. At Northshire Abbey, Brother Paxton is frustrated by misplaced and missing tomes. He asks young adventurers to find Daniel, his daydreaming assistant, and take stock of the library archives, but Daniel's thoughts keep wandering to local tradeskills, making a straight answer hard to get. Northshire Abbey preserves old scholarly works, spiritual writings, and historical records that survived the First War in the Kingdom of Stormwind. Brother Paxton, a meticulous monk, takes great pride in the collection. Lately, books have gone missing from the shelves, and Paxton needs a clear inventory to learn how widespread the loss is. He has little patience to chase after his daydreaming helper. Daniel works as Brother Paxton's assistant in the abbey library, but his thoughts rarely stay with parchment and catalog numbers. He is fascinated by the practical trades of Elwynn Forest: smithing, leatherworking, tailoring, and herbal craft. Paxton grows exasperated as inventory work leads Daniel to ramble about local crafters instead of locating lost scriptures.

quest:922.text: Rellian Greenspyre. At Denalan's lakeside retreat in Teldrassil, you carry a timberling seed to Rellian Greenspyre in Darnassus. The handoff brings news of trouble spreading through the World Tree's boughs. Denalan has studied the plants and elemental life around Lake Al'Ameth. After gathering seeds from the local timberlings, he sends you to Darnassus with a sample for his colleague, Rellian Greenspyre. Rellian is a druid who walks the Cenarion Enclave's terraces. He had shown interest in Denalan's research and hopes to grow a timberling of his own.

quest:923.text: Tumors. In Darnassus, the Cenarion Circle seeks to contain the sickness spreading through Teldrassil. You are sent to Wellspring Lake to gather mossy tumors from afflicted timberlings, so druids can study the poison and burn the growths safely. Teldrassil’s native plants and animals are being twisted by a strange affliction. Its timberlings, usually placid nature spirits with bark for skin, have grown hostile and erratic. Grotesque mossy tumors spread across their living wood, pulsing with unnatural poison. Cenarion scholars Denalan and Rellian Greenspyre search for the cause, while timberlings already lost to the sickness must be culled to protect the rest of the boughs. Wellspring Lake in northern Teldrassil has become a focal point of the outbreak, and its timberlings are among the most tainted on the World Tree. Rellian Greenspyre asks you to kill these corrupted guardians and cut away their tumors. Bring the growths to the druids in Darnassus, where they can be burned safely. The night elves hope this will slow the contagion while they search for the disease’s source.

quest:924.text: The Demon Seed. Neeru Fireblade's orders reach Ak'Zeloth, who sends Horde travelers to destroy the Demon Seed atop Dreadmist Peak. An unstable Flawed Power Stone can break the Burning Legion's conduit before its influence spreads farther through the Barrens. High in a cave on Dreadmist Peak, the Demon Seed hangs above an altar of fire. The artifact anchors demonic power in the heart of the Barrens for the Burning Legion. The orc Ak'Zeloth prepares specialized power stones to break its link to the Nether. One must reach the peak before the stone's unstable energy runs out.

quest:92460.text: Coming of Age. Coming of Age marks the initial rite of passage for young Skyborne taking their first steps beyond Thendal Village on Zephras Isle. Guided by Ailee Farheart, novices report to village leader Rorian the Dayseeker to receive an ancestral relic and formally pledge their aid to the shen'dorei. For every young Skyborne coming into adulthood, the journey begins in Thendal Village. Guided forward by Ailee Farheart, fledglings make their way just west to the greatfather tree where the village elder awaits. Passing into maturity among the shen'dorei is not merely a social milestone, but a ceremonial commitment to serve their community amid rising local troubles. At the entrance of the greatfather tree, Rorian the Dayseeker presides over the ceremony. He formally bestows an ancestral relic upon the initiate—an heirloom passed through generations of shen'dorei. Borne by many who came before, the relic serves as a lasting token of the winds of home, destined to return to the people only when its bearer's ashes are scattered to the breeze.

quest:92461.text: Harmony in Balance. Harmony in Balance is an early rite of duty given to fledgling adventurers on Zephras Isle by Rorian the Dayseeker. It tasks the player with culling juvenile vuldren in Thendal Grove to preserve the natural equilibrium of the island. Through this mundane necessity, novices learn how sensitive local beasts are to the shifting magical currents around them. Even in an era defined by uncertain futures and mounting peril, daily survival on Zephras Isle requires humble diligence. In Thendal Grove, the local vuldren population has grown at an unsustainable rate, threatening the delicate environmental harmony that sustains the island's wildlife. Rorian the Dayseeker assigns young protectors the sober task of thinning their numbers to avert widespread ecological strain. While culling wild beasts may appear to be ordinary gamekeeping, the vuldren's surge reflects deeper concerns. Though typically docile creatures, the wildlife of Zephras is attuned to the island's atmosphere and reacts sharply when the magic carried on the winds falls out of balance. Correcting imbalances early prevents docile creatures from degenerating into unpredictable and dangerous pests.

quest:92462.text: Infestation Investigation. Infestation Investigation is an early task given to young adventurers stepping out into Thendal Grove on Zephras Isle. Ranger Elatrell Featherlight orders a cull of pesky cirrusflies that have begun swarming the eastern groves. Left unchecked, the fast-breeding insects threaten to destabilize the peaceful grove and endanger local settlements. Thendal Grove has long maintained a delicate balance, but recent reports by local rangers indicate a sudden population surge of pesky cirrusflies on the eastern edge of the woods. While individual cirrusflies are minor pests, their swarms quickly turn aggressive and destructive when numbers balloon. Ranger Elatrell Featherlight wastes no time dispatching capable youth to cull the flying insects before their presence completely overwhelms the grove. Following their initial coming of age, young defenders are thrust directly into the practical upkeep of Zephras Isle. Clearing out pests might seem like menial labor, but keeping the woodlands safe from creeping wildlife outbreaks is vital to safeguarding the settlements nearby. The sheer abundance of entrails and insects clinging to returning hunters proves that the swarm's scale is far worse than initially feared.

quest:92463.text: The Cirrusfly Queen. The Cirrusfly Queen is a hunt targeting the matriarch of the aggressive insect hive dwelling in Thendal Grove on Zephras Isle. Following early reconnaissance of the infestation, Elatrell Featherlight directs recruits into the heart of the grove to eliminate the queen and cull the swarm at its source. Ending her reign provides immediate relief to the local rangers working to keep the wilderness manageable. Initial efforts against the cirrusflies revealed that simply swatting away stray worker drones would never curb the infestation spreading across Thendal Grove. Elatrell Featherlight tasks capable wanderers with penetrating deeper into the southeastern reaches of the grove where the main hive lies. There, the queen directs the colony under the vigilant protection of heavier soldier drones. While common cirrusflies might seem like petty pests from a distance, their larger breeds pose a serious physical danger to anyone passing beneath the boughs of Zephras. By hunting down the matriarch and withstanding her guards, novices prove their martial mettle, earning high praise and a nod of respect from Featherlight's ranger cadre.

quest:92464.text: Elemental Unrest. Elemental Unrest is an introductory task given by Rorian the Dayseeker on Zephras Isle. Following the departure of the island's sentient elemental benefactors, the lesser wind spirits near the Thendal Standing Stones have grown agitated and unpredictable. You are sent into Thendal Grove to find Rorian's apprentice, Yala Windwatcher, and discover what is unsettling the local breeze. For generations, the people of Zephras lived alongside powerful, sentient wind spirits who guided and protected them. With those elemental benefactors gone, the island has drifted into persistent imbalance. The air is no longer tended by benevolent minds, leaving only simple sprites that reflect the volatile emotions and forces lingering across the landscape. Northeast of Rorian's post, near the ancient Thendal Standing Stones, the air has grown sharply hostile. Because these lesser manifestations lack true self-awareness, their turbulence is not born of malice, but of reaction. Rorian sent his apprentice, Yala Windwatcher, to monitor their erratic behavior from the edge of the grove and deduce what unseen tension is disturbing them.

quest:92465.text: Agitators. Agitators is an early task on Zephras Isle issued by Yala Windwatcher. The aggressive Al'Aketh cult has pushed into Thendal Grove, agitating the peaceful native wind sprites into hostile elementals. Adventurers are sent to disperse the roiling winds and clear out the cultist converts threatening the area. Thendal Grove has fallen under the shadow of the Al'Aketh cult. Known for their unsettling designs on Zephras Isle, the cultists have encroached on the grove and actively riled the delicate wind spirits dwelling there. Once peaceful sprites have turned violent, forming volatile roiling winds that threaten anyone passing through the region. Yala Windwatcher tasks passing champions with subduing both the enraged elementals and the Al'Aketh converts fomenting the unrest. While putting down the wind creatures restores a fragile calm to the grove, dealing with the cultists is a somber duty: Yala laments the shedding of shen'dorei blood among their own people, yet recognizes that the cult leaves little choice.

quest:92469.text: Return to Rorian. Return to Rorian is a mission carrying urgent reports from the field back to Thendal Grove on Zephras Isle. After aiding Yala Windwatcher against encroaching forces, an adventurer is dispatched to inform Rorian the Dayseeker that the Al'Aketh cult has actively escalated their presence by disturbing the local wind spirits. Following the disruption dealt to the agitators harassing Zephras Isle, Yala Windwatcher stays behind to mop up remaining hostiles while tasking you with an essential duty: delivering intelligence. Thendal Grove needs to know that the mysterious Al'Aketh are no longer operating purely in the shadows.

quest:92470.text: Foul Matriarch. Foul Matriarch is a trial of survival assigned by Aetheen of the Gales to budding initiates in Thendal Village. The task demands delving into the southern caves to cull the scavenging ursera and slay their vicious den mother, Urs'anah. Completing the hunt proves that an adventurer possesses the resolve required to face greater perils across Zephras Isle. Aetheen of the Gales maintains a watchful eye on newcomers finding their footing around Thendal Village. Once an initiate demonstrates early competence, Aetheen issues a dangerous rite of passage: a direct assault against the predatory wildlife threatening the perimeter. Rather than simply fighting on the open paths, the initiate is sent directly into the dark caves to the south to thin the local ursera packs and confront their broodmother. The local rangers have long noted the ferocity of the ursera, but none poses a greater threat to the haven than Urs'anah, their formidable matriarch. Sheltered deep within Thendal Cave, she directs her scavengers and aggressively defends her lair. Bringing back her severed head serves as definitive proof that an adventurer is capable of handling ferocious beasts and is ready to push beyond the borders of the starting grove.

quest:92471.text: Aetheen of the Gales. This quest marks a rite of passage for young adventurers on Zephras Isle, directing them to report to one of the island's leading authorities. After completing early trials under Rorian the Dayseeker, promising youths are sent into Thendal Grove to meet Aetheen of the Gales, an elder who reads the winds and evaluates the next generation. The early tasks set before novitiates on Zephras Isle are not merely mundane chores; they serve as informal tests to evaluate whether rising youths possess the grit and spirit needed to defend their homeland. Recognizing that island life faces growing trials, mentors such as Rorian the Dayseeker keep a watchful eye on candidates who prove capable of handling greater responsibility. Deep within Thendal Grove sits Aetheen of the Gales, a respected member of the Council of Elders governing Zephras Isle. Aetheen spends her time reading the currents of the air and assessing young shen'dorei as they come of age. Stepping before her signifies that an initiate has outgrown minor perimeter duties and is ready to tackle direct threats facing the community.

quest:92472.text: The Next Step. Following the resolution of the immediate beast threats near Thendal Village, Elder Aetheen of the Gales directs travelers southward toward Shen'dar Village. The journey marks a shift from clearing wild fauna to confronting the organized zealotry of the Al'Aketh Cult, who revere the Windlord Al'Akir. After proving capable against the local predators and the matriarchs plaguing the northern wilderness of Zephras Isle, adventurers are called to broader duties. Elder Aetheen of the Gales recognizes that simple pest control is secondary to the true peril taking root across the island. To protect the isle's inhabitants, capable defenders must be dispatched to support the outlying settlements. The primary danger facing southern Zephras is the Al'Aketh Cult. Described as ruthless zealots, the cultists dedicate themselves to Al'Akir the Windlord, ruler of the elemental realm of Skywall. Their growing power poses an immediate menace to Shen'dar Village. In response, Aetheen sends travelers southward down the road, past lurking ambushers in the highlands, to reinforce Constable Aonda's local guard.

quest:92473.text: Aggressive Encroachment. Aggressive Encroachment is a task issued by Valreaa Valewind to protect the local settlement from desperate wildlife. Ursera from a nearby den have grown increasingly bold, wandering into the village and threatening its inhabitants. The ursera population nesting southwest of the village has become an urgent safety hazard. Recently, a hungry adolescent beast strayed right up to the base of the village's central elder tree, nearly mauling a young child playing nearby. The settlement's rangers were forced to cut the creature down before tragedy struck. Recognizing that hunger and starvation are driving these predators to attack civilized grounds, the rangers have ordered a cull of the scrawniest ursera in Thendal Grove. By eliminating the desperate and malnourished beasts prowling outside the dens, the Rangers of the Grove hope to halt further encroachment until they can uncover what is disturbing the local wildlife.

quest:92474.text: Falling With Style. "Falling With Style" is an introductory rite of passage for young Skyborne in Thendal Village. Offered atop the local watchtower by the mischievous Myriaal Mistwake, it challenges novices to test their innate slow-fall ability by leaping from the platform toward Rorian the Dayseeker below. Perched high above Thendal Village on Zephras Isle, Myriaal Mistwake invites young Skyborne to test their heritage through a game of daring. Rather than treating their innate magical gifts as sacred relics kept under strict restraint, Myriaal encourages newcomers to leap into the open air from the watchtower ledge. The purpose is practical as well as playful: mastering the instinctive art of walking upon air before life beyond the grove demands it in perilous situations. The exercise serves as a vivid demonstration of two contrasting Skyborne attitudes. While Myriaal delights in sudden descents and startles onlookers for amusement, Rorian the Dayseeker embodies traditional caution. When novices glide down to land squarely before him, Rorian admonishes the reckless display, warning that thoughtlessly exhausting one's magical gifts can leave a traveler helpless when danger strikes. Even so, he concedes that controlled practice within the safety of the village has its place.

quest:92481.text: A Student of the Arcane. A Student of the Arcane is an introductory trial and summons for novice spellcasters on Zephras Isle. Initiated by Rorian the Dayseeker after newcomers prove their basic mettle, it directs budding mages to review a Glowing Recall Crystal and report to the local mentor, Dorii Brightwhisper. After helping manage the troublesome vuldren lurking near Thendal Grove, fledgling mages are entrusted with a curious artifact: a Glowing Recall Crystal. Left behind by Dorii Brightwhisper, the island's resident arcane instructor, the crystal serves as a magically recorded missive designed to test an initiate's aptitude and welcome them into deeper mystical study. According to Dorii Brightwhisper, mastery of the arcane has slowly dwindled among their people during their long millennia spent secluded high in the clouds. Dorii views each new practitioner not merely as a student, but as an essential pioneer meant to recover lost knowledge and restore their people's once-mighty magical heritage.

quest:92482.text: The Way of the Hunter. The Way of the Hunter is an introductory training quest for fledgling hunters in Thendal Grove on Zephras Isle. After proving their mettle against the local vuldren threat, young trackers are directed by Rorian the Dayseeker to present themselves to Tai'ree Farsight to begin their formal tutelage. Upon returning from thinning the disruptive vuldren prowling the outskirts of Thendal Grove, young hunters find that their practical skills have caught local attention. Rorian the Dayseeker passes along a scribbled summons from Tai'ree Farsight, the grove's resident hunter trainer. For novice rangers setting out into the wider wilds of Zephras Isle, this marked the shift from simple island defense to true martial and survival instruction. Found near the center of the village, Tai'ree Farsight welcomes promising pupils with stern realism. Emphasizing that thriving in untamed nature demands sharp senses and lightning reflexes, she offers guidance born of her own long years of experience. Her mentorship marks the foundational steps for any island tracker looking to hone their marksmanship and survival skills.

quest:92483.text: At Home in the Shadows. "At Home in the Shadows" is an introductory rogue quest on Zephras Isle. After aiding Rorian the Dayseeker in Thendal Grove, budding rogues are directed to read a summons and meet their local class mentor, Akeri Duskblade. The quest marks the moment young rogues transition from general village chores to serious stealth and combat training. While handling basic threats around Thendal Grove, young rogues draw the attention of Akeri Duskblade, the grove's resident rogue trainer. Rather than mingling openly in the settlement, Akeri passes a simple note through Rorian the Dayseeker. Rorian recognizes that despite Akeri's suspicious demeanor, the mentor understands the practical skills needed to survive outside the grove's sheltered boundaries. Tucked away inside the village watchtower, Akeri Duskblade wastes no time mincing words. He evaluates every newcomer's footing and awareness immediately upon their arrival, warning that sloppy footwork outside Thendal Grove leads straight to an early grave. By surviving Akeri's scrutiny, a rogue takes their first formal step into mastering stealth, precision, and survival on Zephras Isle.

quest:92484.text: Embracing the Elements. Embracing the Elements is an introductory shaman quest in Thendal Grove on Zephras Isle. Initiated by Rorian the Dayseeker, the task directs young practitioners to Windshaper Boro, the local shaman trainer. It introduces the silent rift between the local people and the elemental spirits of the winds. After helping manage the vuldren pest problem around the village, aspiring shamans are approached by Rorian the Dayseeker. During their time afield, Windshaper Boro left behind a humming recall crystal, signaling that it is time for formal elemental instruction to begin in the center of the grove. Upon meeting Windshaper Boro, he explains the difficult state of local shamanism. The spirits of the four winds abruptly severed communication years ago, abandoning their former communion. Zephras shamans now dedicate themselves to deep study of the natural world, striving through rigorous training to bridge the silence and coax the spirits into dialogue once more.

quest:92485.text: A Student of Nature. A Student of Nature marks a fledgling druid's introduction to formal training on Zephras Isle. After helping restore local harmony, novice druids are summoned by Xyton Silverwind beneath the boughs of Thendal Grove. It serves as the opening gateway into understanding the deeper balance between flora and fauna on the isle. Following the resolution of local disturbances caused by overzealous wildlife, Rorian the Dayseeker delivers a personal summons to young initiates. Left behind by the local mentor Xyton Silverwind, the folded parchment invites aspiring druids to step forward and dedicate themselves to the deeper mysteries of the wild. It signals that an initiate's natural talents have caught the eye of the grove's elders. Meeting Xyton Silverwind on the lower level of the great tree in Thendal Grove anchors a novice to their calling. Silverwind regards the vibrant flora and fauna of Zephras Isle as an intricate living tapestry, one that demands constant preservation and vigilant balance. To walk the path of the fang, claw, feather, and branch requires enduring mentorship, and this meeting marks the true beginning of that lifelong stewardship.

quest:92532.text: The Warrior's Path. The Warrior's Path is an introductory martial quest offered to budding fighters on Zephras Isle. Following instructions delivered through Rorian the Dayseeker, young warriors are directed to Blademaster Ren in the Thendal Village watchtower. Ren stands ready to offer combat instruction and discipline to those prepared to shield their people. Upon returning to Rorian the Dayseeker in Thendal Village after restoring balance nearby, aspiring fighters receive word that the settlement's blademaster has taken notice of them. Rorian delivers a crumpled note penned by Ren herself, asking the novice to seek her out directly. Elevated above the settlement within the village watchtower, Ren keeps an observant eye over both the island's borders and the recruits who may one day defend them. Reaching the watchtower introduces the warrior to Blademaster Ren's philosophy of combat. To Ren, martial mastery is not simply an exercise in brute strength, but a vital duty to lead, endure, and protect in an increasingly uncertain world. She pledges her guidance to the recruit as they hone their skills, offering rigorous training as they grow strong enough to face the greater perils threatening their home.

quest:92544.text: Al'Aketh Thugs. The peaceful roads around Thendal Grove are threatened by a violent band of Al'Aketh cultists occupying the nearby temple ruins. Dispatched from the Shrine of Akir under orders to harass wayfarers and force recruits into their ranks, these zealots pose an immediate danger to local travelers. Hanaa Nightwind tasks adventurers with breaking their hold and slaying their brutish commander. Just southwest of Thendal Grove lie ancient temple ruins that should offer quiet shelter to wanderers. Instead, the grounds have been overtaken by the Al'Aketh, an aggressive cult driven by fanatical ambition. Far from peaceful worshipers, these cultists act as highwaymen and enforcers, preying upon those traveling along the outskirts of the grove. The Rangers stationed nearby suspect these ruffians were sent directly by High Priestess Lorthuna from the Shrine of Akir to bully and coerce the populace into bowing to the cult's influence. Heading the rabble at the temple ruins is Malduko Cloudcrush, a brutal leader who uses violence and fear to keep both his initiates and unsuspecting wayfarers in line. With brutes and newly indoctrinated neophytes answering his commands, Malduko has established an aggressive outpost right on the doorstep of Thendal Grove. By striking down Cloudcrush and scattering his underlings, Hanaa Nightwind hopes to shatter the cult's confidence and send a clear warning that zealotry and coercion will not be tolerated in these lands.

quest:92597.text: Reading the Ley Lines. Reading the Ley Lines is a rite of passage for young Skyborne discovering their Highborne magical heritage. Entrusted by Falorne Fallwind on Zephras Isle, novitiates travel to the standing stones in Thendal Grove to sense and draw upon the raw arcane currents surging through the elemental terrain. Even within the windswept confines of the elemental plane, latent arcane conduits run beneath the earth. While strange elementals and the hostile Al'Aketh drift across Zephras Isle, subterranean ley lines have begun pushing toward the surface.
